We have an abundant supply of birch trees in this nation, and their papery white bark will become our parchment.

The Novgorod First Chronicle details the history of our country, from the days of the legendary Varangian chieftain Rurik up to the present. It is a cultural heirloom that is proudly handed down from one generation to another.

There are over eighty Orthodox churches in Novgorod, and some are the largest landholders in the principality. Their wealth and religious prestige allows the Church to significantly influence the population in many areas, and our citizens are more pious as a result — in a good way.

Novgorod is an important cultural center in Europe. Epic tales are told of our's literate and intellectual population, intricate religious art, and grand architecture, increasing the prestige of our flourishing city and indeed the whole nation.

The Posadnik is the highest administrative position in our towns and cities, and is a more significant role than that of a mayor. As their city grows, so do the responsibilities, influence, and number of Posadniks in the administration.

The Viking-like Ushkuynik pirates were once a useful tool to suppress our competitors. Unfortunately, we were forced to stop using them due to foreign intervention, mainly from Moscow. We should begin funding them again, and send these pirates to plunder farther shores — that will show everyone who the true masters of the North are!
Fur, the silken gold of Russia! While other states gain their wealth from trading in Gold and other rare metals, our source of income comes from the high-quality Fur the motherland provides us with.

Leading troops is the most important duty for the Grand Duke, who is appointed to rule over the Veche Republic. Under such strong and experienced leadership, our armies will become far more deadly in battle.
We shall build a grand shipyard on the eastern coast of the Baltic Sea, and dominate overseas trade!

The Republic of Velikiy Novgorod is the target of many external threats. But be it the western heretics from Scandinavia, the rampaging Germans to our southwest, or even other Russian powers to our south; they all shall all crumble at the feet of our unbreakable fortifications.

Well-trained elite troops, these men have been honed to represent the best our people have to offer. Raised as slaves purchased from foreign masters, they are disciplined and taught our religious and military doctrines as they are expected to form the core of our standing army. Oftentimes, they come equipped with heavy armor and sturdy spears. Their unique helmets and presence in the battlefield is a terrifying sight for our foes.
Formidable traders that primarily deal in spices, these mercantile giants have profited greatly from the flow of exotic goods that trail their origin as far as the shores of India and beyond.

Under Baybars, our barīd reached a sophistication unmatched in the Islamic world: relay stations with fresh mounts at fixed stages, carrier pigeons for the most urgent dispatches, and intelligence agents posted along every route. Word of a frontier raid can reach the capital in a matter of days, and our orders return just as swiftly.
Auxiliary units that often accompanied their Mamlūk counterparts, these light and quick troops will offer great support to their parent forces on the battlefield.

Our Sultanate is enormous, and therefore we must make wise, careful choices about its administration. To employ particularly learned individuals as local governors is a brilliant move, one that should eventually tip the geopolitical scales in our favor.

The spice trade flowing through the Red Sea is a key source of our wealth, and we must seize full control of it. By threatening to burn down any Red Sea ports outside our authority that accept spice traders, we can capture the lion's share of this lucrative commerce. We may not win many friendships with our aggression, but we shall have gold enough to comfort us.
The later Mamlūk troops are categorized by a renewed attention to detail and discipline. A series of military reforms are set in place, to restore the old standards and retrain our standing armies.

The Royal Mamluks are the elite core of the Mamluk army, serving as the Sultan's personal guard. Handpicked and rigorously trained, they are renowned for their loyalty, exceptional combat skills, and unwavering dedication.

The heart-vein of our Sultanate is the river Nile. Traversing our nation, its touch creates our most fertile lands, and its life-bringing waters of the river channel prosperity and ample wealth throughout our domain.

Our merchants deal in goods from the markets of Alexandria, to the shores of Aden, and as far away as India itself. These extensive networks of contacts, business, and capital have positioned us at the forefront of maritime commerce.

The great empires of Europe and the East have made groundbreaking advances in the use of gunpowder and its military applications. To study their ways and make the according improvements to our own armaments would greatly strengthen our own military.

Designating our ports as official merchant zones for incoming cargo is a move that will certainly increase the mercantile significance of our territory, albeit at the expense of our neighbors and foes alike.

Our ports across the Mediterranean Sea are some of the most affluent in the entire region. Merchants from every corner of the known world travel to Alexandria and Cairo to deal in spices, Silk, and precious stones. The creation of a merchant navy to facilitate and protect our maritime avenues would therefore be a wise idea.

ref.d: The Sultanate's rule over the vastness of Egypt depends greatly on maintaining a powerful standing army. Its upper class consists of factions of these powerful slave soldiers, who often ascend to the throne themselves, and can be the deciding factor between a long and short reign.

adv.d: The horses of Genghis Khān trampled and conquered territories stretching from Europe to China. As his heirs and successors, our cavalry will instill fear of the same thing happening into our enemies.
The legacy of Genghis Khān is ours through his son Chagatai. All shall tremble before us as we reclaim his glory!

Surrounded by people that would oppose us, we face a constant struggle to maintain our borders. Our ever-vigilant soldiers have plentiful opportunities to hone their skills in battle, giving birth to a combat-hardened warrior people ready to reclaim the legacy of the Great Khān.
We lie sheltered between Balkhash Lake and the Tiānshān Mountains. It is a harsh and unforgiving land, one which our people know how to use as a weapon against would-be invaders.

The Karluk language of the eastern steppes is far more worthy to carry the thoughts and ideas of our great lineage than Persian or Arabic ever could be. We must promote the use of our ancestral language, and create a new literary tradition.

We can trace our line back to Chagatai Khān, the second son of Genghis Khān, who once ruled these lands and established a powerful Mongolian successor state. Although a long time has passed since then, we can still claim considerable legitimacy by appealing to the legacy of our fierce ancestor.

The constant power struggles between the various princes, nobles, cities, and tribes in the Chagatai Khanate have produced a nation of highly adept schemers. If we can put aside our quarrels and channel this energy towards outsmarting our enemies, it would be a great boon to our people.

Conquering people can be a tricky business; not everyone is ready to accept our enlightened government. Still, we have discovered that there are easier ways to bring people into our empire than building a mountain of skulls — something that our ancestors never learned.

Let it be known that boy cannot be a man unless he has ridden first with our invincible host, that he can take no wife until he has taken another man's wife, that he is not worthy of a hut until he has burnt down someone else's. Let service in our armies be the only route to manhood.
Our armies shall march like the great hordes of Genghis Khān. Our troops shall trample our enemies under our hooves like blades of grass of our native steppes. All shall fear the power of our armies!

Korea was home to many kingdoms in the past. However, the influence of one kingdom in particular is still felt today: Goguryeo, the precursor to Goryeo. Goguryeo has left us many legacies, including its stone fortifications and castle-building techniques, which are still in use to this day.

Korea has always had artistic traditions, but art has truly blossomed since our national unification, thrusting us into a golden era of cultural achievement. Among our many accomplishments, the artisanry of our people shines as a beacon of skill and refinement.
Our armies need a steady supply of troops to keep them in prime condition. Having local centers of recruitment and training will allow us to have easily available reserves.

Our aristocracy puts great emphasis on the cultural development of their spirit and mind. Literature, such as poetry in Classical Chinese, is seen as greatly valuable by the court. The nobility and ruling class alike are enthusiastic about the cultural impact of the written word.

Our forces have been aware of gunpowder's tactical value for centuries. Through reverse-engineering Chinese designs and the innovations of Choe Museon, we have mastered both gunpowder production and the construction of machines that employ it for military use.
The Gwiseon Turtle Ship is a Korean warship which utilizes oars and sails to outmaneuver other types of galleys, while also being equipped with light Chongtong - Korean firearms.
The Hwacha deliver devastating firepower through their barrages of rocket-powered arrows or iron-headed bolts. Their maneuverability forces them to take a more defensive role in battles.

As gunpowder technology advances, so does our ingenuity, and as a result we have devised a new defensive system. Although simple in concept and execution, installing cannons in our fortifications will increase their defensive capabilities tremendously.

Movable type is an ancient printing technology first used by the Chinese people many centuries ago. But it is the Goryeo dynasty who developed the metal form of movable type, streamlining the printing process. We can now print books with unparalleled efficiency.

Our borders are constantly threatened, both by barbarians from the north and pirates from beyond the seas. To ensure our armies are always ready to meet every threat with swiftness, we will establish a council of officers dedicated to controlling and securing our borders.
To ensure proper, stable governance, we must first codify exactly how the government will work. This will be the basis for our nation's first written constitution.

Agriculture is the bedrock of our economy, and therefore efficient village management is paramount. To this end, we will implement the hyangyak system, which establishes self-governance for villages. These agreements establish behavioral standards, dispute resolution regulations, and other civil procedures aimed at creating stable, self-reliant communities.

The Korean language is so fundamentally different from any form of Chinese that the use of Chinese characters renders all except the most highly educated people illiterate. Our new alphabet is more scientific, and will allow all our people to be able to read and write in their own language.

Defending our coastlines is vital to our survival, and as a result of this vigilance, we have developed the ingenious 'turtle ship'. These heavily armored behemoths will ensure that no enemy ship penetrates our coastal holdings.

The Panokseon is a multi-deck warship with greater size and firepower than the usual Geobukseon Turtle Ship. While still relying on oars, the sails of the Panokseon allow it to reach a greater speed comparable to galleys for its size.

The hopae is an identity tag system requiring all Korean people to carry proof of their name, birthplace, status, and residence. This allows authorities to quickly verify identities, and to track a person's movement, if needed.

Although we are already quite experienced at using gunpowder and cannon, we should not stop making technological advancements. By developing smaller, but more durable cannons, as well as inventing more efficient methods of reloading, we will revolutionize our artillery and greatly benefit both our army and our navy.

A new set of reforms that will gradually introduce previously ignored improvements into the tax system. The tribute tax levied against households will be replaced with a unified tax on arable land, and the tax on goods will be limited to a quota which lets enterprising peasants and wholesalers make and sell surplus goods. This will result in lower taxes for the peasantry, increased revenues for the state, and an overall rise in commerce.

The Norwegian land cannot provide our people with enough food to sustain themselves. We will look to the sea to feed our people instead. Fortunately, the waters of the North Sea provide us with plenty of fishing grounds.
The Norwegian people have always chosen to traverse the country by boat, whenever it is convenient. This makes our people adept sailors, ready to man our navy whenever necessary.

With the growth of our fishing industry, we have also seen a corresponding expansion in the number of sailors in our realm. We should take advantage of this and recruit some of them to our navy, as seamanship is just as important as the ship itself.

Long ago, our illustrious forefathers sailed forth and established colonies in the North. Our sagas even tell us that they reached a new world and established Vinland. We must follow in their footsteps.
The expansion of our fishing industry has also led to an expansion in shipbuilding. We have a ready pool of trained shipwrights at hand to expand our own production process.
In days gone by, our people would brave the high seas to establish colonies on distant shores. Let us rekindle this adventurous spirit in our people so that they sail forth again!
Keen minds preserve knowledge Known from ages past Sung in the sundown Sagas are our inheritance Encouraged by the establishment Each country will have its own

The ports of Norway have long been a desirable destination for merchants from all around Europe. It is time that we not only host foreign merchants in our ports, but benefit from the trades of northern Europe ourselves.
Our people coexist with fellow men and women of many faiths. This diverse social composition is embedded in our legal frameworks and beliefs. Together, we are stronger!

Mercantile opportunities and the promise of a better life are some of the reasons as to why our towns and settlements tend to receive constant waves of immigration. Many men and women relocate to our lands seeking their fortune, and their presence and contributions increase our fortune in turn.

To help connect our people across our vast realm, we need a unified language, and require many literate members of the clergy to spread it. The development of such a language to record our history and maintain our administrative apparatus is not only a sign of national pride and prestige, but also a means of creating a distinct government, separating us linguistically and culturally from our neighbors to the east.

Due to the size of our realm, our jurisdiction falls under two distinct frameworks: To the north lies the core of our territories, proudly embracing our cultural traditions and social mores. However, our southern and eastern regions often diverge to a certain degree from our central norms. To respect such diversity will strengthen our nation as well as our position on the geopolitical stage.

Over two remarkable centuries of warfare, Lithuanian warlord dukes transformed a loose federation of tribes into a unified warrior state. They mounted fierce resistance against the aggression of Catholic holy orders, while simultaneously conquering vast territories in the East. These legendary achievements continue to inspire our military leaders today.

If we are to defend ourselves against our aggressive Polish and East Slavic foes, we must project strength! Establishing the title of Supreme Duke of Lithuania will decisively assert our authority, especially against the growing power of our nobility and others who seek to violate our sovereignty.

Years of negotiations with the Holy Father have resulted in our embracing Catholicism, with the blessing of our Polish neighbors and the Pope himself, during a turbulent and unique Christianization process. After our struggle to seek our spiritual identity subsided, it is clear that we have become a beacon of Catholicism, a shield against the heathens and heretics that threaten our society.

The abolition of Romuva, a faith embraced by our ancestors, has shaken the very foundations of Lithuanian society. Yet, in order to secure a brighter future, we have chosen the path of Orthodoxy and fully celebrate our new identity. But if we are to be successful in that, the religious authorities of our newfound Orthodox faith must maintain autonomy from foreign patriarchates in order to avoid external interference.

Statutes of Lithuania are a set of three different legal reforms which aggregate, unify, and update the laws of the realm. Known for harsh punishments and the introduction of the death penalty, these statutes are in line with many contemporary Western penal codes. Each crime is supposed to be punished the same regardless of the class of the person committing it, but in practice, the peasants were often at a disadvantage compared to how members of other estates were treated.

The coat of arms that hangs on our banners originates from one of our most celebrated dynasties, the Gediminid family. Many of their brightest have led our nation through turbulent times into ample prosperity with careful statesmanship and capable guidance. The columns of such great leaders symbolize the strong foundation and tenacity of our country and our fellow men and women.

Lithuania experienced a Renaissance in the late 15th and early 16th centuries. Inspired by the ideas of the Reformation and influenced by the Italian Renaissance, there was a prolific flourishing of education, arts, architecture, and literature during this era. This period will also see the creation of a written form of Lithuanian and, subsequently, the first works of Lithuanian literature.

ref.d: With the Valakų Reform, our Nobility are more regulated in their behavior towards our subjects. This supports the Commoners within our realm, while also solidifying their status as an independent estate.

adv.d: Elephants are impressive creatures and tower over any other animal we have seen. It is time to utilize these qualities to strike fear into our enemies by using these majestic animals in warfare. Elephants are also able to carry great weight, allowing us to mount war machines on them. Constructing double-stringed crossbows and equipping our elephants with them will create a tool that will allow us to dominate the battlefields better than ever before.

Our rulers excel at creating dazzling processions, events of glorious splendor that very few others can rival. These extravagant demonstrations of our national wealth confirm the power and brilliance of the ruler and the astonishing riches of our nation. The glittering procession of elephants, treasure, and the royal guard will strike awe and respect in the hearts of our people, winning their unbroken loyalty and admiration.

Our country has lived through tumultuous times as royal patronage shifted between both Hinduism and various branches of Buddhism. We must promote the chosen faith throughout our country to breed stability, and trust that our ruler has chosen the true path for our people.

Our great cities are home to many barays and canals, primed to store and disperse water throughout the area. Constructing and maintaining this network of waterways with skill will ensure our population will thrive even during the unstable monsoon seasons.

We will need to reinforce our army with new recruits, which are easily found among the peasant class. With some training, we will be able to ensure the ranks can be refilled at any time by capable soldiers.

While our own people are not familiar with silk-weaving and prefer other fabrics, we are lucky that foreign artisans have settled in our cities and established their own weaving workshops. We should adopt this approach for other industries by directly inviting foreign artisans to bring their skills here, and thereby universally expand our production.

Our rivers provide an excellent way to transport goods harvested and produced in our inland territories to our harbors, which are connected to foreign trade routes. Utilizing this transport network will also connect our cities and make communication between them faster.

In the past, we both fought with and alongside the fierce warriors of Champa. If we can secure the service of their most capable leaders in times of conflict, we can ensure our own forces are trained and well-rested, ready to leap into battle as fresh reinforcements.

The great city of Angkor was once a brilliant example of our architectural genius. Due to external pressures, we had to abandon our construction efforts, but we should connect to the roots of our society and start constructing new monuments to our splendor again.
We cannot allow others to dominate the seas and control the trade our state depends on. Let us create a new, modern naval force capable of taking on any pirate or rival navy in South East Asia.

While our existing water reservoirs meet our current agricultural demands, we could easily support more people if we were to dig new barays in other parts of our country, creating the foundations for new urban hubs.

Our people were humiliated in the past by being forced to bow to foreign invaders. While not every defeat can be avoided, we use these old rivalries to spur our people to fight harder and longer on the battlefield, burning to erase the shame of these ancient humiliations.

Our lands are frequently threatened by invasion, and our precious Angkor lies especially vulnerable to siege. We must invest into a comprehensive system of fortifications, with sufficient garrisons to withstand any invading force, so that we can protect our people and national treasures from foreign conquest.

Ever since antiquity, Yemen has been known as 'Arabia Felix', the Fortunate Arabia. Blessed with a temperate highland climate and fertile soil in a sea of desert, it remains one of the most naturally prosperous regions of the peninsula. Let us nurture that prosperity and use it as the foundation of a thriving realm.

Though others have attempted to transplant our beloved bean, the Coffee of Arabia remains unmatched in flavor and fame. From the bustling port of Mocha to the courts of faraway rulers, the world's desire for our drink is insatiable.

The Rasulid dynasty brought unprecedented administrative order to our lands. With census records, tax systems, and a robust cabinet structure, they transformed Yemen into one of the most efficiently governed realms in the region.

The highlands of Yemen have long been home to the Zaydī imamate, a center of learning and piety. Rooted in Islamic jurisprudence, theology, and rationalism, our scholars have ensured the rule of law and the moral integrity of our governance for centuries.

The port of Aden has been a nexus of trade for millennia — its natural harbor welcoming ships from India, Egypt, and East Africa. If properly supported, it can once again become the cornerstone of our maritime economy and the pride of the Red Sea.
Any and all trade from India and Africa must pass through the strait called Gate of Grief. Let us enforce our dominion over this maritime chokepoint and turn every passing ship into an opportunity.

From the Tihāmah coast to the Ḥarāz mountains, our realm is home to countless fiercely independent tribes. While they have long resisted centralized authority, they are also our strength. By uniting them under a single cause, we can better utilize them as a workforce.

Founded in 1224 by Emperor Frederick II, the University of Naples is one of Italy's oldest public institutions. Embracing a secular ethos, it has provided generations of students with a comprehensive education and contributed to intellectual advancements across various fields.

For a long time, Naples has striven to be a center of modern learning, attracting the great minds of the age and spreading the light of the Renaissance. Under the leadership of Giovanni Pontano, these discussion circles have been given structure and organization. It is only fitting that we name the academy after its industrious leader.

b: Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities: +0.5
adv.d: We have inherited an exquisite city from our predecessors. We must continue to beautify and improve this metropolis of the Mediterranean so that it can continue to grow and prosper. No longer can we content ourselves with merely repairing and maintaining the port and buildings; we shall make holistic improvements that better sustain our people by also building aqueducts, draining wetlands, and paving more roads.

For centuries, the Arsenale of Naples has been the center of our ship production and our main naval installation. However, it needs to be expanded and modernized to remain effective against hostile Mediterranean fleets. Let us expand both the commercial and military capabilities of our port, building a more efficient Arsenale to maintain a larger, more powerful fleet.

By abolishing the Collateral Council and establishing the Real Camera di Santa Chiara, we will implement important legal reforms in Naples. Ongoing projects will aim to reorganize the legislative complex, consolidate laws into the Codice Carolino, and implement the Onciario Cadastre for tax reform.

Naples has witnessed a gradual industrialization process over the past decades. Key sectors such as textiles, shipbuilding, and ironworks have experienced significant growth, fueled by investments and technological advancements. This shift towards industrialization will play a significant role in transforming Naples into a major economic center.

The Vietnamese countryside is built upon the enduring strength of the làng, autonomous villages that embody the principle: 'customs of the village outweigh the laws of the king.' In a land of rugged mountains and winding rivers, these communities govern themselves, raise local militias, collect taxes efficiently, and uphold royal authority at the grassroots.

Throughout our history, the Nghĩa Quân — 'righteous militias' — have risen in defense of our land during times of great peril. Composed of farmers, scholars, and local patriots, they stood against foreign invaders and internal tyranny alike. Though irregular in nature, their valor and devotion to the country have made them a formidable force when mobilized.

The Qal'at al-Mashwar at the heart of Tlemcen rises as both fortified royal residence and the seat of Zayyanid court ceremony, housing the dīwān that taxes the Saharan caravans from Sijilmasa and Ouargla, the Mediterranean shipping from Oran, and the overland passage between Fez and Tunis. Its triple-walled enclosure concentrates the apparatus of state, including administrative chambers, the mint, the markets of the Mechouar quarter, and the sultan's personal guard, within a single defensible compound. This dual-purpose stronghold gives the Zayyanid capital both a fiscal weight that no purely territorial Maghrebi state can match and the political resilience that comes from holding every organ of state under the same set of walls.

The Zayyanid Ghulām are the mamlūk-style slave retainers of the Zayyanid emirs of Tlemcen, bought from the Saharan caravan trade and Genoese factors at Oran, trained from boyhood, and sworn to the emir alone. They garrison the Mechouar fortress and form the emir's strike force when the tribes threaten the throne.

b: Nobility Allowed to Build Roads: yes
adv.d: Our roads link Tlemcen to its outport of Honein on the Mediterranean, to the Saharan staging-post of Sijilmasa, and to the great Maghrebi trunk routes that cross our territory under royal escort. We charter our noble houses to maintain the carriage-tracks and the funduq stations along these arteries in exchange for tax exemptions and grants of land along the route. This infrastructure of merchant convoys keeps the central-Maghrebi trade flowing reliably even when factional warfare disrupts Fez or Tunis.

Our urban looms, concentrated in the Bāb al-'Aqaba and Bāb Sīdī Bū Madyan quarters, weave the celebrated sajjādat Tilimsān, the dense-knotted pile carpets whose geometric medallions distinguish them from every other Maghrebi rug tradition. Andalusi master-weavers who settled in our city add new vegetal patterns and indigo-vermilion palettes that command premium prices from Genoese, Marseillais, and Venetian merchants at the Oran fairs. This regulated carpet industry gives our crown a luxury-cloth output and an urban artisan class that the wool-and-tent producers of the inland tribes cannot match.

Our city's Mālikī jurists, the heirs of the great Tlemceni qādīs Ibn Marzūq and the long line of teachers at the Ya'qūbiyya madrasa, convene as the recognized synod of orthodox jurisprudence for the entire western Maghreb. Rulings of the Majlis Mālikī Tilimsān circulate through the Qādirī and Shādhilī Sufi networks, are cited at the courts of Fez, Marrakesh, and the trans-Saharan emirates, and bind even sultans who would prefer juridical authority of their own. This concentrated legal-scholarly authority extends our cultural influence well beyond our political frontiers and binds the western-Maghrebi clergy to our court.

The Mālikī faqīh Aḥmad at-Tijānī founds his namesake Ṭarīqa Tijāniyya at the oasis of 'Ayn Māḍī at the southern edge of our territory, claiming an exclusive spiritual pact with the Prophet and a chain of authority bypassing all earlier Sufi orders. Tijānī missionaries fan out from our state across the western and southern Sahara, into Fez, the Senegalese marches, and as far as the Sudanic emirates, propagating both the order and the diplomatic prestige of its Tlemceni hearth. This new Sufi network extends our religious soft power across every Muslim court of the Atlantic basin and the trans-Saharan world.

Our cultural revival, the Tlemceni Nahḍa, centers around the scholars Muḥammad as-Sa'īdī, Ibn Khūja, and the salons of the Old Mechouar, reclaiming the Zayyanid–Andalusi heritage that earlier interventions had let lapse. We restore the great madrasas, reprint the medieval Tlemceni manuscripts from the libraries of Fez and the Escorial, and publish bilingual periodicals that introduce European thought into the western-Maghrebi conversation. This linguistic and intellectual renewal binds the scattered Zayyanid heritage into a shared modern Tlemceni identity that no foreign administration can easily fragment.

ref.d: The ability to rule this state is largely dependent on the support of the Zenati Bānu 'Abd āl-Wād in the environs of Oran. Should our backing amongst those Tribes falter, so will our legitimacy and ability to govern effectively.

adv.d: In 1330, Basarab I defeated the Hungarian King Charles Robert, securing Wallachian independence through superior mountain tactics. This victory proved that a smaller, localized force could utilize the treacherous Carpathian passes to dismantle imperial armies, setting a military precedent for the next five centuries. Our troops are now experts in hit-and-run warfare and utilize the terrain to bleed invaders long before they reach the Danubian plains.

The formalization of the Princely Chancellery allows for the systematic recording of land grants and diplomatic treaties in Church Slavonic and, eventually, Romanian. This bureaucratic evolution will enable the Voivodes to more efficiently tax the rural peasantry and maintain a permanent corps of diplomatic envoys at the courts of Europe. It will mark the transition from a tribal military society to a sophisticated medieval state.

adv.n: The Order of the Dragon Influence
adv.d: We will introduce a culture of brutal psychological warfare and absolute law and order in Wallachia. By purging the corrupt boyars and imposing strict legal codes, we will consolidate princely power and transform the military into a centralized force loyal only to the Voivode. This ruthless reputation will serve as a primary deterrent for the forces of our enemies.

Under the visionary leadership of our rulers, we will achieve the geopolitical impossible: the unification of all Romanian lands under a single banner. This 'Great Idea' will ignite a latent national consciousness that will transcend ancient feudal borders, proving to the world that a unified Dacia can stand as a European Great Power in its own right. This vision will set the legal, military, and symbolic precedents that will provide us with a permanent, historical claim to regional hegemony and the eventual gathering of all Romanians.

Under the patronage of high officials, we have established the Princely Academy of Saint Sabbas, bringing Italian and Greek professors to our capital. This investment in high education has created a generation of 'Philosopher-Diplomats' who are as comfortable discussing Latin rhetoric as they are negotiating secret treaties with our neighbors. By turning our capital into an intellectual beacon, we have ensured that our administrative elite remains the most sophisticated in the Balkans, capable of outmaneuvering anyone at every turn.

Under the reformists in our nation, we have taken the radical step of legally abolishing serfdom, before many of our neighbors. By transforming the peasantry from 'chattel' into 'taxable subjects', we have centralized the state's fiscal power and broken the absolute control of the rural boyars. This social revolution provides the Voivode with a more direct relationship with the people, creating a more mobile and economically active population capable of supporting a modernizing central administration.

Our grand order was forged in the flames and blood of the Third Crusade during the siege of Acre in 1191. While we originally nursed the sick and feeble, the order has transformed into a militarized group of knights of unbreakable devotion and discipline.

There is no greater symbol of power and military prowess than the heavy cavalry. While for many states the cavalry is made of nobles, every Teutonic Knight is also a member of our heavy cavalry, and undergoes the strict training of a crusader.

It has become clear to us that we can no longer rely on foreign volunteers to fill up our army ranks, no matter how experienced and valuable they might be. Instead, we will develop a system that would allow us to levy our subjects, both German and non-German folk alike.

The German knights, and veterans of the Crusades and other wars are simply not numerous enough to remain the base of our armies. We must reorganize the army to incorporate domestic levies, regiments capable of replacing the knights on the battlefield.

Contemporary battles in Europe have proven that the age of infantry is about to begin. It is now time to develop new tactics, adopt use of the pike, and reform our medieval concept of auxiliary infantry into the main fighting force of our future armies.
We will put an end to the loose religious autonomy local bishops hold within our realm. All religious matters, from taxation to converting the populace, will be state matters from now on.

Grant autonomy to the local governors of our border regions, and reform their holdings into marches. These special zones will pay fewer taxes to the state in return for an obligation to maintain the highest combat readiness during times of war as well as peace. This should provide us with substantial military flexibility at little cost.
We shall grant further rights and privileges to our Prussian bishops, ensuring their loyalty in all matters.
Reserve all state offices only for those who follow our religion. Heretics and heathens are no longer welcome in our realm.

All powers of the state are consolidated in our order. Every action taken and every decision made goes through the hierarchy of the Teutonic Order first before it gets executed. Of course, this bureaucracy is not in everyone's favor, but it ensures the absolute power of the Hochmeister.

It has been said that Ormus is 'a vast emporium where there were peoples and goods of every description from all parts of the world' or that 'If all the world were a golden ring, Ormus would be the jewel in it'. Our realm's identity is inseparable from commerce. Indeed, ships from Gujarat, Arabia, and even China anchor in our ports, exchanging spices, Gems, Silk, and stories.

Ormus controls the strait that links the Indian Ocean to the interior of Asia. Whoever holds this vital passage dictates the rhythm of maritime traffic. Our command of these waters must be absolute, lest our influence be diminished.

At the narrowest point of the Persian Gulf stands Ormus, the gatekeeper of east-west maritime trade. No vessel passes without our knowledge — or without paying our fee. For centuries, this toll has not just made us richer, but shaped our diplomacy and how we project power across the vast seas.

For generations, our realm maintained peace with the mainland through the ancient tribute system known as Moqarrariya. Rather than depending on custom and negotiation, let us codify these tributes into formal pacts — securing fresh water, overland safety, and long-term stability through reliable diplomacy.

Though dry and rocky, the islands of Qeshm and Ormus have sustained urban life thanks to careful provisioning and rich trade. With proper investment, their ports and workshops can flourish further, turning them from logistical hubs into centers of innovation and productivity.

The Persian Gulf is crossed daily by our fleets — be they traders, patrols, or armed escorts. But to match the ambitions of those who envy our position, we must expand and modernize. Let Ormus become more than just a trading post: a maritime arsenal.

Ormuzi coinage circulates from Basra al-Hamra to Bengal, trusted for its purity and weight. By institutionalizing our mint and expanding our issuance, we reinforce our financial sovereignty — and claim fiscal supremacy over the Indian Ocean.

adv.n: An Army for the City of Victory
adv.d: For the City of Victory to be worthy of its name, we must have an army that can bring about these namesake triumphs. We will ensure our troops are well-trained and take great pride in their service.

Vijayanagar — the 'City of Victory' — is the heart of our state, and will one day become the heart of the entire Hindu. Let it shine as a beacon of culture and tradition even as it fends off the Muslim invaders!
The numerous invaders of our Hindu people have shown time and time again the same weakness: the tendency to fight amongst themselves. We must be ready at all times to exploit this to our own ends.
Horses from Arabia are far superior to our local breeds. We will use our trade connections to ensure that we have a steady supply for our military.
The military application of gunpowder is not yet widespread, but it has the potential to mold the future of warfare. We must explore the utility and benefits of gunpowder.
Our society is built on agriculture in the rather arid Karnakassala area. The bunds, also called anecut, provide our cities and fields alike with much-needed fresh water.

We must resist the Muslim invasion on all fronts. The musical traditions of the Northern States are already showing signs of foreign influence. This is blasphemy, because we all know that music is a divine art form that originated with the Devas and Devis themselves. We will show the Hindu people that we are committed to defending this holy art form.

Our territory is situated on one of the key trade routes from East to West. We must ensure that our ports are safe and secure so that visiting captains will land there... giving us the opportunity to tax them.
The cultural diversity of India is one of our defining traits. By allowing our various settlements to rule by their own customs, we will assure their loyalty and integration into our society.
Dharma is a major pillar of our religious and social values. Our state can only be just and virtuous if our rulers themselves embody and live in accord with dharma.

As our state grows, so do our administrative burdens on the government and the risk of revolt. To counteract this, we shall establish a system of decentralized rule, where settlements can manage their own minor issues, only seeking intervention from the central court for severe matters.

Harsh punishments — including being put to death — are how we uphold law and order in this society. By establishing and strictly enforcing a harsh penal code, we ensure criminals fear the consequences of their actions, creating stability through the certainty of punishment.

India has been subject to Muslim threats for far too long. Heathen empires claim their rule from Delhi in the north, yet their beliefs and government are in direct opposition to what our people want. No, a new seat of power must be established — and Vijayanagar shall be the new Throne of India!

Konya, our spiritual center, is home to the followers of Mevlânâ Jalāl ad-Dīn Muḥammad Rūmī. Their sacred practice — the sema — symbolizes the soul's journey toward divine truth. Their presence deepens the mystic traditions of our realm and reinforces our Sufi roots.

Cavalry has always been the cornerstone of Turkmen warfare. Our riders, trained from a young age and mounted on hardy Anatolian horses, uphold the proud traditions of steppe warfare with discipline and striking force.

Meḥmed I issued a decree demanding that only Turkish be spoken in courts, dervish lodges, assemblies, and public squares. This act rejected Persian and Arabic dominance in elite circles and laid the groundwork for a uniquely Turkmen cultural policy.

The Karamanids trace their ancestry to the Salur, one of the major Oghuz tribes. Known for both their leadership and valor, the Salur legacy shapes our state's identity and our claim to represent the Turkmen of Anatolia.

u.t: Government reform: Council of Clan Heads

adv.d: Delegating administrative duties to local clan heads may mean relinquishing some of our central authority, but our advisors insist that we shall reap great benefits in return.
Used throughout the Muslim world, these small fortifications have provided protections to caravans, commercial hubs, and isolated communities alike.
By establishing permanent military camps at strategic locations throughout our domain, we will ensure our army suffers fewer casualties from attrition and can be mobilized quickly when needed.
As warfare tactics advance, so must our strategy. By adapting foreign innovations and techniques like formations, lines of fire, and new gunpowder recipes, we will surely be victorious!
Our armies are experienced with siege machinery, but adopting mobile artillery that can maintain sustained fire would secure our victory whenever we attack an enemy's walls!

ref.d: By seeking advice from the leaders of our most important clans, we can achieve a more stable government, and hopefully bring more prosperity to our society.
This complex system of succession laws and administrative procedures establishes religious obligations and requires demonstrations of piety from the ruling dynasty.

adv.d: Some of the most efficient fishing techniques are employed in local fish traps, known as Bubu. Woven soft wood, such as bamboo, they are tended to by experienced fishermen in strategic locations such as river mouths and employed intricate techniques to maximize their catch.

Used widely across the entirety of the Indonesia, the Kabang is a versatile ship of medium size and often crafted from a single piece of wood. Beyond its role as transport of people and goods, it has come to be synonymous with sea nomads. These folk consist of populations of peasants and fishermen who used the tide and monsoons to migrate from port to port, making a living off the sea.

The Jong has proudly served our people for a long time. Its characteristic number of masts and hull are made of thick wood, making it the perfect vessel for a combination of ferrying goods across long distances, as well as troops.

In our many conquests across Indonesia, we have encountered many new and incredible forms of art, all of which could be adopted and refined by our people to further our legacy. By introducing new techniques and sponsoring artists, our culture will come to exemplify the artistic achievements of our region.

Armed with rudimentary armor and their trademark blade, these warriors rely on mastering speed, ferocity, and fluent movements. They excel on close combat where the karambit's curved blade is extremely efficient at slashing, hooking, and gutting opponents. The adoption and proliferation of new formations and combat maneuvers has turned these warriors into a fabled armed force, feared throughout the archipelago.

The head of our military directly answers to our ruler, and holds enough influence and power to shape the future of our realm. To ensure they understand what an important role they have been given, they are required to swear a special oath, one that underlines our dreams of conquest and bolsters our spirits.

A ceremonious gate of magnificent proportions, the Bajang Ratu follows the architectural design of a candi bentar, or split gateway. Using high quality red brick, the gateway is to be one of the tallest constructs across the Majapahit domain. Its usage is vital, as the structure is used for grand ceremonies of religious and political nature.
Our geographical position, complemented by our growing influence, has led to us presiding over the extensive and profitable trade network that carries Silk and spices from East to West.

One of the most prominent muzzle-loaded cannons of our era is the Cetbang. Armed with a cylindrical short barrel, it delivers a devastating blow with tremendous power. Such is its popularity, that it finds use in many aspects of our conduct of warfare, from protecting our ports to being the main armament of our warships and armies.

The people that populate the Madura Strait have come to serve in our navy. Their naval prowess and great shipbuilding skills have given rise to a new kind of vessel, the Madurese Ghali. A large ship, it is used for offensive and voyager-adjacent tasks, as it will soon comprise the backbone of our fleet.
Scattered throughout Nusantara are a series of temples known as candi. We should restore these temples wherever we find them to renew our people's faith.
Contact with our neighbors in the archipelago has shown us clearly that the raw resources and unclaimed lands are ripe for the taking, promising to become secure and prosperous under our control.
The history of the Javanese people is an integral part of our cultural identity. To protect this identity, we must preserve the traditions upon which we built our great country.

The coiled serpent of the Visconti has become the most recognized symbol of power in Northern Italy, stamped on our coins, our seals, and the gates of every city that answers to us. By making the Biscione the official mark of the ducal state, we tie the region's loyalty to our dynasty rather than to any one noble faction. This visual authority makes it far harder for rivals to question our rule, and our ambassadors find that the serpent on their credentials opens doors that other Italian lords cannot.

The Veneranda Fabbrica del Duomo has maintained a permanent workforce of stonecutters, engineers, and master builders in continuous employ for generations, treating the Cathedral not as a project with an end but as an institution that trains craftsmen and refines technique for as long as the work demands. We have extended its remit and its funding, ensuring that the knowledge it preserves flows outward to every construction site in our territory. This institution turns Milan into a school of practical building, and the craftsmen it trains are sought across the whole of northern Italy.

A breastplate made in our workshops commands a price that craftsmen in Cologne or Toledo cannot match, and our armories supply courts and captains from Portugal to Poland. We formalize the armorers' guilds under ducal oversight, setting standards that protect our reputation and keep the technical knowledge — and the profit — within our walls. This monopoly on premium military equipment brings us steady revenue and keeps our own troops better equipped than any enemy who has to import their plate from elsewhere.

Carlo Borromeo's administration of Milan became the most closely studied model of institutional reform of the age — rigorous reorganization of local hierarchies, standardized training for officials, and regular inspection visits that reached every village in our territory. We adopt his model wholesale, using every institution at our disposal to extend education and discipline throughout our realm. This reform builds a population that is both more literate and more tightly bound to the institutions of the realm, making civic order far easier to maintain.

Our city produced Cesare Beccaria, whose treatise on crimes and punishments has become the most-read legal text in Europe, arguing that laws should deter crime through certainty rather than cruelty. By reforming our criminal code along these lines — replacing torture and arbitrary sentencing with proportional penalties and open courts — we create a legal system that the urban population sees as fair rather than predatory. This makes our cities easier to govern and more appealing to merchants and investors who know their disputes will be resolved by law rather than by bribes.

We have raised a theater on the site of the old church of Santa Maria alla Scala, large enough to seat two thousand and fitted with stage machinery that no other house in Europe can match. The first night drew every ambassador, merchant prince, and noble family who could claim a connection to Milan, and within a season premieres here were being discussed from London to Saint Petersburg. This stage makes our court the cultural arbiter of the continent, and the artists who succeed at La Scala carry our city's name everywhere they travel.

ref.d: Originally an instrument for resolving local disputes between peasants, the Council of Justice has developed into the land's most prominent court, handling cases and operating as a shield for our people.

The Secret Council is a body of nobly-born individuals. Its jurisdiction encompasses our entire domain, and often clashes against the ruler's agenda. The majority of critical decisions made by or on behalf of the ruler frequently fall under the Secret Council's review.

adv.d: Once a spiritual stronghold of Orthodox Christianity and home to one of the oldest bishoprics in the region, the Diocese of Smolensk embodies our people's unshakable faith.

Positioned between forest and steppe, Smolensk has long been a crossroads of war and commerce. By improving overland infrastructure and securing the arteries of caravan travel, we can reforge our role as the vital hinge between northern Rus', the Baltic, and the southern trade routes of the steppes.

For centuries, Smolensk has been a land carved up by outsiders — Lithuanian dukes, Polish kings, and Muscovite princes. To survive, we clung to what united us: our faith and our fortitude. If we are ever to rise again, we must cast off divisions and rally around the sacred idea that, above all, there is only Smolensk.

Long has war defined our fate, but now it shall define our strength. From the ruinous embrace of warfare and siege, Smolensk rises as a center of military production — cannons, firearms, powder and doctrine flow outward from our armories. Let the world see us not as a prize to be taken, but as a hammer to be feared, ready to strike the anvil of foreign conquerors.

After decades of warfare on every border, we learned to fight with weapons of both east and west. Blending Muscovite grit with western precision, our armories now produce elite artillery and tactics unmatched by our rivals. From our forges comes firepower — and from firepower, domination and perseverance.

Brandenburg's infertile, sandy soil has earned it the unflattering nickname 'Sandbox of the Holy Roman Empire.' Such poverty spurred the margraves to aggressively expand, pursuing claims to neighboring territories. These conquests have made our country much more culturally diverse than the rest of the Empire.

In the early days of the Holy Roman Empire, the Brandenburg area was settled and governed by Slavic tribes, until the Emperor created the Northern March to subjugate and fortify the area. Over time, this Northern March evolved into Brandenburg, becoming one of the most important regions in the Holy Roman Empire.
United, the three estates form an effective block against the power of the ruler. To consolidate our control, we must systematically leverage the nobility against the other estates.

Our lands are sparsely populated, for the most part, and surrounded by enemies. The necessity for more robust defenses has prompted us to hire soldiers from foreign lands, who will fight under our banner for a price.

Dividing our lands between heirs has weakened dynasties across the Empire. We will establish a clear rule of succession, the eldest inherits all. Our nobles may grumble, but an undivided Mark is worth their discontent.

In order to regularize control of the Mark of Brandenburg, we will replace local common law with Roman law. We will further regulate justice by moving the Supreme Court from the court of the Elector, who is prone to moving around, to a fixed central location. This will simultaneously improve justice and curb the power of local magnates.

Enhancing our court's control over the Margraviate's lands will earn our ruler the moniker Iron Tooth, as if we bit it like an attack dog. Our rule will leave a mark on our nation, a mark which will instill a sense of pride and loyalty in even the lowliest peasant in Brandenburg.

The authority of the Margrave is greatly threatened by the ever-increasing power of our Estates. The Estates are of great benefit to our nation, but the threat they represent to our base of power necessitates the creation of a new council, one which reduces the very real power that the estates hold over our nation into more of an advisory position for the Margrave. This way, we may continue to enjoy the benefits of our Estates while having fewer concerns about their needs.

Our estates have long held sway over the governance of the Mark. By establishing a council of advisors answerable to the Elector alone, we bring our ablest men to the center of power, and quietly reduce the estates to a consultative role.

Stability in our home regions is the key to our success elsewhere. Expanding outwards while fostering religious tolerance, we not only improve stability at home, but we also make our realm a haven for those fleeing persecution elsewhere.

b: Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities: +0.1
adv.d: Our neighbors drive out their most industrious subjects for the sake of religious conformity. Their loss is our gain. We open our doors to the persecuted and the skilled alike, and our cities grow richer for it.

A great court needs more than soldiers and clerks. By welcoming artists, philosophers, and men of science into our service, we turn the court of Brandenburg into a beacon of culture, and show the world that our ambitions reach beyond the battlefield.

New ideas spread fast in our cities, and the minds of Brandenburg have never been idle. We will cultivate this spirit of inquiry, drawing scholars and thinkers to our court. A nation that thinks clearly governs itself well.

ref.d: We have gone to great lengths to unify our internal legal systems, rooting out abuse and malpractice while creating a professional judiciary.

adv.d: Ever since our ancestors came from Britain, our extensive coastal holdings have been bustling with activity. Our people live by the sea and for the sea, and our ports are always full of trade and fishing boats.

Brittany has never truly been part of France Though we have been ravaged by Franks, Vikings, and the English in the past, we have, thus far, maintained our unique identity as a people. Let all of our neighbors be aware that Brittany shall remain forever free, the last bastion of true Gallic traditions!

First called in the 14th century, the Estates of Brittany allowed free men from all rungs of society, even the Third Estate, to share their grievances and petition the ruler for redress. By calling in the Estates, we can mitigate some of the tension felt throughout our domain.
Our position as the collector of tribute for the Golden Horde has given us many years of experience in gathering tribute... and in retaining some of the profits for ourselves.
The lands of Russia have been ruled by one dynasty since time immemorial. We should utilize our position among our peers and our blood ties to take a leading role.

The Russian people need firm religious guidance. We have historically cooperated well with the Church, and expanding this relationship would benefit us all. If we can move the seat of the Metropolitan Bishop to Moscow, we will be able to strengthen the bonds between our faith and our state.
By redistributing plots of confiscated lands to noble cavalrymen, we can build a new class of soldiers to defend our principality.

The Boyar class is in many ways the foundation of Russia, but just as we need to strengthen the Boyars, we also need to control them. We must protect seats for the Boyars in the Duma, but also to make sure that they are dependent on us to further their influence.

In order to withstand the constant threat of Tatar raids, our ancestors have built a line of tightly positioned and well-defended forts. As our state grows larger, we should keep expanding this 'Abatis Line' to ensure our people are always protected from foreign attacks.

The designs of Feodor Apraksin are robust and resilient, enabling ships to weather most storms that Mother Nature is able to conjure. The innovative construction greatly contributes to any burgeoning maritime ambitions.

The 'Toy Army' is organized into elite companies, forming the Imperial Guard which protects the interests of the monarchy. They are frequently involved in court ceremonies, parades, and other significant events, showcasing their importance beyond their military duties.
Governing the vast expanse of Russia is no easy task. We should establish local recruitment centers to make drafting levies into our armies easier.

ref.d: The Prikazi is an overhaul of the administrative structure used for government bureaucracy. It establishes several bureaus that are responsible for various aspects of governance, such as taxation, justice, military affairs, and trade, which facilitates more rapid implementation of the policies and decisions made by the Tsar.

The Razriadnyi Prikaz introduces a census, which is used to maintain records of the country's population, property, and taxation. It is updated at regular intervals, assesses the military obligations of the estates, and maintains a record of land and property ownership, ensuring that what is due is paid.

The introduction of the Byzantine Court Ceremonies ensures grand ceremonies are carried out in accordance with Byzantine traditions. Meticulous court etiquette is upheld, thereby elevating the prestige and splendor of the ruling elite.

The Chosen Rada creates a powerful council loyal to the ruler, with sweeping authority to suppress the power of the elites. The council's influence extends to matters of governance, policy, and decision-making.

The Collegium is an overhaul of the administrative structure used for government bureaucracy. It establishes several collegiums as government departments, with a systematic separation of responsibilities to avoid possible overlapping of duties. The collegiums are also tasked with case resolutions, with the help of advisory guidelines.

The Nakaz is an overhaul of the legal code concerning equality, justice, and humanitarianism. Heavily influenced by the Enlightenment, it aims to emulate the progressive reforms that are taking place across Europe, whilst simultaneously simplifying the code of law.

adv.d: Emperor Frederick II, the Hohenstaufen King of Sicily, drafted a legal code for Sicily known as the Constitutions of Melfi, or Liber Augustalis. Still in use centuries later, it represents a solid foundation for the governance of our state, regulating public law, judicial procedure, and feudal, private, and penal law.

Founded by King Alfonso V of Aragon, the University of Catania was the oldest in Sicily and one of the few southern institutions granted full Studium Generale status. Unique for its royal charter and blend of scholastic and legal education, it produced jurists, theologians, and scientists who served both Church and Crown in a culturally diverse region.

adv.n: The Court of the Royal Patrimony
adv.d: We will create this specialized court to manage the royal properties and the Secretias (customs offices). By professionalizing the collection of export duties on silk, tuna, and grain, the state will significantly reduce corruption and 'leakage' to local barons. This administrative rigor will turn our lands into the most reliable revenue stream for the Crown, funding our wars across Italy and the Mediterranean.

To maximize agricultural output and tax revenue, the state granted Licenses to Populate to the nobility. This will allow lords to build brand-new towns in the desolate interior of the island, attracting peasants with promises of land and lower taxes. This internal colonization effort will transform the Sicilian landscape, turning wild hinterlands into a patchwork of profitable agricultural communities.

Our island trembles often, causing many buildings to collapse. In order to replace these old structures, the state will orchestrate one of the most ambitious rebuilding programs in human history. Rather than simply repairing old ruins, the government will redesign entire cities using the theatrical, earthquake-resistant Sicilian Baroque style. This will demonstrate the state's incredible ability to mobilize labor and capital in the face of total disaster.

Thanks to foreign investors, Sicilian wine will be transformed from a local peasant drink into a fortified luxury good that can survive long sea voyages. The culture of the 'Vineyard Estate' (the Baglio) will be the new symbol of Sicilian wealth and sophistication. It links the island's ancient agricultural traditions to the modern, industrial world of global commerce.

req: March to the Sound of Guns
adv.d: Adapting to the ever-changing tactics of war is no easy task. Against potentially superior enemies, we should rely on our own mobility over everything else. If we are able to pin our foes into a melee fight and send a regiment to flank and encircle their troops, we will be able to inflict devastating casualties.
Our lands are home to many skilled warriors. Among them are the Rozwi, disciplined fighters who stand ready to defend our people against any who would dare try to take our rightful lands from us.

Bosnia is home to several faiths. Not only is our land shared between the Orthodox and Catholic Churches, but it is also home to the South Slavic Christian faithful, the Krstjani. Isolated from central supervision, we will have to foster a local understanding and harmony between these different groups to maintain our stability.

Our nobility regularly gathers together to discuss the most pressing issues for our country. These meetings ensure our noble lords are aligned in their policies and show unity during our parliament sessions.

The achievements and hard work of our people deserve recognition and protection. We will establish a prestigious title for ourselves and thereby secure that recognition from neighboring rulers, formalizing our status through diplomatic bonds.

As the mines of Srebrenica become the premier source of bullion in the Balkans, the realm has moved beyond the mere export of raw ore. We have established a Royal Mint and an Assay Office to regulate the purity of Bosnian silver, producing a coin which rivals those of Venice in reliability. By mandating that all silver extracted by Ragusan or Saxon miners be processed through state-controlled refineries, we capture a massive share of the value-added profit. This liquid wealth allows us to make Bosnia the most financially solvent power in the Dinaric Alps.

In the secluded valleys of our nation, monks of our monasteries have compiled the Ljekaruše — extensive medicinal codices written in the native Bosančica script. By synthesizing ancient Greco-Byzantine theory with the high-altitude herbalism of the Dinaric Alps, these manuals provide a sophisticated system of community healthcare in an era where professional physicians are a rarity. This mastery of folk-medicine and surgery ensures our population remains resilient against the plagues that devastate the lowlands, fostering a cultural identity defined by intellectual self-reliance and the preservation of Slavic scientific knowledge.

Drawing on the inexhaustible silver veins of the central mountains, our urban craftsmen have perfected the art of Filigran — intricate silver wire-work that has become the hallmark of Bosnian luxury. These guilds operate as a powerful economic estate, exporting ceremonial daggers and fine jewelry to the markets of Venice and Vienna. By turning our raw mineral wealth into high-value artistic exports, we have created a prosperous urban middle class that is fiercely loyal to the Crown. This industrial refinement elevates the prestige of our nation in every foreign court, proving that the 'Iron Heart' of the Balkans possesses a sophisticated cultural edge that rivals the great capitals of the West.

The resinous heartwood of our native trees, known as agarwood or Trầm Hương, is treasured not only for its enchanting aroma but also for its spiritual and medicinal properties. Across the seas, nobles and monks alike covet it for incense, perfumes, and offerings. By protecting our forests and refining our harvesting methods, we can turn this rare natural gift into one of our most prized exports.

Within the lush valleys of central Champa lies the sacred temple complex of Mỹ Sơn, where for generations our kings and priests have performed solemn rites to Śiva, protector of our realm. These towers are carved with devotion and adorned with sacred symbols, connecting us to our ancestors and the divine. As long as incense burns in their sanctuaries, the soul of Champa shall endure.

Ever since our descent from Arabia and Persia, we have established communities across the Swahili Coast that integrate the local Bantu in an effort to maintain social order and make way for the rise of new architectural and cultural advances.
Attracting merchants from as far away as Persia and Arabia, our capital has become a bustling commercial hub, facilitating business from the horn of Africa all the way to the shores of China.

We may not have a very robust manufacturing industry, but one thing we do have in abundance are palm trees. Sturdy enough to support construction and shipwrighting, but flexible enough to be shaped by our artisans, mastering the use of this unique lumber will help us expand our seafaring activities, improve production, and ultimately line our pockets.

Known for their slender and elongated hull design, the Kilwan Dhow is famous for being the backbone of our maritime trade that connects our ports to faraway lands. The ship itself is a manifestation of our mastery of shipwright, as our workers utilize palm trees for a sturdy body as well as locally-grown cotton for the sails.

The Kilwan Zambuc is a smaller variation of the Kilwan Dhow, and it is primarily used for local trade, transportation of goods and pottery between the various city-states across the Swahili Coast, as well as serving as trustworthy faring vessels for short distances.

The dawn of a new age in seafaring has given us new opportunities to seek sustenance for our people. Whereas once we would only trade with the interior of Africa to procure crucial supplies of Sturdy Grains, Livestock, and Rice, we can now access new ports where food may be cheaper and more readily available.
Our superior ship technology allows us to sail further and for longer than any of our competitors, giving us a significant edge in any seafaring activity.

Originally a term to describe the inhabitants of inner Africa, particularly those of Bantu origin, these folk make up a substantial portion of our demographics. While they have many liberties and responsibilities, they are taxed accordingly in order to preserve these privileges. Their peaceful, relatively autonomous place within our legal framework has led to the organic development of linguistic phenomena and new cultural traditions.
Our ancestral founder came from Širâz, son of the 'Amīr of Persia, which makes our right to rule undeniable.

Our abundant reserve of Gold from many sources across East Africa is the cornerstone of our economy. We must take full advantage of our reserves, and use our wealth to support and disseminate a strong currency. This will help us develop as a trading hub.

We are uniquely positioned at the confluence of wealth coming from China, India, and Europe. This not only benefits us financially, but it gives us great influence in the diplomatic game between Empires and foreign powers...

ref.d: The might of our dynasty is imprinted upon the coins that circulate the markets from the Italy coast, to India, and beyond. This trimetallic coin is primarily made of Copper, Silver, and Gold, and is the first of its kind to exert such influence on a multiregional scale. Control of its circulation is synonymous with continued prosperity!

A series of loose confederations, often led by a governor that strengthens the power of local merchants, these communities push for local autonomy and urbanization. Their trading skills provide a steady stream of revenue for our treasuries.

adv.d: The legacy of Rollo, the Viking founder of Normandy, continues to define our ruling house. Such a prestigious line has led to strengthened legitimacy and respect from our peers.

Our state is governed by its own customary legal code, the Coutume de Normandie. By enshrining noble privilege, decentralized power, and property rights, this legal tradition ensures local stability while asserting our distinct identity.

Our position along the English Channel allows us to flourish as a commercial gateway. By investing in our port towns and merchant infrastructure, we can dominate regional trade while minimizing the cost of overseas operations.

During the long conflicts between France and England, we stood as a strategic battleground. The pressures of war forged a hardened officer corps and traditions of battlefield excellence that endure to this day.

Our legislative body must remain distinct from any outside influences, in an effort to preserve our cultural identity and independence. Inspired by Anglo-Norman fiscal institutions, our parliamentary procedures will surely bolster crown revenue and improve administrative oversight.

The Anka system is our method of documenting the regnal years of our rulers. Years ending in 6 or 0 are skipped, except for year 10, which is retained. The count begins at year 2, not year 1, and always starts on the Sunia, our fiscal new year.

The Muslim faithful have invaded India and subjugated many Hindu residents under their gruesome rule. Yet, Orissa stands unflinching against the warriors of Islam. We are the bulwark of Hinduism, and we shall defend our traditions and culture against any foreign invader!

Horses are not native to Orissa, and the lands here are unsuitable for raising them. Our jungles are, however, famously teeming with elephants. In the dense jungles of Eastern India, well-executed tactical cooperation between elephants and infantry can be just as deadly as a cavalry. Let us further increase the size of our elephant corps and refine their tactics, so that we will be known as a true Gajapati, 'Lord of the Elephants'.

Worship of Jagannath, the Lord of the Universe, is what unites our people. Previous rulers of Orissa were even considered to be the scions of Jagannath. Our current ruler might not be one of his descendants, but we must imprint on all that our leader is the servitor of Jagannath, and that any disobedience to them equals treason against Lord Jagannath himself.
The Muslim threat never ceases, nor does it ever rest. We must ensure our military is ready to face and combat invaders at any and all times.

Orissa has long been divided among many different princes, but their time is over! We will take control of these lands, and appoint regional governors — parikshas — instead of allowing these petty princelings to dilute our imperial authority.

The glory of past dynasties is reflected by the grandeur of the temples they left behind. We should improve our many magnificent temple complexes, and construct new ones to further the development of Kalinga architecture.
Orissa has been famous for its high-quality textiles since ancient times. Let us further encourage the textile guilds of Orissa to refine their methods of producing their fine Kalinga Cloth.
The high-quality Salt of Orissa is in demand all over India. Let us do whatever we can to encourage the Salt trade so that we may grow rich from it.

As technology advances, so does the number of people in our realm. Industrialization has driven significant population growth, and as such, we must expand our infrastructure to accommodate these growing communities.

Every caravan from the Sahel terminates its journey at Sijilmāsa, the great trans-Saharan way-station at the heart of Tafilalt where Wangara gold dust, Sudanic kola, and Saharan captives change hands for slab salt, Maghrebi textiles, and the silver of the Iberian Mediterranean. Our merchant clans operate the assay foundries, the gold-dust scales, and the bonded warehouses through hereditary charters that secure the prosperity of the entire oasis. This unbroken commercial primacy fills the Tafilalt with the wealth of the southern caravans and gives our oasis a sustained prosperity that the inland Maghrebi cities far from the desert termini cannot match.

Each ksar of Tafilalt provides its share of the seasonal horse and mehari camel-rider muster, a light cavalry of the Saharan school trained from boyhood to ride down raiders across the dunes, ambush caravans, and outpace any pursuing force across terrain no infantry can cover. Our oasis stables breed the dark-coated Berber horse on the date-palm fodder of our gardens and on the brackish wells of the deep oasis, producing mounts of stamina that no Mediterranean-bred warhorse can match in the Saharan climate. This oasis cavalry tradition gives our crown a swift mobile force whose endurance and operational speed the standing forces of the centralizing northern courts cannot easily counter.

The qā'ids of Tafilalt levy a regulated ṣadaqa al-qāfila (caravan protection tariff) on every load entering or departing the oasis at the published rates of our customs houses at Sijilmasa, Rissani, and the desert gates, in exchange for armed escort across the pre-Saharan frontier. The collection passes through bonded accountants of the qā'idal houses, with a fixed share routed directly to the central court and the remainder retained for the maintenance of the desert escort and the upkeep of the watering posts. This published-rate tariff system stabilizes our exchange of caravan custom for state protection and routes the proceeds straight to the sultan's court, sparing our treasury the inefficiency of provincial intermediaries.

Mūlay 'Alī ash-Sharīf, eldest of the Alaouite sharifian house long established at Tafilalt, receives the bay'a of the assembled qā'ids, marabouts, and tribal chiefs of the oasis as the founding emir of an autonomous southern principality. Our administrative chamber of viziers, our reformed treasury, and our court ceremonial draw equally on the Saharan Idrīsid heritage of our forefathers and on the Marinid chancery practice of the northern Maghreb, forging an emirate whose internal coherence the lands of dissidence around us cannot easily match. This consolidation of the Tafilalt under a single sharifian throne gives our court the administrative reach, the legitimacy across confessional lines, and the dynastic continuity that the older Maghrebi sultanates spend decades trying to reproduce.

The Tafilalt's irrigation register, the meticulous record of every seguia channel, every date-palm parcel, and every household water-share kept by the assembly of qā'ids, lets our fiscal officers assess and collect taxation with an accuracy and equity that the makhzen's roving inspectors cannot duplicate elsewhere. The Tafilalti caravan-houses keep their accounts under the same registry, settling state contracts at fees so modest that no inland court can negotiate comparable rates from its own merchants. This deep-rooted oasis fiscal practice gives our treasury both a steady tax efficiency and a low-cost merchant-maintenance discipline that the makhzen's central provinces cannot easily reproduce.

The qā'ids of Tafilalt maintain a chain of garrisoned outposts at Tindouf, In-Salah, Wadi Saoura, and the desert waterposts between, through which our merchant houses, our scribes, and our diplomatic envoys project influence across the deep Sahara to the emirates of Adrar, Walata, and the Sahel beyond. Our resident garrisons at each funduq station combine watering-rights, escort capability, and bonded warehousing, anchoring the trans-Saharan commercial system on Tafilalti capital and Tafilalti tariffs rather than on remote-court directives. This outpost network multiplies the commercial reach of our oasis far beyond its formal frontiers and gives our merchant houses a transit infrastructure that the inland Maghrebi states cannot easily duplicate.

The Bishop of Rome holds a position unlike any other in Christendom — not merely the highest-ranking prelate but the Vicarius Christi, whose pronouncements on matters of faith bind every Catholic ruler and kingdom whether they welcome them or not. We cultivate this authority as much through spiritual relationship as through institutional power, presenting ourselves as the father of all the faithful rather than simply their ecclesiastical superior, which gives rivals pause before they choose open confrontation with the See of Rome. This dual standing as institutional head and spiritual father generates a continuous religious influence across Europe and makes antagonizing us a costly act for any ruler who depends on the loyalty of Catholic subjects.

When the Papacy speaks in matters of faith and governance, it speaks with an authority that no secular ruler can claim — the force of divine mandate expressed through the Bulla Papalis, a formal pronouncement that carries the weight of scripture to every Catholic court in Europe.
