adv.d: Founded in the woes of the Western Schism, the Löwenbund is sworn to protect our lands from heretical revolts. We should grant them our official sponsorship and incorporate them into our court to further our cause.

In the mountainous frontier of southern Thessaly, the lords of Neopatras — first Brienne and later Aragonese — constructed and repeatedly strengthened one of the most formidable castle complexes in Frankish Greece, turning the ancient city into a virtually impregnable stronghold that withstood repeated sieges by their enemies. These towering walls, deep ditches, and cleverly situated outworks became a symbol of Latin tenacity, allowing a small but determined garrison to project influence deep into central Greece and delay the northward advance of hostile powers for generations.

Using our connections to the Crown of Aragon and the merchants of Barcelona, Neopatras has become the primary entry point for Iberian goods into the Levant. We operate a Consulate of the Sea that provides legal protection and standardized weights for all Catalan and Spanish traders. This special relationship makes Neopatras the wealthiest outpost of the Western Mediterranean in the heart of Greece.

The nation remains governed by the democratic-military traditions of the Catalan Company, where officers are elected and the spoils of war are shared. This egalitarian structure creates an army with incredibly high morale, as every soldier feels they have a personal stake in the survival of the state. While the rest of Europe moves toward absolutism, our 'Soldier's Republic' remains a fiercely loyal and cohesive fighting force.

In the fertile Spercheios valley, the Dukes have established royal stables to breed a new strain of warhorse, crossing Catalan stallions with local Balkan mares. The resulting Neopatras Charger is famed for its endurance in mountainous terrain and its shock power in the charge. This cavalry advantage allows us to dominate the open plains of Thessaly and strike fear into our rivals.

adv.n: The Ordinance of the Viles Noves
adv.d: The realm has moved to centralize its scattered mountain population into 'New Towns' (Viles Noves in the Catalan language) modeled after the planned fortified villages of Catalonia. The governance of these towns is handed to a 'Consul of the Hearth', an official tasked with managing communal wood-fuel and grain storage for the harsh winters. By controlling the heat and the bread of the highlands, our rule effectively ends the age of independent mountain-warlords, replacing them with a streamlined, urbanized bureaucracy.

Neopatras needs to replace its hereditary 'Captain-Governors' with graduates of a dedicated Administrative Lyceum. Candidates are tested on their knowledge of our civil law and the latest techniques, ensuring that the nation's officials are as comfortable with a quill as they are with a sword. This shift from 'Birthright to Merit' has turned Neopatras into the most efficiently governed territory in Central Greece, capable of precise census-taking and rapid tax-levying.

Our oasis sits at the northern terminus of the great trans-Saharan caravan routes coming up from Gao, Timbuktu, and the Niger bend. Every Soninke, Songhay, and Tuareg merchant arriving from the south must clear customs at our gates before pushing on to the Mediterranean. Our caravanserais (Sidi Lakhdar, Sidi Boumendil, the fanādiq of the central market) host the caravan crews and their pack-animals for the months between expeditions, and our brokers arrange onward shipment to Algiers, Tunis, and Tripoli. This terminus position gives our state a commanding share of the trans-Saharan trade revenues that no maritime power can dispute.

Our caravan-masters establish the Ouargla to Niger Bend route as the dominant central-Saharan trade axis, supplanting the older Sijilmasa-via-western-Sahara route as the preferred path for our merchants. We maintain the In Salah staging post jointly with Tuareg confederations, each side providing guards, water-rights guarantees, and warehouse capacity, and our jurists formalize the customs and toll schedules at every staging-post. This formalized trade-route infrastructure gives our state a logistical reach across the Sahara that no other oasis-state can match.

Our caravan-protection auxiliary corps — the mehārist companies of mounted camel-cavalry recruited from the Banū Wargla and the desert-edge Berber tribes — patrol the southern approaches to our oasis, escorting incoming caravans through the Tassili and Tademaït plateaus where Tuareg raiders are most active. They serve under our crown on a contractual basis, paid through caravan-toll revenues rather than the central treasury, and our officers integrate them as auxiliaries to the regular oasis garrisons during inter-state campaigns. This camel-corps system gives our state a flexible Saharan striking force that no settled-cavalry tradition can match in long-distance desert operations.

Our central market becomes the dominant clearing-house for the trans-Saharan gold-and-slave trade reaching the Maghreb. Bambara, Songhay, and Hausa captives are sold here to Mediterranean buyers, while the Wangara gold from Bambuk and Buré is assayed and forwarded under our seal to the mint-houses of Algiers and Tunis. Our merchant houses extend credit to caravan-masters waiting for season, our shrines accept votive offerings from grateful caravan-survivors, and our cisterns serve every passing trader who pays the standardized water-tax. This commercial primacy gives our state a fiscal cushion drawn from continental trade that no purely-agricultural oasis economy can match.

We have established unrivalled dominance over the central-Saharan trade. The Algerian-Regency caravans, the Tunisian-Hafsid merchant convoys, the Tafilalt-bound western traffic, and the deep-Sahara Tuareg routes all pay tolls at our gates. Our caravan-officers maintain registers of every animal passing through, our scribes record the goods and their values, and our crown takes a share of every transaction that the more decentralized oasis-confederations cannot match. This unrivalled trade-route dominance gives our state a continuous fiscal stream that other Saharan polities can only attempt to challenge through banditry.

Our local sharīf, Sīdī Muḥammad ben 'Abd Allāh claiming Idrīsid prophetic descent, proclaims a unified Saharan rising under a single banner of dynastic-religious resistance, gathering desert tribes, Tijāniyya brotherhoods, and disaffected oasis notables to his standard. His campaigns mobilize the deep-Sahara confederations, the Tijānī lodges, and the Tafilalti caravan-houses into an armed coalition that holds the southern Algerian frontier for years against any centralizing court that seeks to bring it under direct rule. This protracted Saharan rising gives our state a prestige of armed defiance and a cross-confederation mobilization capacity that the more rapidly-subdued northern oases never achieved.
We have been granted the rulership of Bavaria directly by the Emperor! By embellishing ourselves as the divinely-appointed protectors of Bavaria, we will ensure our legitimacy cannot be questioned.

Our nobles have distinguished themselves as formidable knights in the service of the Holy Roman Empire. We should nurture and scrupulously maintain these troops to ensure the survival of our ducal integrity.
Our lands are rich in the crops and fresh water required to brew beer, and our people readily enjoy this abundance. Many small breweries could grow into successful businesses, with the right support.

Our lands are frequently crossed by merchants wishing to trade Salt, Silver, and Livestock in the rich lands to our south. We would be foolish not to take advantage of their presence, and therefore will establish bustling trade hubs in our own lands to attract their business.

With our homeland at the feet of the beautiful Alps, we are a destination for artists from all over Europe, who seek inspiration in our incredible landscape. If we were to construct and support the appropriate cultural institutions, we could refine our court into a center of refinement and elegance, one that could rival even the most prestigious powers of Europe.
We once were ruled by Bavaria, unified in culture and allied under a single banner. We must ensure that the new Bavarian state is equally mighty, a home worthy of its strong and proud people.
Establishing a council with the sole duty of advising our ruler during times of conflict will help us develop a more capable fighting force.
We must ensure our people remain united in their faith, and that they will not be divided by heretical thoughts.
Only with a formidable standing army will we have the military might necessary to match our ambitions. With careful focus, we can expand it without having a ruinous impact on our state's finances.

No matter if we are answering to an Imperial overlord or cozying up to a potential foreign ally, our diplomats must be prepared for everything. But only if they keep Bavarian interests first and foremost in their efforts will we be able to claim true success in our diplomatic maneuverings.
Our realm needs a new standardized coin to serve as our national unified currency. Establishing a state-owned mint in our capital would ensure our total control over this new coinage.

The excellent quality of our beer has been celebrated for centuries, but for our brews to achieve legendary status, we must ensure their continued prestige and superiority for all time. Several rulers in the past have created regulations and standards for the brewing of this wonderful substance; and we could use this fact as a stamp of our breweries' quality.

As the spiritual heart of the Frankokratia, Patras has evolved into a sovereign ecclesiastical principality similar to the Prince-Bishoprics of the Holy Roman Empire. The Archbishop wields both the crozier and the sword, ruling his lands through a Synod of Defense that merges religious law with feudal military obligation. This unique status allows us to mobilize the peasantry through religious fervor, viewing every border skirmish as a localized Holy War.

The purported relics of Saint Andrew attract thousands of Catholic pilgrims who seek safety in the East, and we have established a network of fortified 'Hospices' to protect them. By charging a modest 'Protection Fee' for passage and lodging, the Archbishopric funds the maintenance of a standing army of Crusader-Monks. These funds are also used to beautify the city, making Patras the 'Rome of the East' and a beacon of Latin architecture.

To counter the influence of the Orthodox world, the Archbishop has established the first Greek-language Catholic printing press in the Peloponnese. We produce Bibles and liturgical texts that use the Greek language but adhere to Latin dogma, slowly winning the 'War of the Word' among the literate Greek classes. This cultural offensive reduces the risk of rebellion and integrates the Greek population into the Latin social hierarchy without stripping them of their linguistic heritage.

Patras has secured the right to mint its own coinage, the Patrine Soldo, which is recognized for its stable value across the Aegean. By acting as the central bank for the Frankish Morea, the Archbishop exerts a powerful economic influence over secular lords. We control the pulse of trade through the purity of our silver.

The Archbishop has established a school to train clergy in the art of international negotiation and secret correspondence. Our 'Black-Robed Diplomats' serve in the courts of Europe as the eyes and ears of the Latin East. This clerical intelligence network gives Patras a level of geopolitical influence that rival kingdoms envy.

Our ports have been declared 'Neutral Holy Ports', where merchants of all nations — Catholic, Orthodox, or otherwise — may trade in safety. This sanctuary status has turned our ports into the primary neutral ground for Mediterranean commerce. Even in times of total war, the trade of Patras continues to flow, protected by the Archbishop's ban.

The chasquis are the messengers of our state. Chosen from the fittest and most durable runners of our country, these agile men carry Quipu strings, messages, gifts, and other kinds of information, and deliver them to the target recipient. The spread of ideas, as well as the bulk of our diplomacy, rests on their shoulders.

Our road system is one of our empire's most valuable assets. To further benefit our military and administration, we will erect tambo way stations along all the main roads. These stations will be built within a day's march of each other, and will provide shelter and carry supplies for travelers.

The mit'a is a mandatory public service system fundamental to Incan society, and forms the backbone of the military service. Every ayllu must contribute capable men, adapted to combat in the highlands, to provide labor for state projects and military service.

In order to undertake great building projects in the past, our rulers had to fulfill ancient traditions by inviting every single petty chief in our empire to the capital, showering them with gifts, and holding lavish feasts. As our state grows, however, this is far from an ideal way to undertake these projects. Supplying labor and materials for construction should be the duty of each and every chief in our lands.

The Tambo is a supply depot of the Incas. The purpose of the Tambo varies significantly depending on the size of the structure. Smaller tambos serve as road stops for passing travelers while larger ones can even serve as an office for the province's administration.

No other empire is as well adapted to the heights of the Andes as we are. By maintaining settlements and storehouses at every altitude, from the lowest valleys to the highest plateaus, we have mastered the method of moving men and goods across the most difficult terrain, where other states would falter. Our llama caravans, our roads carved into sheer cliffsides, and our highland communities turn the Andes from a barrier into our own highway.

The warachikuy is a holy ceremony where young men are tested in their skills, valor, and wits, as well as their physical abilities like racing, marksmanship, combat, and durability for extended lengths of sleep deprivation. Those who pass these tests with excellence are promoted to the rank of officers for our ever-growing army.

Llamas have many functions in our society. They act as beasts of burden, as sacrifices, provide meat and wool, and even give us fertilizer for our crops with their dung. Controlling the breeding and use of llamas through government michis, or herders, we ensure that the llama population is strictly monitored. This will provide an opportunity for the llama population to increase

A system which uses knots on a string to store information, do accounting, and perform other informational tasks. Each knot represents a number from zero to nine. The knots can also be used to refer to logograms on the same string. The knots show which syllable in the logogram to use, and by combining more strings, sentences can be formed.

The Hatun Runas are the peasant class of our empire. One in fifty men are chosen for military service on their twenty-fifth birthdays, and conscripted for the next seven years. This conscription system helps us maintain a substantial professional army with superior discipline than the troops of our adversaries.

Invaders from strange lands have set foot in our territory, and threaten our very existence. But our armies are adaptive; they adjust to new enemy tactics, learn to wield their very own weapons against them, and fight with an unbreakable resolve inspired by their foes.

To ensure a stable environment for international investment, Ragusa has codified its laws into a comprehensive legal framework that defines property rights and maritime codes. By limiting the power of any single noble and establishing the Consilium Rogatorum, we create a predictable mercantile environment that attracts the wealthiest traders of the Mediterranean. This legal clarity allows a small city-state to punch far above its weight, turning a rocky outcrop into a sanctuary of Libertas that no feudal lord can easily subvert or ignore.

Facing the recurring devastation of the Black Death, Ragusa has pioneered the world's first mandatory maritime quarantine system on the islands of Mrkan and Bobara. By isolating incoming crews and goods for forty days (quaranta), we protect our urban population while maintaining the functionality of our port when other Mediterranean hubs are paralyzed by plague. This scientific approach to public health ensures that the Republic remains a reliable and clean port of call, preserving our manpower and mercantile networks during even the most lethal periods of European history.

Our shipyards have become famous for producing the argosy, massive carracks capable of surviving the Atlantic and the Indian Oceans. By standardizing our shipbuilding techniques and securing high-quality oak from the Bosnian forests, we ensure that the Ragusan merchant marine is the most technologically advanced in the Adriatic. These vessels are designed for maximum cargo capacity and defensive firepower, allowing our merchants to dominate the spice and silk routes while flying the flag of Saint Blaise in every major port from London to Goa.

To maintain our status as a center of refinement, we have established the Collegium Ragusinum, a Jesuit-led institution of higher learning that attracts the sons of Balkan and Italian nobility. By producing a class of highly educated diplomats, scientists, and poets, we ensure that Ragusa's leadership is never outmatched in the courtrooms of Europe. This intellectual investment turns our small city into a center of culture, where the fusion of Latin logic and Slavic spirit produces the scholars who will define the cultural awakening of the entire Adriatic littoral.

As the wars between our neighbors intensify, we have declared our city a strictly neutral Porto Franco (Free Port). By refusing to host foreign warships while offering high-quality repairs and storage to all merchant vessels, we ensure that the conflict only serves to increase our profits. This 'Economic Non-Alignment' makes Ragusa the only safe harbor in a burning sea, allowing us to capture the trade routes that our rivals have abandoned in their pursuit of military glory.

We have moved beyond mere shipping to the world of high finance by formalizing one of the first sophisticated systems of maritime insurance. By pooling the risks of our merchant families through the Monte di Pietà, we allow our captains to undertake daring new voyages to the Americas and the Far East with minimal personal risk. This financial innovation ensures that Ragusan capital is always in motion, creating a self-sustaining cycle of wealth that keeps our city wealthy and relevant even as the traditional Mediterranean trade routes begin to fade in importance.

The mountain passes that cross through our lands connect the plains of Italy with the highlands beyond, and we have learned to profit from every traveler and merchant who must pass our gates. Control of the Alpine Routes gives us a leverage that no army alone can provide, and we use it to sustain friendships on both sides of the mountains. This geography is our greatest inheritance.

The trails and roads that thread through our mountains are known to us as no outsider can know them, and this knowledge shapes how we move and supply our armies. Our soldiers march along paths that would leave foreign troops exhausted and disoriented, arriving fresh where others would arrive worn. This intimate mastery of the Alpine Terrain is a form of strength no fortress can replace.

Our court has fostered a distinctive literary tradition that weaves together the languages and voices of both sides of the mountains, producing chronicles and verse of surprising richness. The Occitan and Italian tongues mingle in our writings as they do among our people, creating something that belongs to neither tradition entirely. This chronicle of who we are preserves our identity in letters that outlast stone.

We have fortified the natural strongpoints of our mountains with walls and towers that make our land a nightmare for any invader who seeks to hold it by force. Every valley approach leads to a defended pass, and every pass to a Hilltop Citadel that must be taken before any advance can continue. Any army that enters our lands uninvited will find the mountains themselves arrayed against them.

Our soldiers have been forged in the hard school of mountain warfare, where endurance and discipline matter more than numbers and where every man knows the value of his comrades. The Highland Regiments of our marquisate have built a reputation for steadiness that makes them sought after even when our state is not at war. This tradition of arms is the shield behind which our people have always stood.

The highland villages of our marquisate have long sustained themselves through skilled craftsmanship, producing goods of quality that find their way into the markets of the plains below. The knowledge of our artisans is passed within families and guilds, ensuring that each generation inherits the Alpine Craft Traditions intact. This industry sustains the prosperity of our communities and earns our highland towns a reputation for quality that outlasts any political upheaval.

We assert a prestigious, albeit disputed, descent from the French Royalty, granting our diplomats a unique standing in the courts of Europe. This perceived noble pedigree allows us to negotiate as peers with the Italian city-states and the Papacy, securing alliances that would be denied to common Balkan warlords.

Our house has risen to preeminence by masterfully navigating the clashes among the clans, positioning the Thopia family as the arbiters of Albanian sovereignty. By weaving together a complex web of alliances, we will secure the first true Princeps Albaniae title recognized by both the East and the West. With the lion of our crest flying over the ramparts of the coast, we have established a professionalized administrative core that outpaces the primitive feudalism of our rivals, ensuring our house remains the apex predator of the Adriatic shore.

We have moved away from loose clan associations toward a semi-professional core of infantry based in our central urban axis. This modernization allows us to respond to threats with a speed and discipline that traditional tribal levies cannot match.

We have funded the construction of grand cathedrals and fortifications, blending Gothic and Byzantine styles to showcase our wealth and piety. This architectural splendor serves to legitimize our rule in the eyes of the Church and our subjects, turning our cities into symbols of permanence.

Our name has become synonymous with the state itself, allowing us to integrate various ethnic groups under a single banner. By promoting the most talented individuals regardless of their origins, we have created a meritocratic bureaucracy that outshines our feudal rivals.

We have expanded our commercial influence by offering state protection to all merchant vessels flying the Thopia banner. This naval security has turned our ports into the preferred hubs for Levant trade, siphoning wealth away from the decaying ports of our rivals.

The Pau dels Dos Coprínceps — the perpetual peace agreed between the Bishop of Urgell and the Count of Foix in the paréage of 1278 — establishes Andorra as a dual sovereignty in which neither prince may act in our valleys without the consent of the other. Our diplomats learn from the start that every external relationship must be balanced against the watchful eye of a second prince, breeding habits of careful drafting and patient negotiation rare in courts that answer to a single sovereign. This dual-headed sovereignty teaches our envoys to extract more from foreign courts than the size of our delegation alone could ever justify.

The Sis Parròquies — Canillo, Encamp, Ordino, La Massana, Andorra la Vella, and Sant Julià de Lòria — each send representatives to the Consell de la Terra to deliberate on taxation, public works, and the customary law that governs our valleys. Decisions taken in council bind every parish equally, and the parishes in turn administer their own commons, irrigation, and dispute resolution without sending matters to the co-princes for routine governance. This parish-level self-government keeps the costs of administering our Crown remarkably low and gives every household a direct voice in the policies they live under.

Our annual tribute to the co-princes — the Questia — is paid in alternating years to the Bishop of Urgell and the Count of Foix, a sum that has remained nominally fixed for centuries while our valley economies have grown substantially. The modest scale of the tribute, combined with the deflation of its real value over time, allows our parish councils to fund themselves through local revenue. This favorable fiscal settlement frees court spending for public works and the ceremonial obligations of statecraft rather than on tribute paid to outside powers.

Our Síndic Procurador General presides over the Consell de la Terra and acts as the executive face of Andorra before the two co-princes, negotiating on behalf of the parishes without ever surrendering the council's ultimate sovereignty over their own affairs. The síndic is chosen by consensus among the parish representatives — typically a respected churchman or notable — and serves as a permanent buffer between local interests and external pressure. This neutral mediator role keeps both clergy and nobility committed to the council's decisions and limits the factionalism that more partisan executives produce.

The high passes connecting our valleys to French Ariège and Catalan Urgell — the Port d'Envalira, the Coll de la Botella, and the Port de Cabús — are maintained year-round by parish corvée labor that clears rockfalls, marks the snow stakes, and stocks the refuge huts that allow military and commercial traffic through. Centuries of mountain road-building have produced a corps of parish engineers who can move men and supplies across alpine terrain in conditions that defeat lowland armies. This high-altitude logistical capability lets our small forces concentrate against intruders faster than any flatland army can reposition.

Our policy of Neutralitat Pirinenca — Pyrenean neutrality — keeps Andorra clear of the great wars that consume our larger neighbors, our valleys serving instead as a refuge for political exiles, smugglers, dynastic claimants in transit, and the occasional troubadour whose sudden popularity has rendered his home kingdom's tax-gatherers uncomfortably attentive. Both co-princes find the arrangement convenient enough that they spare us from any formal alignment with their wider conflicts. This neutral reputation makes our envoys welcome at conferences from which combatant states are excluded and gives our small army the time to prepare defensive positions no aggressor cares to assault.

Our ancestral home in the highlands of our nation is a natural citadel of jagged peaks and narrow ravines that is nearly impossible for a conventional army to navigate. We have further fortified every strategic pass and mountain peak, ensuring that any enemy invader must pay a staggering price in blood for every inch of our territory they attempt to occupy.

adv.n: The Iron Mines of the Interior
adv.d: The rugged mountains of central Albania under our control are rich in high-quality iron ore essential for the tools of war. We have established state-sponsored smelters to provide our clans with a constant supply of superior steel blades and armor plates, ensuring we are never dependent on foreign imports to equip our growing armies.

Following the heroic example of our leaders, our house is known as the first to rise and the last to surrender against our foes. This legacy of unyielding resistance has forged our people into a nation of warriors who see struggle as a sacred duty rather than a burden.

By providing significant land grants and funds to our monasteries, we maintain the spiritual loyalty of the nobility and the peasantry. These sacred sites serve as the cultural heart of our principality, where our victories are celebrated.

We have sworn an eternal oath that so long as we breathe, the heart of the rebellion will continue to beat. Our troops are drilled with a fanatical devotion to our ruling house, ensuring they maintain discipline even in the face of overwhelming imperial numbers.

We have evolved our traditional skirmishers into elite mountain grenadier units, specialized in heavy assault and siege warfare. These troops combine their ancestral mountain agility with the devastating firepower of modern explosives, making them the terror of any fortress garrison.

Our fief sits upon the most famous pass in history, and we have taken the lessons of Leonidas to heart by fortifying the mountain tracks with Frankish stone. Every narrow path is a deathtrap for the invader, and every cliffside is a vantage point for our archers and scouts. To pass through Bodonitsa is to run a gauntlet of steel, ensuring that the heart of Greece remains shielded from northern threats.

adv.n: The Curia of the Three Keys
adv.d: To manage the wealth generated by the resurgence of the northern trade routes, the Marquisate has established the Curia of the Three Keys. The state treasury and the legal archives are locked in the citadel of Bodonitsa, requiring three separate keys held by the Marquis, the Latin Bishop, and a representative of the local Greek burgesses. This primitive but effective system of 'Checks and Balances' prevents the embezzlement that often plagues small feudal states, ensuring that the heavy tolls collected at Thermopylae are actually spent on the fortress walls.

Living among the crags of Mount Kallidromos, our people have developed a form of light infantry combat that emphasizes vertical mobility and the use of the crossbow. These 'Mountaineers of the Pass' can disappear into the rocks after a volley, making them impossible for traditional heavy infantry to engage. They serve as the eyes and ears of the southern states, providing early warning of any movement from the north.

Reflecting our Venetian heritage, we have established consulates in the major ports of Euboea and Attica to represent the interests of Bodonitsan merchants. These offices act as intelligence hubs, funneling information about naval movements directly to the Marquis. We may be a mountain state, but our eyes are always fixed on the horizon of the sea.

The Marquisate of Bodonitsa had evolved from a mere frontier watchtower into the administrative nerve center of Central Greece, necessitating a transition from feudal whim to a professionalized civil service. The establishment of the Great Chancellery overlooking the Spercheios valley signals a move toward a centralized, modern state where the old Frankish baronial privileges are replaced by a cadre of legally trained 'Civil Knights' who manage the complex tolls and land registries of the Phocian heartland.

In the age of gunpowder, the rugged woodsmen of the Oeta mountains have been organized into specialized light-infantry corps. These riflemen excel in hit-and-run tactics, using the steep terrain to harass invading columns with lethal precision. They are the nightmare of any general attempting to force the northern passes of Greece.

Our country survives through its strong ties to maritime trade and the constant exchange of goods. To maintain an orderly harbor, we will need to dredge fresh waterways and build more docks and warehouses, attracting new merchants and their ships.
A newly founded organization between cities with a strong Hanseatic presence, the Wendish Coinage Treaty will provide us with a strong basis to facilitate trade and commerce in our lands.

Our domain is protected by the labyrinthine Karavasta Lagoon, where our people have mastered navigation through mudflats and hidden channels. This watery landscape serves as a natural fortress that is nearly impossible for heavy foreign armies to map or conquer, providing a sanctuary that no cavalry charge can reach.

The biological wealth of our coastal waters provides a stable food supply that supports a larger standing militia even during regional famines. By monopolizing the harvest of the lagoons, we ensure that our population remains healthy and our granaries full, fueling our state's survival.

We specifically train our levies to lure enemy units into the deep bogs where their armor becomes a liability. In these environments, our light, unarmored infantry reigns supreme through ambush tactics, turning the very earth into a weapon. Our ability to adapt to any terrain and move fast in the worst conditions makes us a dangerous foe.

By controlling the river mouths and coasts, we can successfully dictate the flow of timber and grain from the interior to Venetian galleys. We have positioned ourselves as the indispensable middlemen of the Adriatic trade, ensuring no merchant can bypass our tolls.

We have begun the process of draining parts of the Myzeqe marshes to create even more fertile farmland. This engineering feat not only increases our tax base but allows us to construct permanent roads through what was once impassable bog.

We have unified all coastal harbors under a single administrative authority, streamlining the collection of dues and customs. This centralization has made us the most efficient trade administrators in the Adriatic, attracting foreign investment.

Our fortresses are a brilliant emblem of our resilience and fortitude, built to endure not only the difficult local climate, but also any foreign invader foolish enough to mount an attack into our unforgiving territory.

The fertile valleys of our heartland allow us to fund a lavish court and a highly trained cavalry force through advanced irrigation. This agricultural surplus provides the economic bedrock for our political ambitions, allowing us to sustain a larger professional retinue than our rivals.

Ruling from the Castle of Berat, the 'City of a Thousand Windows', we represent the peak of Albanian urban sophistication and Byzantine-style administration. Our court serves as a magnet for scholars and artisans, turning our capital into a beacon of culture that rivals the grand cities of the East.

Our family keeps meticulous and grand records of our history and territorial rights, ensuring our ancient claims are never forgotten. This literary tradition preserves our high Byzantine titles, overawing local rivals with our imperial dignity and historical depth.

Our land sits on the primary trade routes from the interior; by taxing the silk caravans, we maintain a full and prosperous treasury. This revenue allows us to patronize the finest calligraphers and icon painters, turning our domain into the cultural capital of southern Albania.

We have turned our capital into a center of culture, preserving the wisdom of the East and the West for future generations. This intellectual prestige makes our court the destination for the finest minds of the Orthodox and Latin worlds alike.

We have introduced the large-scale cultivation of cash crops in our most fertile valleys, fueling a new domestic industry. By processing our own raw materials into high-value products, we have created an industrial base that supports a wealthy and loyal urban population.

u.t: Chivalric order: Society with the Lion

adv.d: Founded in the woes of the Western Schism, the Löwenbund is sworn to protect our lands from heretical revolts. We should grant them our official sponsorship and incorporate them into our court to further our cause.

adv.d: Founded in the woes of the Western Schism, the Löwenbund is sworn to protect our lands from heretical revolts. We should grant them our official sponsorship and incorporate them into our court to further our cause.

adv.n: Eternal Alliance of the Forest Cantons
adv.d: We have forged an eternal alliance with our friends in the neighboring Cantons. Had it not been for this treaty, we would have surely succumbed to the Habsburg invaders and fallen under the rule of foreign tyrants yet again. These alliances will ensure our survival for centuries to come.

The vast coastal pine forests (the Pinedi) of the Adriatic coast are managed as strategic state assets. Our people have developed a culture of sylviculture and salt, harvesting timber for shipbuilding and managing the vast salt pans of Cervia. By reinforcing these traditions, our people will provide a non-agrarian source of wealth that is immune to crop failure, giving us the liquid capital necessary to face any challenges.

No city in the Western world preserves the art of the Mosaic as we do — our basilicas and mausoleums are clad in tesserae that glow with gold and deep blue, images that have survived centuries of war and neglect without losing their impact. These works attract scholars, pilgrims, and artists who come to study what the ancient world looked like before it was lost. This tradition of extraordinary craftsmanship deepens our cultural heritage and lends our state a prestige that no contemporary rival can easily replicate.

Ravenna has long been a prize worth fighting for, and the fields outside our walls have witnessed battles of extraordinary ferocity that have made our name synonymous with the hardest kind of fighting in Italy. We harden the walls of the city and steel the soldiery against the shock of pitched battle, drawing on the lessons that only ground stained this often can teach. This martial tradition forges an army that is difficult to break and a city that is difficult to take.

Our city is a living archive of a civilization that has vanished almost everywhere else — the gold-leaf apses, the intricate stonework, the iconographic traditions of the Byzantine world survive here in a concentration found nowhere else in the west. Artists and patrons who come to study these works carry their influence outward, raising the reputation of everything produced in our workshops. This custody of a unique heritage turns our past into a source of lasting cultural and commercial value.

The marshes and lagoons that surround our city are both our shield and our burden — they protect us from armies but flood our fields and breed disease. We commit to a systematic program of drainage and embankment, digging channels and raising dykes that push back the water and claim new agricultural land from the swamp. This transformation of the wetlands into productive territory feeds our growing population and expands the taxable estate of the state.

After generations of stagnation, we invest in our city's renewal — clearing old districts, building new roads and market squares, and offering incentives to artisans and merchants who settle within our walls. The city that results is more open, more prosperous, and more capable of absorbing the growth that comes with a reforming state. This reinvestment in our urban fabric makes Ravenna a place people want to come to rather than one they are merely stuck in.
We have been granted the rulership of Bavaria directly by the Emperor! By embellishing ourselves as the divinely-appointed protectors of Bavaria, we will ensure our legitimacy cannot be questioned.

Our nobles have distinguished themselves as formidable knights in the service of the Holy Roman Empire. We should nurture and scrupulously maintain these troops to ensure the survival of our ducal integrity.
Our lands are rich in the crops and fresh water required to brew beer, and our people readily enjoy this abundance. Many small breweries could grow into successful businesses, with the right support.

Our lands are frequently crossed by merchants wishing to trade Salt, Silver, and Livestock in the rich lands to our south. We would be foolish not to take advantage of their presence, and therefore will establish bustling trade hubs in our own lands to attract their business.

With our homeland at the feet of the beautiful Alps, we are a destination for artists from all over Europe, who seek inspiration in our incredible landscape. If we were to construct and support the appropriate cultural institutions, we could refine our court into a center of refinement and elegance, one that could rival even the most prestigious powers of Europe.
We once were ruled by Bavaria, unified in culture and allied under a single banner. We must ensure that the new Bavarian state is equally mighty, a home worthy of its strong and proud people.
Establishing a council with the sole duty of advising our ruler during times of conflict will help us develop a more capable fighting force.
We must ensure our people remain united in their faith, and that they will not be divided by heretical thoughts.
Only with a formidable standing army will we have the military might necessary to match our ambitions. With careful focus, we can expand it without having a ruinous impact on our state's finances.

No matter if we are answering to an Imperial overlord or cozying up to a potential foreign ally, our diplomats must be prepared for everything. But only if they keep Bavarian interests first and foremost in their efforts will we be able to claim true success in our diplomatic maneuverings.
Our realm needs a new standardized coin to serve as our national unified currency. Establishing a state-owned mint in our capital would ensure our total control over this new coinage.

The excellent quality of our beer has been celebrated for centuries, but for our brews to achieve legendary status, we must ensure their continued prestige and superiority for all time. Several rulers in the past have created regulations and standards for the brewing of this wonderful substance; and we could use this fact as a stamp of our breweries' quality.

adv.n: Eternal Alliance of the Forest Cantons
adv.d: We have forged an eternal alliance with our friends in the neighboring Cantons. Had it not been for this treaty, we would have surely succumbed to the Habsburg invaders and fallen under the rule of foreign tyrants yet again. These alliances will ensure our survival for centuries to come.

Traders travel far afield, to provinces well beyond the reach of our authority, and even to the territories of our rivals. If these traders were to, perhaps, also serve as our eyes and ears, what secrets might we learn?

Our society is remarkably dynamic, offering commoners, also known as mācēhualtin, the path to become pīpiltin, or noble, by exceptional military service through the tlahuiztli honor dress rank system. This unique opportunity for upward mobility grants our people a distinct advantage over those in neighboring societies.

Proficient in terracing hills for cultivation and skilled in crafting arable land on shallow lake portions through ingenious chinampas, our populace's remarkable agricultural abilities will significantly benefit our society.

Whether we take up arms on a search for prestige, to instill fear in our foes, to take captives for sacrifice, or simply to acquire wealth, our people are accustomed to a continuous state of warfare, enduring its hardships with more resilience than members of other nations.

Our tributary regions will receive appointed tribute collectors, called calpixqueh, who will be in charge of ensuring the flow of tribute never stops. There will be a calpixqui in the region, and another in the capital of our nation, for each tributary state.
We will create a system of provinces for the city-states that are integrated into our realm in an effort to centralize our power.

The superiority of Nahua culture is very clear, as neighboring peoples increasingly adopt it as their own. This cultural diffusion and spread of influence creates opportunities for us to extend our political control well beyond our borders.
As we face new enemies, new military tactics have to be developed or learned. This invaluable knowledge will be taught in our Tēlpōchcalli.

The hummingbird holds a crucial role in our mythology. Linked to the god of war, Huītzilōpōchtli, it embodies fallen warriors' reincarnation and is honored for its bravery. The hummingbird will be made a new symbol for our banners, one that will inspire our soldiers to fight unto their deaths!

Contact with foreigners from other continents has given us interesting new ideas about our gods. The Quetzalcōātl prophecy unveils a reality beyond myth — a glimpse of truth. Quetzalcōātl, 'the Feathered Serpent', will soon return and herald a transformative era, vanquishing darkness for enlightenment. Symbolizing cosmic fusion, he will bridge matter and spirit, restoring balance and elevating human consciousness.

The aggressive nature of our warriors is known — and feared — beyond our borders. When battle starts, our enemies shiver in fear at the sight of our combatants charging at them with frenzy, as if they were about to be run down by the heralds of Death itself.
The needs of our people have been adapting to the new markets that have opened to our traders, and we have been training our merchants in methods to maximize our earnings.

In the isolation of the Crimean mountains, the remnants of the Crimean Goths and the local Greek population have fused into a single, resilient identity. This culture combines the stoic, martial heritage of the North with the administrative and maritime brilliance of the South. This 'Theodoran' spirit is our greatest defense, creating a population that views itself as the last true guardians of the Roman frontier, willing to fight to the last man for their unique way of life.

Our capital, Mangup-Kale, is a literal mountain carved into a fortress, surrounded by sheer cliffs that defy any siege engine. We have expanded these natural defenses with a series of sophisticated tunnels, cisterns, and hidden sally ports, allowing the city to hold out for years if necessary. This impregnable base ensures that even if our lands are ravaged by the Golden Horde, the heart of our Principality remains safe, serving as a beacon of hope for all Christians in the North.

Despite our small size, we control the vital ports that connect the vast fur-producing forests of Russia to the markets of the Mediterranean. We have negotiated exclusive rights with the local Tatar Khans to be the sole shippers of these furs across the Black Sea. This lucrative monopoly provides us with the wealth necessary to pay for Genoese engineers and Byzantine scholars, ensuring our tiny principality remains a center of wealth and sophistication amidst the steppe.

As the main Greek-speaking state in the North, Theodoro has become a symbol of religious resistance and cultural survival. We have established our Prince as the Protector of the Pontic Greeks, drawing immigrants and scholars from distant places. This religious prestige gives us a moral authority that transcends our borders, making us a key player in the grand religious struggles as the Northern Star of the Greek Orthodox faith.

Drawing upon the ancient, grim traditions of our Gothic ancestors and the disciplined military manuals of the Romans, we have formed the Red Guard. These elite shock troops are recruited exclusively from the highest mountain villages of the Crimea, trained to fight in the pitch-black tunnels of our fortresses and the claustrophobic ravines of the coast. Armed with heavy polearms and the latest flintlock pistols, they are masters of the sudden, devastating raids. Their reputation for never taking prisoners and never retreating makes them the most feared infantry in the Euxine basin, capable of breaking the morale of even the most hardened regiments.

The Gothic-Greek hybrid culture of Theodoro has fully shed its defensive shell, transforming into a 'War Machine'. No longer content with mere cliffside survival, we have industrialized our mountain strongholds into massive foundries and barracks, producing a professional officer corps and a conscript army trained in the brutal school of steppe warfare. Every citizen of the Principality is now a soldier first, viewing the surrounding plains not as a threat, but as a harvest field for Gothic glory and Roman reclamation. This 'Total War' footing allows us to strike with a ferocity that terrifies our larger neighbors, as we field a military machine that is disproportionately powerful relative to our small territorial size.

adv.d: We have forged an eternal alliance with our friends in the neighboring Cantons. Had it not been for this treaty, we would have surely succumbed to the Habsburg invaders and fallen under the rule of foreign tyrants yet again. These alliances will ensure our survival for centuries to come.

cathedral_advance.d: A cathedral is one of the largest and most important types of Christian temple, where the Bishop has a cathedra, or seat. While a church can be beautiful and detailed, a cathedral is majestic, of enormous dimensions, and adorned with the finest and most intricate details.

three_teachings.d: The Three Teachings are a philosophy originating from China which combines the teachings of Confucianism, Daoism and Buddhism into a harmonious, singular teaching. Confucianism represents the ideology of the law while Daoism is the worldview of the radical intellectuals. These two opposite ends of the philosophical spectrum would then be connected with the philosophies of Buddhism.

four_noble_truths.d: The foundational teachings of the Buddha, the Four Noble Truths explain the reality of being. Nothing is permanent, which causes pain to the spirit, due to its attachment to this transient existence. This spiritual pain can only be eased by liberating oneself from desire and letting go of these attachments, which is achieved by following the Noble Eightfold Path.

noble_eightfold_path.d: The path to being liberated from Saṃsāra and achieving Nirvāṇa, the Noble Eightfold Path is the purest distillation of Buddhist practices. Dictating both one's mental state and physical actions, it determines proper comportment for any follower of Buddhism.

middle_way.d: The Buddha teaches us that we should avoid extremes, as neither with sensual indulgence nor extreme asceticism can one achieve enlightenment.

three_jewels.d: The Three Jewels, or Three Refuges, are the three supports in which a follower of Buddhism takes refuge. These refuges are the Buddha, the enlightened one; the Dharma, the teachings of the Buddha; and the Saṃgha, the monastic community that preserves the Dharma.

buddhist_syncretism.d: Buddhism has its origins in India, but it has since spread far and wide, coming in contact with many different beliefs. As such, it contains much syncretism not only with the previous Hindu traditions, but with the many other deities it has been exposed to.

sutra.d: A type of sacred text in both Dharmic and Buddhist religions, they vary in format and content. Regardless, they are always considered to be valid sources of knowledge, and proper study of them is required if one is to develop their spirit.

buddhist_councils.d: Throughout Buddhist history, monastic councils have discussed canonical texts across different schools. Although the specific form, outcomes, and records of the councils may vary from school to school, the unifying power of such councils — bringing diverse traditions into dialogue — should not be underestimated.

buddhist_canon.d: Called different names and even containing different texts, depending on the branch of Buddhism, the Buddhist Canon is a collection of sacred Buddhist texts. Containing everything from monastic rules to Sūtra, or teachings of the Buddha, any person dedicated to Buddhism should be familiar with them.

pali_canon.d: Although there are many different canons in Buddhism, depending on the school, the Theravāda Pāli Canon is the oldest and most prestigious. Other schools have created their canons from a mix of texts with various sources, but the Pāli Canon has remained unchanged since the times of Ashoka 'the Great', and contains the words of the Buddha himself. It has also served as the foundation of many other schools.

buddhist_universities.d: Since antiquity, Buddhist centers have also been hubs of learning and knowledge, attracting people from all over to study in our institutions. Nālandā was the biggest of these centers in the past, but many others have followed in its footsteps since.

xuanzang_travels.d: Xuánzàng, a Chinese Buddhist monk who lived during the Táng dynasty in the 7th century, embarked on a seventeen-year overland trip to India in order to visit it centers of learning and to gather a great number of Buddhism texts. Among other places he visited Nālandā, where he learned from the best masters, and on his return to China he brought with him more than a thousand documents, which made a great contribution to Eastern Buddhism. His trip and his records served as basis for the tale of Journey to the West, in which a monk is tasked by the Buddha to travel to India in search of some holy texts. accompanied among others by the Monkey King, Sūn Wùkōng.

silk_road_transmission.d: It is undeniable the effect that the Silk Road has had on the spread of Buddhism. Whether via land or sea, trade has allowed Buddhism to spread far from its origins in India.

bodhisattva.d: Regardless of the school of Buddhism one adheres to, a Bodhisattva is an important figure, although their exact characteristics and importance vary between the different traditions. In all cases, however, they are deserving of reverence and admiration.

avalokitesvara.d: Also known as Guānyīn or Kannon, Avalokiteśvara is one of the most revered Bodhisattvas. Represented as a male or female depending on the school, and even in some considered to be the origin of all Hindu deities, Avalokiteśvara is the Bodhisattva of compassion, and is associated with the mantra Oṃ maṇi padme hūm̐.

maitreya.d: Maitreya is currently a Bodhisattva, prophesized to be the future and final Buddha of the current era. His destiny is to reestablish the teachings of the Dharma in the world after they have been forgotten by humanity, and as such he is the successor of Siddhārtha Gautama.

mount_meru.d: Mount Meru is the sacred mountain at the center of the universe in both the physical and spiritual sense for Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism. As it is the center around which everything else revolves, so does our entire country revolve around our ruler.

naraka.d: Also called Niraya, Naraka refers to the realms of suffering where one's bad karma is cleansed before being reincarnated. There are many Naraka realms, and both the time an individual must reside in them and the punishments they will receive while doing so depends on how much karma they need to gain before being reborn in one of the upper realms.

four_heavenly_kings.d: Each presiding over one of the cardinal directions, the Four Heavenly Kings are in charge of protecting the Deva realm from the Asuras. They are also responsible for assessing the virtue and morality of mortals.

vegetarianism.d: Although it depends on the school, there are some rules in the Dharma regarding abstinence from meat consumption. Each school has different views about the strictness of this abstinence, and also whether it should apply only to the monastic community or to the population in general.

edicts_of_ashoka.d: A legal code published by Emperor Ashoka 'the Great' in the 3rd century BCE, these edicts include strictures promoting for Buddhism. Although this code is from many centuries ago, it still deserves respect and reverence from any member of the Buddhist faithful.

five_precepts.d: The foundational code of Buddhist ethics and morality, the Five Precepts represent the most basic rules believers must follow in Buddhism, whether part of the ordained monastic community or not. They instruct people to abstain from killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, and intoxication.

monastic_communities.d: Buddhist life is centered around its communities of monks and nuns, called the Saṃgha. They are governed by the Vinaya, the rules and precepts that dictate the operations of any Buddhist religious community.

prestigious_schools.d: Buddhism has developed into a myriad of schools, each one centered around one type of monastic community and declaring a preference for certain texts. However, some of these schools have gained recognition, while others have been relegated to obscurity. Associating with the more prestigious schools gives those people a bit of prestige as well.

offerings.d: It is a precept of Buddhism to make offerings to the Three Jewels in order to accumulate merit. These offerings may be material or non-material, and some monastic communities depend completely on food donated by their followers for their survival.

incense_burning.d: The practice of burning incense is a staple of any Buddhist ritual or offering. Varying in shapes and forms, it is common for both lay people and ordained monks and nuns alike to light incense before performing any ritual or meditation. As such, the smell of incense constantly permeates any Buddhist temple.

ascetic_practices.d: Although the Buddha warned us about the dangers of extreme asceticism, some among the monastic community still perform these strict practices. Limiting the type of cloth they can wear, the food they can eat, or where they can live are some of the restrictions adopted by those who wish to walk this path. Although such abstemious behavior is not a requirement for obtaining merit, it has its own benefits for the practitioner.

mindfulness.d: An essential part of Buddhist practice, Mindfulness means to be aware of the phenomena of both body and mind, while keeping the teachings of the Buddha always present in the mind. With this, one can avoid the arising of unwanted states, and develop into the wanted ones.

dana.d: Denoting generosity, Dāna is defined as the act of giving without anything in return, and is a key virtue in all religions related to the Dharma. Helping others selflessly, whereas individually or communally, is one of the key ways of accumulating karma.

ahimsa.d: The concept of Ahiṃsā, or nonviolence, is a key virtue among all religions following the Dharma. Any conflict is encouraged to be resolved peacefully through dialogue, rather than the use of force. Unfortunately, that is not always possible, but violence should always be the last resort, and its use must be just.

resistance_to_persecution.d: Although it has spread widely throughout the world, Buddhism has also seen its fair share of persecution across the ages. Its temples and images may have been destroyed, its followers slaughtered or forced into hiding, but nonetheless its faithful have persevered.

buddhist_meditation.d: Meditation is a common practice among all Buddhist followers, regardless of their school. The aim is to train the mind and the spirit to develop mindfulness, tranquility, and insight, and thus ultimately achieve enlightenment.

res_publica_christiana.d: We must pursue good relations with our fellow Christian faithful of all denomination, even if we consider some of their practices to be heresy.

roman_orthodoxy.d: The righteousness of the Roman Catholic faith and its doctrines must remain unquestioned, in order to entrench its authority in the minds of our people.

marian_devotion.d: Our dedication to the Virgin Mary must remain a central pillar of our worship.

crusading_knights.d: In this country, we have a long tradition of sending our finest knights and aristocrats to spread the true faith to heathens in the Baltic and Mediterranean regions. We will fulfill our Christian mission by bringing the faith to the unenlightened, while also acquiring experienced commanders for our armies.

catholic_pilgrimages.d: The holy sites of our faith should be seen by every follower. Encouraging pilgrimages, and elevating those who have undergone the process, should be a priority of our administration.

inquisition_advance.d: The Inquisition was created in the 12th century as a means to combat the Cathar heresy, but its reach grew significantly in the Late Middle Ages as the main tool of the Catholic Church to counter the spread of dissident doctrines.

preaching_friars.d: Preaching friars — members of Mendicant Orders like the Dominicans and Franciscans — have taken their ministry beyond the monastery walls to preach directly among the people. By supporting and praising them openly for these acts of devotion, we can strengthen religious conviction throughout the realm, even among the most remote peasants.

devotio_moderna.d: The Devotio Moderna, or modern devotional movement, is rapidly gaining popularity among members of our faith. We should implement some of their teachings into our court, so as to make ourselves appear particularly devout.

denounce_heretics.d: We must ensure the supremacy of the one true faith, and denounce all criticisms of it as the bitterest of heresy.

beguins_and_beghards.d: Many of the faithful have devoted themselves to a life of prayer and good works, which usually comes with taking the veil or becoming a monk. However, they have not taken formal vows, and act without official Roman approval. Nevertheless, we should support these popular efforts to do good deeds and help our people.

grand_display_of_faith.d: To honor God, we need to construct great monuments in His name. Not only will this display our devotion to our faith, but it will also demonstrate the magnificent skills of our sculptors and architects.

monastery_productions.d: The holy occupants of our monasteries are bastions of sensible, frugal living. Our clergy should consider adapting their own lifestyles to more closely resemble those of these monks and nuns.

reform_church_music.d: We must accept the proposed reforms to our liturgical music. The diluted, soulless tunes currently in fashion can no longer be considered acceptable ways to express the glory of the divine.

frequent_councils.d: It has been proposed that holding religious councils more frequently would prevent theological disputes and criticisms from festering unchecked. While we may not have full control over the curia, we can at least use our influence to encourage regular synods that address relevant issues before they can become crises.

mendicant_orders.d: The orders of our faith, who have taken vows of poverty and live itinerant lives, have brought assistance to many remote parts of our country. We should support their efforts as much as we can without disrupting their holy missions.

exsurge_domine.d: To eradicate the evil of heresy, the Lord Himself will arise and purge them from our lands!

confutatio_augustana.d: In these turbulent times, we must clearly define orthodox Christian doctrine, while systematically refuting the false beliefs that endanger the very souls of our people.

roman_catechism.d: Our clergy must adopt the official Roman Catechism as their guide for instruction. This text will improve priestly education and ensure only consistent, orthodox teachings are transmitted to the populace.

oversea_missions.d: Our clergy is ready and willing to spread our faith into new territories overseas. With their contribution, settling new lands will be made easier and cheaper.

baptism_books.d: We must confirm baptism as an important cornerstone of our faith by keeping meticulous records of who in our population has or has not yet been baptized.

second_scholasticism.d: We will need to revive and refine the philosophical movement of medieval scholasticism.

catholic_sunday_schools.d: Educating the people is an important part of our religious duties. We should establish schools, closely tied to our normal worship services, to provide basic education to our flock.

index_librorum_prohibitorum.d: The dangerous ideas of the Reformation will spread like a toxic fungus in the minds of our subjects if they have access to written works propagating these silly thoughts! We must forbid certain dangerous texts, and keep a comprehensive list of which books are not allowed.

catholic_cuius_regio_eius_religio.d: Whose realm, his religion. We will have to accept that other countries follow other faiths, and that this will sometimes be a crucial factor in diplomacy.

embellish_baroque_art.d: Our faith has a long tradition of sponsoring and promoting great works of art. The development of the splendid new Baroque style reflects the pathos and glory of our theology beautifully, and should receive particular sponsorship.

national_churches.d: The State must take greater control over the Church in our land. We cannot allow foreign entities to exercise undue influence over our ecclesiastical administration; our Church must serve our realm first.

entrenched_church.d: No matter which people we rule over, the Church provides a way to give them a unified structure.

catholic_enlightenment.d: For our faith to withstand the attacks of the Enlightenment, we must adapt, and present new perspectives in and about the Church.

divine_church_music.d: Many of our composers have created their greatest works thanks to the inspiration provided by their faith. We should actively seek out the most talented artists and hire them immediately so as to never let our churches and cathedrals suffer from inferior music.

continue_missionary_works.d: Missionary efforts to carry our faith to the far corners of the world can never be considered finished. We need to sponsor more missions to further bring the light of Catholicism to these unilluminated souls.
