epic_poetry_advance.d: For millennia our people have preserved the legends of gods and heroes through epic poetry. Works such as Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, alongside Hesiod's Theogony, stand among the greatest monuments of our cultural heritage. These timeless narratives continue to shape our identity and inspire generations.

cond.t: Has DLC: Fate of the Phoenix

makaron_nisoi_advance.d: The Makaron Nesoi, the Blessed Isles, are believed to be the ultimate destination of the most virtuous souls. Those who live lives of piety and excellence may earn their place among heroic spirits in the Elysian fields. Tales of these sacred realms inspire the pursuit of virtue, honor, and moral excellence throughout society.

cond.t: Has DLC: Fate of the Phoenix

religious_dialects_hellenic_faith_advanc.d: Although our faith is shared across many communities, notable divergence exists in ritual, tradition, and local religious practice. Over time these variations develop organically, sometimes even within the same province. Much like language evolves into regional dialects, our religious customs gradually form distinct local expressions while remaining within the same sacred tradition.

cond.t: Has DLC: Fate of the Phoenix

offerings_to_the_moirai_advance.d: Each year a portion of our ritual offerings is dedicated to the three Moirai, the Fates who govern destiny itself. Clotho the Spinner, Lachesis the Alloter of life's portion, and Atropos the inevitable end preside over the completion of every mortal life according to the cosmic order. In many theological traditions their authority is considered primordial, sometimes even surpassing that of the gods.

cond.t: Has DLC: Fate of the Phoenix

on_hubris_and_morality_advance.d: The principles of our faith originate from the will of the gods and are interpreted through priests, seers, and acts of divination. Through prophecy and sacred interpretation mortals attempt to understand the divine order of the cosmos. Yet the surest path to moral virtue remains piety, reverence, and the careful avoidance of destructive hubris.

cond.t: Has DLC: Fate of the Phoenix

variety_in_divine_identity_advance.d: Our pantheon contains a remarkable variety of deities, each representing different virtues, crafts, and ideals. This diversity allows every individual to discover a divine patron that resonates with their life and vocation. The modest altar of a blacksmith to Hephaestus carries meaning equal to the noble devotion offered to Zeus.

cond.t: Has DLC: Fate of the Phoenix

mystai_advance.d: Hidden behind masks, symbols, and sacred ritual, influential initiates gather within secretive mystery cults. These organizations exercise considerable social and political influence, shaping events through ritual authority, wealth, and discreet alliances. Wise rulers maintain good relations with these mystai, lest their influence and intrigue turn against the state.

cond.t: Has DLC: Fate of the Phoenix

preserve_theogony_advance.d: Hesiod's Theogony recounts the origins and genealogy of the gods, revealing the birth of the divine order itself. Through its verses, symbols of authority such as the scepter and the voice of rule are presented as sacred responsibilities. The work reminds rulers that true authority must be exercised through wisdom, moderation, and reason.

cond.t: Has DLC: Fate of the Phoenix

unify_priestly_class_advance.d: For much of our history the priesthood responsible for sacred lands and temple revenues has functioned in a decentralized manner. Yet recent developments in foreign religious institutions have introduced new ideas of organization and central authority. These influences now encourage the unification and coordination of our own priestly hierarchy.

sruti.d: Meaning 'that which is heard', Śruti are the holiest and most ancient texts of Hinduism. They are considered to be a divine revelation and thus not attributed to human authorship, although some deny their divine origin while still accepting their authority.

vedah.d: The main texts among the Śruti are the Vēdaḥ, which are the oldest Sanskrit texts. Their authorship is attributed to Brahmā in the Mahābhārata, and they are the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda, and the Atharvaveda.

smrti.d: Meaning 'that which is remembered', Smṛti texts are inspired by or originated from the Vēdaḥ, and thus are considered less authoritative than the Śruti due to being derived from them. However, unlike the Śruti, the Smṛti texts have attributed authorship and are transmitted through manuscripts.

mahabarata.d: One of the two major Smṛti texts together with the Rāmāyaṇa, the Mahābhārata is an epic of ancient India. It is the longest epic poem ever written, about ten times bigger than the Greek Iliad and Odyssey combined, and it narrates the story of a dynastic struggle for the throne of the ancient Indian kingdom of Kuru culminating in the Kurukshetra War, also called Mahābhārata War. The story ends with the death of Kṛṣṇa and the end of his dynasty.

ramayana.d: One of the two major Smṛti texts together with the Mahābhārata, the Rāmāyaṇa is an epic of ancient India. It narrates the life of Rāma, avatar of Viṣṇu, as a prince of the kingdom of Kosala. It emphasizes the importance of virtue in all aspects of one's life.

purana.d: Considered part of the Smṛti, the Purāṇa are texts with a variety of content. Cosmology, divine genealogies, astronomy, grammar, love stories... almost everything can be found within them. As such, even though they are not part of the Śruti, their influence on Hindu beliefs and society is strong, as they combine diverse local beliefs and traditions into the common narrative of the Vēdaḥ.

atman.d: Referred to the true and eternal unchanging Self, it is the essence of each individual's consciousness. According to the astika schools, this Ātman is distinct from the mind and body, and it is also different from the Jivātman that persists across multiple lifetimes. In contrast, the nastika schools interpret the concept differently, or reject it entirely.

nastika_schools.d: Some schools of thought in Hinduism deviate from the mainstream, rejecting the authority of the Vēdaḥ and the existence of Ātman. These schools, like Jainism and Buddhism, are thus heterodox, although they still contain many of the shared core beliefs of Hinduism.

astika_schools.d: Called the orthodox schools of Hinduism, they accept the authority of the Vēdaḥ and the existence of Ātman. Although consisting of many different branches, this commonality of acceptance gives the Āstika Schools a lot of common ground.

diversity_of_beliefs.d: The beliefs of the people of India center around the concept of Dharma and the text of the Vēdaḥ, but they are manifested in a myriad of forms and practices. Even the gods recognized and worshiped are not the same for everyone, but a common thread of concepts is present throughout.

ishvara.d: Interpreted differently depending on the school or branch of Hinduism, Īśvara refers to the Supreme Being or God. Therefore, it can refer to Śiva for Shaivism, to Viṣṇu for Vaishnavism, or to any personal god of the individual.

sanskritization.d: Hinduism has spread much farther than its origins in India, and many other cultures and countries have adopted Sanskrit concepts and titles to refer to their own identity. As such, the concepts of Hinduism have seamlessly permeated and blended into foreign beliefs.

bhakti_movement.d: Having emerged in the 6th century, this movement promotes love and devotion to one's personal god or towards an enlightened individual. It appeals to the lay population by speaking to them directly on their own terms. A highly influential movement, it is changing how religion and belief themselves are understood by our people.

yoga.d: A prominent Hindu school and philosophy, Yoga is a set of practices both physical and spiritual, with the purpose of controlling the mind and body. Performed for millennia, it has almost become synonymous with the path of enlightenment.

diwali.d: Called the festival of light, Diwali is when we celebrate the triumph of the Dharma; the victory of good over evil and light over darkness. We will light candles and lanterns to symbolize this victory, and we will honor our ancestors.

holi.d: Held at the beginning of spring to celebrate its arrival, Holi is the festival of colors and love. We commemorate agriculture and good harvests, and at the same time enjoy the myriad of colors that spring offers. It is also the time to have fun and resolve conflicts, removing one's emotional impurities.

holy_rivers.d: Rivers and their veneration have always been an important part of Hinduism. From the Indus to the Ganges, there are many rivers considered holy, on the shores of which many rituals are held. Their waters are considered sacred, and they are a common site for purification rituals.

advaita_vedanta.d: Rejecting the dualism between consciousness and matter, Advaita Vedānta claims that the Ātman, or the innermost self or consciousness, is one and the same as the supreme reality or consciousness of the universe, Brahman. In this sense, the physical material world is just an illusion hiding the ultimate reality of the Brahman.

hindu_muslim_relations.d: There has been a lot of interaction in the past between Hinduism and Islam, and there will continue to be so. Our peoples have learned to live peacefully together and there has even been some degree of syncretism between the two faiths.

hindu_unification.d: Despite the differences in beliefs and practices throughout Hinduism, there are more commonalities between us than differences. A common unified view of Hinduism has started to emerge, and our people can gain a great sense of unity through it.

hindu_architecture.d: Regardless of the style of construction, be it a Śikhara, Vimāna, or Prāṅg, Hindu temples are recognizable everywhere for their tall, decorated towers. A representation of Mount Meru, more or less emphasized depending on the region, these spires serve both as a signal of faith and a demonstration of power.

varna_system.d: Since the times of the Vēdaḥ, there has existed the concept of one's Dharma being classified as one of the four possibles: Brāhmaṇa, scholars or priests; Kṣatriya, rulers or warriors; Vaiśya, farmers or merchants; or Śūdra, artisans or servants. These classifications are not rigid, but instead represent the ideal of an individual's calling, and they have been very influential in Hindu society.

extreme_pacifism.d: Based on the concept of Ahiṃsā, Hinduism always advocates for pacifism and nonviolence. However, our enemies should still be wary of provoking us, lest we end up exemplifying the complete opposite extreme when roused into war.

hindu_empires.d: There have been many empires in the past that followed Hinduism. From the Maurya and Gupta empires in India, to the Śrīvijaya Empire in Indonesia, and the long-lasting Chola Dynasty, Hinduism has always been the spirital force behind the throne of powerful rulers.

sacred_cattle.d: As part of Ahiṃsā, it is prohibited to slaughter cattle. They instead are respected and venerated as maternal figures, and are symbols of selfless provision and sacrifice. Having been worshiped since the time of the Vēdaḥ, they still command enormous respect and attention.

judaism_communal_autonomy.d: Our communities govern themselves through the kahal — the rabbinic-elder council that adjudicates internal religious law, raises communal taxation, and represents our religious people to the host crown.

judaism_court_patronage_finance.d: Religious-minority status exempts our financiers from the Christian usury prohibitions binding majority counterparts, opening moneylending and mint-master niches at every royal court that needs credit.

judaism_tikkun_mysticism.d: Our mystical school develops the doctrine of Tikkun — cosmic repair — framing the dispersed condition of Jewish as an active spiritual mission to mend a shattered world through prayer, study, and ethical action.

judaism_halakhic_codification.d: Our jurists organize centuries of accumulated halakhic rulings into structured legal compendia, giving every observant community access to harmonized standards through manuscript and printed networks.

judaism_court_patronage_banking.d: Our financiers transcend individual royal lending to operate multi-court banking houses simultaneously, leveraging the diaspora as a cross-state credit network no single-religion banking community can replicate.

judaism_rabbinic_council.d: Leading rabbis of our communities convene a regional council to harmonize halakhic rulings, regulate inter-communal commerce, and represent our religious people before the crown — appointing negotiators and resolving disputes.

judaism_diaspora_communal_institutions.d: Our communities formalize the Beit Din — the rabbinic court — with codified jurisdiction over marriage, divorce, inheritance, and excommunication, binding our religious community into a coherent legal-spiritual order independent of host tribunals.

judaism_state_credit_apparatus.d: Our religious banking houses transition into the apparatus of state credit, provisioning entire wars and underwriting peace-settlements directly — the host state's fiscal-military capacity becomes inseparable from our religious community's collective creditworthiness.

judaism_hasidic_movement.d: The popular-mystical movement of Hasidism revolves around charismatic tsaddikim who guide their communities through emotional-experiential piety, joyful song, and personal closeness to the divine — reaching the unlettered peasantry that pure-textual scholarship cannot.

judaism_rationalist_yeshiva.d: Our scholarly yeshivot sharpen Talmudic analysis into a precise rationalist method — close textual reading, systematic legal deduction, and rigorous critique — publishing commentary and responsa for the wider observant community.

judaism_religious_emancipation.d: Absolutist and revolutionary states grant our religious community civic equality, opening guilds, professions, military service, and elective offices that were religiously barred for centuries — our worshippers continue their internal religious life while becoming full subjects of the host state.

judaism_reform_movement.d: Religious reformers modernize observance by introducing vernacular liturgy, decorum reforms, and theological reinterpretation that aligns religious practice with the bourgeois civic life into which emancipation has placed our religious community.

judaism_international_banking_networks.d: Our religious banking dynasties — spanning multiple courts through interlocking family banking houses — serve as informal diplomatic conduits between states that cannot openly negotiate, transferring not only funds but messages, terms, and quiet pressure.

judaism_mussar_movement.d: The Mussar ethical-spiritual movement turns inward — replacing externalized practice with deliberate self-cultivation, character refinement, and meditative ethical discipline as the response to modernization pressures eroding traditional observance.

judaism_modern_orthodoxy.d: Orthodox observance reconciles itself with secular education, civic participation, and bourgeois life — formulating the principle of religious law within modernity rather than against it, while maintaining strict ritual observance.

judaism_positive_historical_movement.d: The Positive-Historical religious approach treats halakhic law as historically conditioned but enduringly authoritative — embracing scholarly historical analysis of religious sources while preserving the legal binding of those sources.

second_council_of_ephesus.d: The Second Council of Ephesus, convened in 449 at the instance of Pope Dioscorus of Alexandria, was a legitimate Christian council despite its denunciation by the Catholic and Orthodox Churches. At this council, the formula of Cyril of Alexandria — which states that Christ is a single incarnate nature, both human and divine — was officially accepted.

rejection_of_chalcedon.d: As they did not accept the Second Council of Ephesus, the Council of Chalcedon was called at the instance of Pope Leo I, who demanded the nullification of the Second Council of Ephesus. We reject this false council, and stand by the decisions made in the original one.

monophysite_vs_miaphysite.d: Although Miaphysitism also proclaims that the figure of Christ has only a single nature, it differs substantially from the Eutychian Monophysite view which proclaims that the humanity of Christ was absorbed into his divinity. Though there may be some that also call us followers of Monophysitism, it is just an agreement in words, as in substance our views are clearly different.

original_christianity.d: There have been many schisms and divisions in the Christian world, but our creed traces its roots on the original true Christianity formulated from the First Council of Nicaea. Every split from the main branch after this is mere heresy.

beyond_the_borders.d: Christianity undoubtedly originated inside the cradle of the Roman Empire, and many of its branches have been content to stay in that region. Miaphysitism, however, was on the edges of the Empire after being denounced by the Chalcedonians, and has spread far beyond its birthplace, bringing the light of God to the most remote places.

isolated_reaches.d: Miaphysitism has managed to spread to very distant places. Even while surrounded by enemies and heretics, our faith has remained strong.

independent_leaders.d: Due to the isolation of Miaphysitism, it has been difficult at times to contact other patriarchates. As such, our leaders have learned to act independently, while at the same time keeping in contact with the rest of the Christian world as much as possible.

jerusalem_focus.d: We always keep the holy city of Jerusalem in our minds, as not only it was the place where Jesus preached and died, but also where he will return to in his Second Coming. As such, we always pray facing in the direction of Jerusalem, no matter where we are.

acceptance_of_old_testament.d: Some Christian denominations have decided to reduce the importance of the Old Testament, claiming that the arrival of Jesus completely supersedes it. We, however, maintain that it is still relevant, and that some instructions in it are as valid as they were when they were written.

primacy_of_alexandria.d: Although Miaphysitism has many branches and independent leaders, we recognize Alexandria and its seat as our spiritual leader. However, this is a sign of respect for the Apostolic Throne and a way to honor it, rather than a bestowal of any special prerogatives.

school_of_alexandria.d: The Catechetical School of Alexandria, allegedly founded by the Apostle Mark himself, is the oldest school of catechism in the world. There, biblical and theological studies have been taught since the start of Christianity itself. Although the school itself was destroyed when the Bishop of Rome was declared to be above the Patriarch of Alexandria, its tradition has endured.

preserving_of_local_languages.d: Despite the importance of Greek and Latin in early Christianity, Miaphysitism has preserved its liturgy in more local vernaculars, like Coptic, Aramaic, and Armenian. Venerable languages in their own right, each Miaphysite branch preserves its own historical tongue.

double_patriarchate.d: Both Alexandria and Antioch see themselves as having two different patriarchates, one for Miaphysitism and another for Orthodoxy. Although they both may claim legitimacy, only Miaphysitism preserves the true patriarchates.

eastern_christianity.d: We are part of the branch of so-called Eastern Christianity, which amalgamates many different denominations with different theological and liturgical traditions, but also with many common cultural aspects.

life_among_infidels.d: The lands of the faithful have often been tainted by the presence of unbelievers, but this is why our clerics have ventured forth towards the unknown to bring the light of Jesus to distant lands. We have thus influenced these lost souls in more ways than what one might expect, even if we have not been able to make them see the error of their beliefs.

gradual_departure.d: Although they were quick to brand us as heretics, Miaphysitism did not cut ties with the rest of the Christian world instantly. We kept in contact with the other patriarchates, and attended the councils, but it was gradually made clear that Miaphysitism is too different from those heretical beliefs.

thrive_under_persecution.d: Although our faithful have been persecuted by heretics for centuries, our beliefs have persevered. No matter how many times they bring us down, we will rise again!

preserver_of_national_identity.d: It is because of our history of being persecuted and oppressed that our Church became responsible for preserving our identity. It is in the bosom of the Church where our languages and traditions have been kept safe, and therefore we have unshakeable faith in this institution.

defense_against_heretics.d: Ever since our split from other Christian faiths, the heretics have come to us with accusations and condemnations many times. They may call themselves Christian, but their views are obviously clouded, whereas our vision is made clear by the light of God.

remote_patriarchates.d: Conquest and persecution have repeatedly forced our patriarchates to relocate after their seats have fallen under control of heathen conquerors. Though we now operate from new locations, the original seats remain spiritually revered in our tradition, albeit from a distance.

further_reaches.d: Despite many attempts by nonbelievers to stop our faith from spreading, it has nevertheless made its way to many different peoples and cultures, bringing light wherever it goes.

internal_communion.d: Despite having independent patriarchs, all branches of Miaphysitism maintain mutual communion. This helps them build relationships with each other, and promotes unity in the Church.

cradle_of_monasticism.d: Monasticism in Christianity was born in Egypt, when the Christian faithful retreated to the desert to pray and dedicate their lives to God. Miaphysitism can therefore claim this history as their own through the Alexandrine tradition.

unique_architecture.d: The relative isolation of our patriarchates have resulted in the development of unique architectural styles for our holy places. Although other Christian denominations may be more prominent, our captivating architecture is an inspiration to the faithful.

people_of_allah.d: We are the followers of Allāh, the only true God, and abide by His Word. All those who believe in Him are our brothers and sisters in His eyes.

holy_revelation.d: The Word of Allāh was revealed to His Prophet Muḥammad, peace be upon him, and transcribed in the Holy Qur'ān. Through its verses, Allāh's will is passed to His faithful, and all Muslim believers should be familiar with its passages.

islamic_calligraphy.d: Islam is not only a religion of peace, but of the arts. The calligraphy used to write the verses of the Qur'ān and the names of the prophets often straddles the line between scripture and art.

islamic_prayer.d: One of the Five Pillars of Islam, Aṣ-Ṣalāh is the obligation for a Muslim faithful to perform daily prayers. Although the number of times one must pray every day and the specific movements when doing it may vary from school to school, the act of daily prayer is common among all Islam.

zakah.d: One of the Five Pillars of Islam, Al-Zakāh is a form of almsgiving considered a religious obligation for any Muslim faithful. Giving money to help the needy is a mandatory charity for everyone that can afford it, and it is considered a tax.

muslim_lineage.d: Ever since the times of Muḥammad, peace be upon him, Islam has been intrinsically linked to rulership structures. As such, our dynastic line is also legitimized by the faith itself.

muslim_caravans.d: From the many paths of the Silk Road, to the salt routes across the Sahara, our people have a tradition of embarking on trade ventures to faraway lands, providing us and the rest of the Muslim world with a wide selection of available goods.

islamic_golden_age.d: The impact that the Islamic Golden Age had on the entire world, not only in Muslim countries, is absolutely undeniable. Some of these infidel nations are only now emerging from their dark ages of ignorance, making their first attempts at artistic and scientific 'discoveries' that we invented — and perfected — long ago.

ramadan.d: A commemoration of the first revelation to Prophet Muḥammad, peace be upon him, the month of Ramaḍān is the holiest month in Islam. During this month, all Muslim faithful are expected to perform Ṣawm — fasting and abstinence — during the daylight hours, as well as prayer and reflection.

sunnah.d: Consisting of the traditions and practices attributed to Muḥammad, peace be upon him, the Sunnah dictates how every Muslim faithful should behave, and is also what gives Sunnism its name. Although the different schools of jurisprudence may vary on the details, they all have their basis in the Sunnah.

imamate.d: The basis of Shiite faith is that Muḥammad, peace be upon him, designated 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib as his successor. As such, the figure of Imām is that of a spiritual leader coming from the line of Muḥammad, peace be upon him, to lead all Muslim faithful.

islamic_jurisprudence.d: Centuries of scholarship have matured the science of fiqh and the uṣūl al-fiqh into a complete framework for governing the realm by the Sharī'ah. With the law so thoroughly articulated, the trained jurists who staff our courts can administer the law in its proper way, allowing us to maintain the structures of our government functioning.

indian_sea_trade.d: Muslim traders have sailed the waters of the Indian Ocean for generations, traveling impossibly far in search of rare and valuable goods. From the eastern coasts of Africa, to the shores of India, and even as far as the spice islands of Indonesia, the waters are crossed by vessels of the Muslim faithful.

muslim_trade_communities.d: The presence of Muslim traders in faraway lands puts them in contact with many different peoples and beliefs. The establishment of trade communities among them allows for a certain degree of blending and syncretism of their beliefs with the true Word of Allāh.

expansionist_faith.d: From its origins in Arabia, Islam has expanded far and fast. In a few generations, its believers spanned from Iberia to India, the most rapid religious expansion the world has ever seen. There are new lands waiting to be touched by our light, however — perhaps it is time for a second Muslim expansion.

blend_of_influences.d: Islam has expanded to many new places since its origins in Arabia, and with this spread, it came into contact with many different peoples and ways of life. Many exchanges of influence happened during this process, to the point that many characteristics not originally part of Islam have become intrinsically associated with the faith.

islamic_schoolars.d: Islam has always encouraged study and analysis of its scriptures, to the point where we have developed entirely different schools of thought on how to interpret them. Our scholars are therefore extremely learned in the Qur'ān and our other holy texts, capable of having the most in-depth theological discussions.

gunpowder_empires.d: Gunpowder may have been invented in the Far East, but it was through Islam that it became widely used throughout the world. Gunpowder weapons have been a staple of our armies for generations, and its production and use is one of our defining characteristics.

established_holy_sites.d: While other religions have somewhat lax and inconsistent views towards how their holy sites are used, the rules of Islam about sacred places are quite clear. Our people will undoubtedly make their pilgrimages with the appropriate reverence and dignity.

islamic_courts.d: The royal courts of Muslim countries have always been among the most admired in the world. Praised for our refined culture and luxurious appointments, tales of the magnificence of our courts have spread far and wide, and our people take great pride in this reputation.

schools_of_thought.d: Islam tradition has always emphasized the pursuit of knowledge and education. From schools of jurisprudence and theology to the great libraries and institutions of learning established by various rulers, Muslim scholarship has earned admiration throughout the Muslim world and well beyond.

distant_trade_ventures.d: It is from the most distant places that the most lucrative trade goods come. For many years, Muslim traders have traveled huge distances both on land and across the seas in search of profitable trade opportunities.

resilient_merchants.d: Muslim traders endure the harshest of conditions during their expeditions. From crossing the scorching sands of the Sahara and Gobi Deserts, to braving the monsoon-plagued waters of the Indian Ocean, they have proved time and again that they will undergo any hardship in order to bring about successful trade.

jewels_of_the_desert.d: Islam arose from the sands of Arabia and spread across a largely arid region. Yet some Muslim cities became like prosperous jewels shining in the harsh desert, literal and figurative oasis made bountiful through trade, architecture, and irrigation. With wise investment and planning, any desert settlement can achieve a similar status.

comprehensive_land_survey.d: In order to know who should pay taxes, we must first know who owns what. A comprehensive land survey, and regularly updating it, are therefore essential. We will always get what we are due!

counting_the_people.d: Now that we know who owns what, the logical follow-up is to get a clearer idea of who lives where. This will tell us where to look when we need fresh recruits for our armies.

cosmopolitan_court.d: People from all over admire the beauty and sophistication of our Muslim court. We have therefore become an appealing destination for talented luminaries of all kinds, which only adds to our overall court vibrancy and prestige.

caliphate.d: The Ḵilāfa, or Caliphate, is the union of all Muslim faithful under a single ruler in the form of the Ḵalīfa, who is to be the political and spiritual successor of Muḥammad, peace be upon him. Although there are different ideas about who is eligible to be Ḵalīfa, the idea of all Islam united under a single banner has always been the primary focus of this process.

ibadi_imamate.d: Unlike the Ḵilāfa or a divinely appointed Shiite Imām, an Ibadi Imām does not rule over the entirety of the Muslim world, but instead governs locally. Every community can be ruled independently by its own Imām.

contacts_network.d: The extensive reach of Islam has brought Muslim countries in contact with many different foreign lands. Maintaining a rich network of international contacts such as ours is always beneficial for diplomacy.

infiltration_tactics.d: Although the ancient Nizārī Shiite order of the Ḥashshāshīyīn has been largely mythicized beyond their original scope, their tactics of subterfuge and assassination were undeniably effective. If we employ such infiltration tactics ourselves, we should benefit from the same success.

unified_armies.d: It cannot be denied that Islam has spread to many different cultures and peoples since its emergence in Arabia. As long as they believe in Allāh, any person should be able to fight in His name, regardless of their origin.

harsh_environments.d: Islam has, since its inception, found its way to civilizations in some of the harshest environments of the world. If anyone from outside our region tries to invade our territories, they will find it fiendishly difficult — as they should!

the_pentarchy.d: The old structure of the Church formulated by Emperor Justinian is still in full effect in Orthodoxy. Although the patriarch of Rome believes himself to be above all else, for the authentic Church, the cities of Constantinople, Alexandria, Antioch, and Jerusalem remain far more important.

imperial_creed.d: Orthodoxy has been the official faith of the Roman Empire ever since its adoption of Christianity. The heresies of the West and their falsely proclaimed 'emperors' will not be able to discredit our legitimacy.

filioque_issue.d: The heretical addition of the Filioque clause, which states that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Father 'and the Son', was done without calling the appropriate ecumenical council, and therefore it is illegitimate. We are the guardians of the true prayer, and Rome shall be damned for their heresy!

septuagint.d: Our Old Testament is encoded in Greek, using the version known as the Septuagint, which is a translation from Hebrew done in the 3rd century BC. It was written by seventy-two isolated translators, who all came up with the exact same translations independently. It is thus definitely divinely inspired, and the direct word of God.

anagignoskomena.d: Our Bible contains all books worthy of veneration and study, even though some may have less importance than others. The Anagignoskomena are not present in the Hebrew Bible, so they receive less attention than other texts, but they are nonetheless worthy of being read and should not be disregarded.

religious_icon_power_advance.d: Icons are the physical representation of our faith, sacred depictions of holy figures designed to inspire awe and devotion to those that contemplate them.

church_guidance.d: The Scriptures are the Word of God, but only the Church is able to interpret their correct meaning and to relate it accurately to the flock. Any independent reading or interpretation of the Scriptures outside of Church guidance would only lead to being lost in falsehoods and on the path to heresy.

unchanging_tradition.d: The tradition passed down to us by Jesus Christ and the apostles is consistent, without any changes, additions, or subtractions whatsoever. Our faith is undeniable in its truths, and what is fundamentally true about this world cannot be changed by mortal hands.

church_councils.d: As the Church must be united in its judgments, any matter too complex for a single bishop to resolve requires us to call a council, where the bishops will consult the mind of the Church itself. The council's decisions shall therefore reflect the consensus of the Church as a whole.

greek_rite.d: Our rites and canonical practices have been for centuries well-defined following the Greek rites of Constantinople. Although there may be some small variations in certain places, there is remarkable homogeneity in the rites performed throughout Orthodoxy.

physical_body_of_christ.d: Our Church is the physical manifestation of the Body of Christ on Earth, having no difference from the one in Heaven. As such, the Church is the physical embodiment of the Lord Savior, sent for the benefit of His people.

sight_veneration.d: The most important aspect of veneration is the faithful be reminded of great works, miracles, and figures through their natural sense. As such, our churches are adorned with vibrant images and colors, ringing with music and sweetly scented with our holy incense, so that the presence of Christ on Earth can be immediately felt by all inside.

theotokos.d: The Virgin Mary is a key figure in our beliefs, as she fulfilled the Old Covenant by carrying within her the New Covenant in the figure of Christ. As such, being the bearer of Christ God-incarnate, she was literally the Mother of God, and has a place of prominence above all other saints.

heavenly_architecture.d: Orthodox religious buildings are designed in imitation of heaven. Their construction centralized around the basilica, the central dome that serves as a roof and symbolizes the heavens. Richly decorated in beautiful images and gleaming golden icons, they are a wonder to behold.

iconostasis.d: One key feature of any Orthodox church is that of the Iconostasis, a wall of icons that separates the main body of the building from the altar. The icons it contains serve as a visualization of the link between the worshipers and the Holy of Holies, and thus the link between Heaven and the people, serving as a guide for the people towards Heaven.

julian_calendar.d: The time of our country and our Church has been for centuries measured by the Julian Calendar, promulgated by Julius Caesar in 46 BC. It not only unifies all eastern Christian nations, but it also serves to dictate when the important feasts and celebrations are to be held.

paschal_cycle.d: Orthodoxy contains some movable feasts around Pascha, Easter, organized in the Paschal Cycle. The ten weeks before Pascha are called Triodion, while the fifty days after Pascha are called Pentekostárion. This cycle marks the most important celebrations in the liturgical year.

oktoechos.d: An eight-mode system of writing music, the Oktōēchos has been the system used for writing religious chants and music for the Church for centuries. It is the foundation of Orthodox chant, although with some variations between cultures.

prestigious_monasticism.d: In Orthodoxy, monasticism and asceticism are highly valued and almost a requirement. Any bishop must be a monk first, and they must become a monk before being consecrated if they are not. As such, monasteries and monasticism centers have a big impact on our clerical life.

national_rites.d: The presence of different autocephalous patriarchates in our Church allows for certain variations between the national rites of each country. However, the unity of the message remains, and the Church as a single entity is not broken.

heirs_of_rome.d: Many have claimed to be the heirs of Rome and indeed the whole Roman Empire. However, only our religion is the true faith of the old Empire, and therefore only we can legitimately claim to be a direct descendant from it.

legacy_of_saint_andrew.d: According to legend, Saint Andrew himself visited Scythia and the northern shores of the Black Sea, prophesying a great flourishing of Christianity once he reached the future site of Kyiv.

christianization_of_the_slavs.d: The people of the Kievan Rus' were among the first of the Eastern Slavic people to accept the light of Christ and convert to Orthodoxy. From there, the faith spread throughout the region.

cyril_and_methodius.d: Two Byzantine theologians from the 9th century, these men were instrumental to the evangelization of the Slavs. They are credited for developing the Glagolitic alphabet, the first one to ever be used to transcribe Church Slavonic, and their followers later developed the Cyrillic alphabet, naming it after Cyril in his honor.

interaction_between_church_and_state.d: The patriarchates have absolute authority over their own jurisdictions and those who occupy them. By tying their authority to that of the ruler, we can take advantage of the resources of the Church, and use them to strengthen state authority.

outwards_expansion.d: It is the holy duty of the Church to bring the light of Christ to the pagan and the infidels. We must go beyond our borders to carry salvation to every lost soul!

justified_holy_wars.d: We cannot allow heathens and heretics to dictate our actions. It is our holy duty to cleanse the land of their impurity so that the true realm of God can be manifested on Earth.

resistance_to_the_infidels.d: Our Orthodox brethren have seen themselves at times under the yoke of foreign infidels. However, we have learned to endure such oppression, and even live in peace alongside these infidels.

eastern_ecumenism.d: Christian denominations from the Oriental Orthodoxy are often confused with Eastern Orthodoxy by the uninitiated. Although they are different from us in many key issues, they are still Christian, and our many commonalities could be used to bring them back to the correct faith.

structured_patriarchates.d: Our patriarchates have always been well organized and structured, each with its own attributions and delimitations. This allows for a better-functioning Church, which leads to a better-functioning state.

heian_kyo.d: The city of Heian-Kyō has been the residence of the Emperor for centuries, and is a center for art and culture. It is there where the lavish court of the Fujiwara flourished, and all the people in Japan looked to it with awe and inspiration. We shall embrace its traditional role, and with our patronage make the culture of our capital flourish once again.

matsuri.d: Every local shrine and temple has its own festivals and celebrations. The people are always eager to participate, for it is their chance to offer devotion and gratitude towards their local protector Kami.

onmyodo.d: Coming from China centuries ago, the theories of Yīn and Yáng evolved in Japan into Onmyōdō. Expert practitioners, called onmyōji, deal with the purification and exorcism of evil and vengeful spirits, as well as with divination, astronomy, and the study of nature.

sumo.d: Derived from an ancient agricultural ritual, in which dances served as prayers for a good harvest, the practice of Sumō has escaped the confines of the court and is now a popular practice among the commoners. It also serves as a form of combat training.

nanto_rokushuu.d: The temples of Nara have been influential since Buddhism first came from China. The six schools that formed around these temples are a renowned repository of knowledge, especially about the teachings of the Buddha and the various ways of achieving enlightenment. However, they also teach more mundane, but equally valuable subjects, such as how to properly administrate a monastery.

shinbutsu_shuugou.d: Since Buddhism came to Japan, its teachings have coexisted with the worship of local Kami. This has led to them both blending into a single combined set of beliefs, albeit with distinct ritualistic practices.

honji_suijaku.d: One of the key practices in Shinbutsu-Shūgō is to identify the local Kami as manifestations of the different Buddha, and the Buddhas as manifestations of the different Kami. In the end, they are one and the same, with core forms or Honji taking on different aspects, or suijaku.

hachiman_worship.d: Hachiman is one of the most venerated divinities. Originally a deification of Ōjin Tennō, after the introduction of Buddhism he was later also identified as a Bodhisattva. He is the protector of the Imperial line and the tutelary god of the warrior class.

gozan_jissetsu.d: The 'Five Mountains System' originated in China from state-sponsored Chán Buddhist monasteries, atop the holy mountains that gave the system its name. In Japan, the practice continued in the Kamakura period by the sponsoring of the Zen temples, the Five Mountains of Kyōto and the Five Mountains of Kamakura. By maintaining our sponsorship of such institutions, we can use them to help stabilize our rule.

bodaiji.d: Since antiquity, our people have venerated our ancestors. The most influential of our rulers erect entire temples, where they will be entombed and then worshiped after death, and where their deeds and words will be remembered for all time.

kagura.d: Originally sacred ritual dances performed in front of the court by the miko, the shrine maidens, the Kagura also inspired the performance of popular ritual dances all around Japan. These dances have evolved into a myriad of forms, but all of them preserving the tradition and ritual they come from.

obon.d: One of the most important festivals in our culture, Obon is the time to honor the dead, and our ancestors in particular. During the celebrations, offerings of food and ritual dances are performed. People also light fires and lanterns to guide the souls of the dead back home for the celebrations, and once again back to the land of the dead.

neo_confucianism.d: Confucianism has a millenary history, and Neo-Confucianism has already existed in Japan for centuries. However, active state involvement and support of the faith will strengthen our authority.

danka_system.d: For centuries, households in Japan have had close relationships with local Buddhist temples, giving them financial patronage in exchange for the temples taking care of their spiritual needs. Formally enforcing this system will keep our people devoted to the faith, and secure the vital role our religion plays in society.

b: Cost of Cleansing Ritual Religious Action: -10%
harae.d: In our faith, the practice of Harae, or ritual purification, is key to removing all tsumi, sins, and kegare, spiritual uncleanness. Mandating that our population performs the Harae rituals properly and frequently ensures that our country remains spiritually pure.

jisha_bugyou.d: The administrator and supervisor of all the temples and shrines, the Jisha-Bugyō also oversees the activities these religious institutions perform, making sure that their interests align with those of the government.

kokugaku.d: Almost since its inception as a country, Japan and Shintō have been influenced by foreign ideas coming from China and Buddhism. A new movement is taking root, claiming that our own national spirit is naturally pure, and that our society must be cleansed of any foreign influences.

home_shrines.d: Ritual and religious practice have been traditionally relegated to shrines and temples. However, more and more of our people are placing in their homes both local family shrines, called kamidana, to venerate the Kami, and butsudan as Buddhist altars for their ancestors.

fukko_shinto.d: As people are rejecting foreign influence in our culture, they are also starting to reject the teachings of Buddhist and Confucianism interfering in our faith. Given this emerging demand for doctrinal purity, a formal revitalization of Shintō might be wise.

confucian_school_advance.d: These learning institutions focus their efforts in the education and training of government officials in the Confucian ideals.

confucian_academy_advance.d: Private learning schools for elite-class students who are learning the Confucian teachings and ideals to pass the national service examinations.

fortress_church_advance.d: The Fortress Church is a building with a dual purpose. It serves its community as a normal church with all its religious functions, but is also used in case of sieges as a defensive building.

unlock_baochuan.d: The Bǎochuán is a large vessel designed to transport goods and protect the trade on sea. They are capable of long distance voyages, bringing treasure and tribute from far away shores to our lands.

italian_galleass.d: The galleass was an adaptation of the large merchant galley to counter the increasing use of man-of-war. Larger than the galley, the galleass had about 32 oar pairs, each oar manned by up to five men. As an answer to the men-of-war's armament and higher sides, the galleass had forecastles and aftcastles and gun decks above the rowers. This extra weight meant that they also had to rely more on sails, and were slower and less maneuverable compared to galleys. Like the galley, the galleass went out of regular use with the introduction of more advanced oceangoing men-of-war, but remained useful in shallow waters until the 18th century.

unlock_cakradonya.d: A large and heavily armed ship, propelled by oars and two or even three sails, the Cakradonya will dominate the seas of Indonesia.

unlock_sekibune.d: Build from cider or fir wood, the Sekibune sacrifices a sturdy hull for increased speed and maneuverability.

unlock_atakebune.d: Serving as larger variants of the Sekibune ships, the Atakebune is able to staff a larger crew than before. Sometimes equipped with iron or copper plates mounted on the hull, they improve on the survivability of the previous types as well.

unlock_long_fada.d: The ships of Ireland and the Highlands are most capable at projecting our presence over our coastal possessions, protecting merchant vessels and at the same time, serving as adequate warships in times of need.

unlock_long_fada_2.d: An improved Long Fada, the Great Long Fada is a larger vessel with more oars and a bigger crew, able to carry out longer voyages and project more power over the seas.

uc_bey_advance.d: The Uç Bey is an Army Based Country that serves as a frontier lord under strong Turkic leadership. Tasked with defending borders, leading raids, and expanding territories, these semi-autonomous leaders command loyal Ġuzāt warriors driven by religious fervor, plunder, and land grants, making them crucial to frontier stability and expansion. They can only be created through the Create Uç Bey Action, and they get the Uç Bey Government Reform and always allow army levies, while having greatly reduced payment obligations compared to a normal Vassal but costing increased Diplomatic Capacity and giving their overlord more monthly towards decentralization. A Uç Bey keeps its own Religion, which its Overlord cannot convert or enforce.

fratricide_succesion_advance.d: It is a type of Succession Law of a Monarchy in which the new Ruler ascends to the throne once he has demonstrated that his fortune is superior to the fortunes of his rivals, usually through the elimination of each one of them.

algerian_hilali_settlement.d: The Banū Hilāl and Banū Sulaym Arab clans push west out of Egypt across generations, settling among the Sanhaja and Zenata Berbers of the central Maghreb and imposing their dialect and tribal genealogies on the absorbed populations. Our shayḵs adopt the Hilāli kinship structures, our valleys are partitioned by negotiated pasture-and-village arrangements, and the older Berber tongues retreat into a substratum preserved only in pasture-songs and place-names. This Arab-Berber synthesis gives the central-Maghrebi Tell a tribal-genealogical foundation that distinguishes our culture from the more inland zenati and kabyle highland identities.

algerian_tell_wheatlands.d: The Tell-region plains of the Mitidja, the Chelif valley, the Soummam, and the rolling country south of Constantine produce the wheat harvests that feed our coastal cities and supply the central treasury through state-licensed export. Our fellahin work the irrigated bottomlands under hereditary land-tenure arrangements, our cooperative threshing yards consolidate the harvest at season's end, and our state-licensed grain warehouses bridge the bad-harvest years that the rainfed Tell occasionally suffers. This wheat-export economy gives our urban polities a reliable revenue base that the more pastoral Maghrebi rivals cannot supply from their territory alone.

algerian_carpet_weaving.d: Our Berber and Arab weavers, from the rug-makers of Kalaa Beni Rashed and the Beni Mizab of the M'zab valley to the urban guilds of Algiers and Constantine, produce the geometric-patterned woolen rugs that the Mediterranean and trans-Saharan markets specifically commission for their distinct Maghrebi character. Our spinners work the wool from the Tell flocks, our dyers compound the indigo, madder, and henna into the bold reds and blues that define the regional aesthetic, and our knot-weavers execute patterns passed down through generations of master-apprentice transmission. This Algerian carpet tradition gives our urban guilds an export specialization that no other Maghrebi rug-weaving region can match for pattern diversity and color-fastness.

algerian_makhzen_tribes.d: Our state-allied tribes, the Banū Hilāl-descended Bedouin confederations that historically aligned themselves with whichever Algerian polity could secure their pasture-rights and grain-supply, provide the light cavalry of our central forces and the inter-tribal contact-network that no purely-urban administration could replicate. Our paramount-shayḵs hold formal court titles, our annual stipends bind tribal contingents to the state, and our marriage-alliances with notable tribal families secure recruiting catchments across the Tell. This makhzen-tribal system gives our military a cavalry pool and a frontier-tribal cohesion that the more centralized Maghrebi rivals lack.

algerian_qadiriyya_expansion.d: The Qādiriyya tariqa, the older of our two great Sufi brotherhoods, traced through the Baghdadi line back to 'Abd al-Qādir al-Jīlānī, anchors the rural religious-judicial authority across the Tell and the steppe-frontier. Our zawiyas train Quranic scholars in remote village-mosques, our shayḵs mediate the inter-tribal disputes that no urban qadi could settle by force of law alone, and our lodges provide the loyalty-oath networks that bind frontier tribes to their patron brotherhood. This Qādiriyya rural anchorage gives Algerian religious culture a doctrinal-mediation infrastructure that purely-urban judicial systems cannot replicate at scale.

algerian_tijaniyya_birth.d: The Tijāniyya tariqa, founded by Aḥmad at-Tijānī in 'Ayn Māḍī in the central Algerian steppe, emerges as a uniquely Algerian-soil Sufi order with a distinctive silsila-of-light doctrine and a fast-spreading network of branch-zawiyas across the Maghreb. Our founder receives his initiating vision in the Algerian desert, our first sister-lodges open in Fez and Tlemcen as the order spreads westward, and our scholars publish the doctrinal compendia that define the brotherhood's distinctive practices. This Tijāniyya birthright gives our culture an Algerian-origin Sufi order, a claim no other Maghrebi culture can match for the period.

aragonese_montaneses.d: The high Pyrenean valleys around Jaca and Sobrarbe have forged a hardy population of mountain warriors known as the Montañeses, whose long descent from the foothills gave our kingdom its earliest military reputation in the Reconquista. Trained from youth to fight on broken ground and accustomed to long winter campaigns, our highlanders move faster and strike harder than the lowland levies that have always opposed them. This martial culture gives our armies a core of mobile infantry whose endurance shapes every campaign we undertake.

aragonese_pyrenean_passes.d: The high passes of the central Pyrenees — Somport, Roncesvalles, and the lower seasonal trails — funnel every wagon-load of Béarnais wool, Gascon wine, and Languedocian cloth that crosses into our markets, and our toll-stations at Jaca and Canfranc have collected the Crown's share of that flow since the eleventh century. By improving the roads, garrisoning the watchtowers, and standardizing customs assessments along these Caminos Reales, we transform an accident of geography into a commercial monopoly. This control over the Pyrenean transit routes draws merchants from both sides of the mountains to our fairs and keeps the Crown's treasury supplied with reliable transit fees.

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

aragonese_castillos_frontera.d: The frontier between our kingdom and al-'Andalus is studded with Castillos de la Frontera — Loarre, Monzón, Albarracín, and dozens of lesser keeps perched on every defensible ridge. Each fortress is maintained at the expense of the local commune, with the Crown contributing only walls and a captain, producing a defensive network that no invader can easily breach without costly siegework. This system makes our territory disproportionately expensive to invade and bleeds any attacking force long before our field armies need to give battle.

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

aragonese_salinas_reales.d: Our Crown has long claimed monopoly over the salt-producing valleys of Naval, Sallent, and Remolinos, contracting their extraction to royal officers who answer directly to the treasury. The Salinas Reales provide a steady income that supplements the unpredictable agrarian taxes and gives our state the liquid capital to weather lean harvests. This mineral revenue makes our government uniquely solvent and frees us from constant dependence on the Cortes for emergency funds.

aragonese_sociedad_economica.d: The Real Sociedad Económica Aragonesa de Amigos del País, founded in Zaragoza, gathers our enlightened citizens — clergy, nobles, and burghers alike — to debate agricultural improvement, manufacturing, and commercial reform. Its meetings spread practical knowledge through pamphlets, prize competitions, and direct correspondence with reformers across Europe. This network of patriotic improvers raises the productivity of every sector its members touch and transforms our province into one of Iberia's quietest engines of modernization.

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

aragonese_foralism.d: After several decrees stripped our kingdom of its medieval institutions, a persistent movement of jurists, historians, and provincial nobles have worked to preserve the memory and practical force of the lost fueros. The Foralist cause draws on regional identity to negotiate with the central government for restored privileges, regional courts, and recognition of distinct legal customs. This sustained political pressure prevents Madrid from treating our province as a uniform administrative unit and gives our institutions a resilience that outlives every reorganization the Bourbons attempt.

bos_cultural_customs.d: Our people practice unique customs that transcend religious differences. The construction of stećci, elaborately decorated tombstones, is a tradition shared by all of us, regardless of faith. These distinctive monuments mark our lands as uniquely Bosnian.

bos_katun_communities.d: Parts of our population are organized into self-governing, pastoralist communities. Instead of bending them to a central government's will, we should cooperate with them, and in doing so try to extract more resources from our more remote areas.

bos_defiant_terrain.d: Bosnia is a land of forested hills and mountains, cut through by river valleys. This terrain lends itself naturally to delaying and tiring invading armies, and we should use this to our advantage. Engaging our enemy only when it benefits us and letting the hostile terrain itself claim both their supplies and troops will preserve our strength.

bosnian_bosancica.d: The Bosnian people have unified around Bosančica, a unique, cursive Cyrillic script used for everything from diplomatic treaties to private merchant ledgers. This national script serves as a powerful cultural gatekeeper; it is difficult for foreigners to read but universal among the Bosnian literate class, regardless of their specific confession. By maintaining this distinct script, the people ensure that their legal and historical records remain a 'closed book' to imperial administrators, preserving the secret nuances of Bosnian property law and lineage in a format that reinforces their unique Slavic heritage.

bosnian_people_from_the_hills.d: The geography of the Bosnian heartland is a vertical maze of limestone ridges and valleys that defy conventional mapping. Our people have adapted to this logic, mastering the secrets of the subterranean cavern networks and the logistics of the mule-train.

bosnian_susjedsvto_of_bosnia.d: The ancient cultural concept of Susjedstvo — the sacred social obligation to protect and honor one's neighbor — has evolved into a sophisticated civic philosophy that transcends religious divides. In the face of external pressures, this unwritten code mandates that a neighbor's safety and property are as sacred as one's own. This practice prevents the 'Divide and Rule' tactics often used by foreign powers to incite internal strife. By prioritizing local solidarity and the 'Law of the Neighborhood', we maintain a level of social harmony and internal stability that allows the nation to present a single, unbreakable front against any attempt to dismantle our shared homeland.

bulgarian_orthodox_patriarchate.d: The restoration of the Bulgarian Patriarchate in 1235, confirmed by the Council of Lampsacus, established Tarnovo as a sovereign spiritual rival to both Constantinople and Rome. By the 14th century, the Patriarchate functioned as the ideological spine of the Asen and Shishman dynasties, utilizing its autocephalous status to provide divine legitimacy that transcended the political fragmentation of the Bulgarian lands. From its seat on Tsarevets Hill, the Church managed an expansive administrative network of eparchies and monasteries, such as the Zograf Monastery on Mount Athos, which served as repositories for the Bulgarian recension of Church Slavonic.

reformation_of_the_bulgarian_patriarchat.d: The spiritual heart of the Bulgarian world will undergo a rigorous and profound transformation under the iron-willed guidance of our Patriarch. Recognizing that the survival of the nation depends upon the purity of its faith and the precision of its holy texts, the Patriarchate will initiate a sweeping linguistic and liturgical reform centered at the Holy Trinity Monastery of Tarnovo. By purging the Church Slavonic manuscripts of centuries of scribal errors and corrupt localisms, we will establish a new, standardized orthography that will become the gold standard for the entire Orthodox Slavic world, from the Danube to the Volga.

bulgarian_the_danubian_river_merchants.d: Leveraging their position as the gatekeepers of the Lower Danube, Bulgarian merchant families have established a sophisticated trade network connecting the Black Sea to Central Europe. By utilizing shallow-draft barges and fortified river ports, they have managed to bypass the expensive and dangerous overland routes, controlling the flow of salt, grain, and timber across the Balkans. This riverine expertise has turned the Danube into a Bulgarian artery of wealth, funding the rise of a new urban elite that we can tax so they keep their privileges.

fortress_of_the_balkans.d: We have recognized that spiritual purity alone cannot halt the encroaching craze of the world. To survive, the state has pivoted toward a doctrine of total territorial fortification, transforming the Balkan Mountains into an impassable granite wall. By reinforcing our lands with tiered stone redoubts and permanent garrisons, the nation has created a strategic depth that forces any invader into a lethal war of attrition. This policy ensures that the Bulgarian heartland remains a sanctuary of Orthodox stability, where the flame of our people's heart is shielded behind a ring of iron and stone that no storm can easily douse.

bulgarian_the_bulgarian_cloth_industry.d: The Bulgarian towns will be transformed into the industrial heartland of the peninsula through the specialized production of Aba (a durable, thick woolen cloth) and Gaitan (decorative braid). By organizing the local weavers and shepherds into powerful, self-governing guilds, the Bulgarian merchants will be able to secure massive state contracts for the outfitting of the regional armies and the growing urban middle classes of the Mediterranean. This economic surge creates a merchant aristocracy that will signal the transition of the Bulgarian people from a rural peasantry to a sophisticated, proto-industrial society with the financial power to dictate terms to their neighbors.

bulgarian_the_bulgarian_national_awakeni.d: Driven by the writings of monks like Paisius of Hilendar, the Bulgarian people have rediscovered their imperial history and linguistic pride, sparking a massive educational and political rebirth. This movement has moved beyond local grievances to demand a centralized, modern state that can take its place among the great powers of Europe. The result is a highly motivated and literate populace, ready to serve in a modern bureaucracy or a national army, fueled by the conviction that the glory of the Tsars is not a memory, but a future.

cas_repoblaciones.d: The Repoblación is our standing policy of resettling territories reconquered from Moorish rule, granting fueros and tax exemptions to draw colonists southward. Under kings like Alfonso VI and Ferdinand III, vast tracts of Toledo, La Mancha, and Andalusia have been claimed by frontier councils of free settlers who hold their lands directly from the Crown. This systematic colonization turns conquest into permanence, fixing Castilian populations on every frontier and preventing the territorial reversal that ended earlier reconquest waves.

cas_castilian_navy.d: With our peninsular coastline divided between the rough Cantabrian Sea and the Atlantic approaches, our navy has long been a pillar of state survival, commanded by the office of Almirante Mayor de Castilla. From Santander to Sevilla, our shipyards have fielded fleets that outmatched English and Hanseatic squadrons throughout the late medieval Cantabrian wars, and admirals like Pero Niño have raided as far as the Thames. This naval institution gives us the deep-water capacity that the coming age of oceanic empire will demand.

cas_masters_of_the_orders.d: With the Reconquista complete, the three great Castilian military orders — Santiago, Calatrava, and Alcántara — possess vast estates and private armies but no remaining enemies to fight. The Catholic Monarchs have begun a quiet annexation, by which the Crown will assume the Grand Mastership of each order, transferring their lands, encomiendas, and bullion under royal control. This absorption eliminates the last great rivals to royal power within Castile and adds an unmatched military-religious infrastructure to the permanent resources of the Crown.

cas_marine_infantry.d: Emperor Charles V created the Compañías Viejas del Mar de Nápoles, the world's first standing marine infantry corps, raised to crew the tercios serving aboard the galleys of the Mediterranean. These Infantes de Marina are trained for the close-quarters chaos of boarding actions and for garrisoning fortified coastal outposts from Oran to Manila. This permanent assault arm multiplies the value of every flagship and secures the coastal links of an empire stretching across two oceans.

cas_pasos.d: The Pasos of Holy Week — massive sculpted scenes of the Passion carried in procession through our streets — have become the defining popular art of the Castilian Baroque. Sculptors such as Juan de Juni in Valladolid and Gregorio Fernández, working in polychrome wood, have raised the form to its peak in the early seventeenth century, producing figures so anatomically vivid that crowds weep at their passage. This processional culture binds the urban populace, the parish brotherhoods, and the Crown in a shared devotional spectacle that no Protestant nation can match.

cas_canal_de_castilla.d: Begun under the patronage of the Marquis of Ensenada, the Canal de Castilla cuts north from the Tierra de Campos through Palencia and Valladolid toward the Cantabrian ports. Its locks, aqueducts, and bridges allow the wheat surplus of the Meseta to reach Santander cheaply enough to compete with Baltic grain on European markets. This single feat of engineering transforms Old Castile from a landlocked breadbasket trapped behind the Cordillera into the granary of the Atlantic seaboard.

successors_of_genghis_khan.d: From the days of total conquest to the vast expanses of Genghis Khān's great Empire, our people descend from generations of earthshakers. Our people are the ones destined to author history.

zhongshu_sheng.d: One of the most vital branches of the Three Departments and Six Ministries, the central secretariat is responsible for the drafting and codification of many Imperial reforms and decrees.

lijia_system.d: Under the Lǐ Jiǎ system, we are able to exercise control over our borderlands through the allocation of settled armies. By granting land and agricultural rights to our stationed troops, our borders will be safer and our authority shall be affirmed.

yulin_tuce.d: Tax evasion is a timeless problem that even plagued our ancestors, but we may have found a solution: By compiling registers for districts and provinces, we will keep better track of the taxes owed to the central government by every plot. This taxation is largely determined based on the grain yield of every plot that undergoes survey.

weisuo_system.d: Many would-be conquerors eye our lands with covetous intent. If we are to defend our territory, we must set up a garrison system, aimed at rapidly responding to hostile invasions. Through the recruitment of local troops, our defensive prowess will be supplemented through supplies and more efficient logistics.

grand_coordinators.d: Maintaining control over our territories, policymaking, and military operations is vital for the continuation of our dynasty. Through the creation of Grand Coordinators, a body of high-ranking officials who can coordinate governance across our vast empire, we will succeed in cementing our position through effective stabilization of internal and external matters.

the_censorate.d: Parallel to other institutes within our administration, this branch of our government is in charge of preventing corruption. The censors are tasked with keeping palatial intrigues and malfeasance in check, often seen as the eyes and ears of the Emperor.

the_tea_trade.d: A staple beverage of our society, Tea has come to dominate social gatherings, becoming the choice drink of many. This will undoubtedly lead to not only new varieties being cultivated, but a production boom as well.

reform_the_grand_secretariat.d: Considered the de facto highest institution in our nation, the Grand Secretariat has served our rulers for centuries. Wielding immense influence over administrative affairs, this body of cabinet ministers must undergo a reform to further increase its effectiveness.

woodblock_printing.d: The production of elegant illustrations, artworks, and books using this printing method has captivated our people's attention, and our master printers constantly strive to perfect their techniques. Woodblock printing has become part of our culture and, with recent improvements to and expansion of our literary production, will further elevate our prestige.

green_standard_army.d: The Green Standard Army, a military force mainly composed of ethnic Hàn soldiers, coexists with our Eight Banner armies. Originally formed by surrendered troops and recruited on a voluntary, long-term basis, they attract individuals from socially disadvantaged backgrounds. Used as a police force post-consolidation, they will play a crucial role in local military governance, while Bannermen will be reserved for emergencies and sustained resistance.

junji_chu.d: Also known as the Grand Council, the Jūnjī Chù is tasked with overseeing military affairs. As the most important privy council, it has come to overshadow the Grand Secretariat that held sway over previous dynasties. Despite its crucial role, this council will retain an informal nature within the inner court, with its members holding other official roles besides their councilorship.

req: March to the Sound of Guns
ten_great_campaigns.d: The Ten Great Campaigns are aimed at expanding our influence both inside and outside our borders. To achieve that, we will draft a huge army to crush any resistance that we might find in our way. We shall choke the life out of any rebellion before it has the chance to raise its head, and our glory will be eternal.

cir_tribal_elections.d: We will elect a nominal leader of our people, who will act as our representative but will not meddle with the oversight of local lords.

cir_mercenary_employment.d: Our lands have again and again been raided by foreign powers, and our people enslaved. Some of these slaves, used as soldiers, have advanced in their new lives, accumulating power and wealth of their own. With some convincing, we could convince them to return to our lands, and protect it from future invasions.

cir_horsemen_of_the_steppe.d: Our position at the edge of the steppes has resulted in multiple mounted invasions of our homelands. If we want to ensure our independence, we will need to raise a great host ourselves, and expand our influence over the steppes, securing our heartland.

cir_city_and_fortress.d: Our settlements lie unprotected, and are easy prey to any invader. As these settlements grow, however, we can directly incorporate the hilly terrain into our defensive lines, enhancing their protection. If necessary, we can even create the elevated terrain required ourselves.

cir_grand_prince_of_circassia.d: To unify our people, we shall elect the greatest of our lords as the Grand Prince, who will serve as an inspiring leader for our troops.

cir_multireligious_society.d: Our lands are frequented by many Catholic, Muslim, and Orthodox people, who frequently engage in trade with our population. We should foster a collective tolerance between all our subjects, to promote peace and stability.

croatian_the_glagolitic_lithurgy.d: Our culture is defined by the unique privilege of the Glagolitic liturgy — the only place in the Catholic world where the Mass is sung in the native Slavic tongue. This tradition bridges the gap between the Latin cities and the Slavic heartland, creating a unified cultural identity. By preserving this ancient script, our people maintain a secret cultural language that reinforces their distinctiveness, providing a sense of national pride that resists assimilation by both the Italian and Germanic cultural spheres.

cro_influx_of_foreign_knowledge.d: The coastal cities have become vibrant centers of the Renaissance, where scholars and artists blend classical Italian influences with a distinct Slavic sensibility. This intellectual movement produces great thinkers who contribute to European science, poetry, and philosophy, proving that Croatian culture is at the forefront of the modern era. The patronage of wealthy merchant families allows for the construction of magnificent cathedrals and palaces, turning our coast into a beacon of high culture that attracts the finest minds of the age.

cro_trade_posts.d: The cultural soul of Croatia has reached a literary peak with works like Judita by Marko Marulić, the 'Father of Croatian Literature'. By using biblical allegory to describe the contemporary defense of our lands, Marulić has provided the nation with a high-culture blueprint for survival. This literature creates a bridge between the Renaissance urbanite and the frontier soldier, unifying all classes under a shared heroic mission and ensuring the preservation of the Croatian tongue as a language of high art and theological debate.

croatian_the_peasants_revolts.d: The crushing weight of feudal obligations in the face of constant war caused peasant revolts in the past. The peasantry rose not against us, but against the 'unjust' nobility who failed to protect them while demanding excessive tithes. Though these revolts have been usually brutally suppressed, they have left a lasting legacy of social consciousness and have transformed the relationship between the classes, forcing the state to eventually moderate its tax demands to maintain internal stability.

croatian_the_cravats.d: During these convulsed years, the world has taken notice of the distinct, elite light-cavalry regiments from the Croatian Military. Beyond their legendary mobility and ferocity, these horsemen have introduced a unique sartorial innovation: a functional, knotted cloth worn around the neck to secure their shirt collars and provide protection from the chafing of breastplates. This cravat — a name derived from the French mispronunciation of Croate — has rapidly transcended the battlefield to become the height of Parisian and European fashion. By transforming a rugged military necessity into a hallmark of fashionable dressing, our culture has achieved a subtle but permanent victory. This sartorial dominance ensures that the image of the Croatian officer is one of both tactical lethality and unparalleled gallantry.

croatian_the_illyrian_movement.d: Over the last few years, our nation has witnessed the explosion of the Illyrian Movement, a cultural and political revolution that seeks to unify all Croats under a single banner. This movement effectively aims to unify the disparate regions of our nation into a single, cohesive political and cultural national body. By standardizing the grammar and orthography, we will transform our medieval nation into a modern one, ensuring that the Croatian name, language, and statehood will never again be forgotten or suppressed.

unlock_early_longbowmen_advance.d: The powerful martial longbow, originally deployed with great impact against armored English knights in the Welsh valleys, has been adopted into the military doctrine on either side of the border.

unlock_longbowmen_advance.d: The Longbowmen excel not only due to their powerful warbow but also their years of training on the archery fields.

unlock_late_longbowmen_advance.d: Small innovations in equipment and organization result in continuous devastating volleys that shatter all but the most heavily armored formations.

gra_razzias.d: The ḡazwa — a fast mounted raid into Christian territory for cattle, captives, and plunder — has been the lifeblood of the frontier emirates since the Umayyad century. Our raiders cross the Sierras at night in companies of fifty to two hundred, sweep through poorly garrisoned vegas, and retire before the Castilian mesnadas can muster a response. This raiding economy keeps the Christian frontier impoverished and dependent on our terms, while drawing slaves, livestock, and tribute into Granada.

gra_nasrid_art.d: The artisans of al-'Andalus have inherited a millennium of Umayyad and Almohad refinement in stucco, tilework, and muqarnas vaulting. Their works at the Alhambra and the Madrasa Yūsufiyya of Yūsuf I draw masters from Fez and Cairo to study the Granadan style, and our pottery, silks, and inlaid weapons command premium prices across the Mediterranean. This sustained craft tradition gives us a luxury-goods economy that funds the state even as our political territory contracts.

gra_expand_qanahs.d: The Qanāh — the buried gravity-fed aqueduct inherited from Persia through the Umayyad caliphs — turns the dry plains of the Vega into orchards and silk-mulberry groves. We extend the network from the Sierra Nevada snowmelt down through the Albaicín, Almuñécar, and Almería, with water rights enforced by the ancient Tribunal de las Aguas. This hydraulic infrastructure produces yields per acre that the Christian kingdoms north of the Sierra Morena cannot match, sustaining a population density unique to al-'Andalus.

gra_expand_the_frontier.d: For two centuries the Nasrid territory has contracted under the pressure of the Castilian advance, but our recent consolidation of the Alpujarras and the coastal sierras has finally produced a defensible heartland. We now possess the manpower, fortifications, and treasury to push north into Jaén and east into Murcia, reversing the strategic pattern set since Ferdinand III took Córdoba in 1236. This recovery of the frontier transforms us from a besieged remnant into an offensive power capable of reclaiming the lost cities of al-'Andalus.

gra_modernized_economy.d: The old Andalusi economy of silk, sugar, and almond exports must adapt to a Mediterranean dominated by Genoese banks, Atlantic competition, and the new global trade routes. We will reform the muḥtasib market regulations, invest in modern textile workshops at Málaga and Almería, and replant the sugar plantations of the Costa Tropical along Italian and Madeiran technical lines. This economic modernization keeps us competitive against Christian neighbors who otherwise enjoy unrestricted access to the new Atlantic silver and spice trades.

b: Damage Done versus Heathens in Battle: +10%
gra_ghazawat.d: In an age when monarchies measure themselves by enlightened ministers and standing armies, our state declares each campaign a Ḡazawāt — a sanctified war binding ruler and subject in a single religious-military project.
