The 'ulamā preach mobilization in every Friday sermon, and the militias of the Albaicín, Antequera, and Loja drill weekly under emiral charters that promise paradise to those who fall on the frontier. This holy-war ethos gives Granada a level of military mobilization and morale that the secular monarchies of Europe simply cannot match.

hun_composite_light_cavalry.d: Made up of horse archers as well as swift horsemen, our light cavalry is the backbone of our military force. Our mounted forces have shown their mettle time and time again, and will inevitably lead our forces to glory once more.

hun_multi_culturalism.d: The Carpathian Basin is home to more than just Hungarian people. Slovak, Ruthenian,Cuman, and Carpathian German people, among many other different minorities, call our realm their home. Given this diversity, it is only natural that our government proficiently absorbs and adopts these different cultures into our state.

hun_reformed_coinage.d: To pay for our new professional army, we will need a steady stream of revenue. Reforming the coinage to standardize weights will make this much easier, because we shall know exactly how much people need to pay.

hun_hungarian_hussars.d: Drawing inspiration from the storied legacy of King Matthias I Corvinus' cavalry, this idea introduces the 'Royal Hussar Regiments,' granting a formidable edge to Hungary's light cavalry forces. With their swift and fearless charges, these regiments are a symbol of Hungarian martial prowess, proving indispensable on the battlefields of Europe.

hun_hungarian_reformation.d: The ideas of the Reformation spread through Europe like wildfire, and as such were bound to find their way to our lands eventually. Our realm has been threatened by outside powers for long enough. By joining the Reformation and abandoning the duty of following the Pope like a lapdog, we can break at least one of the shackles oppressing us!

hun_the_catholic_shield.d: The ideas of the Reformation spread through Europe like wildfire, and as such were bound to find their way to our lands eventually. Yet, the hearts of the faithful remain strong. God and His loyal servants will withstand this heretical madness.

hun_realm_of_many_religions.d: The ideas of the Reformation spread through Europe like wildfire, and as such were bound to find their way to our lands eventually. Alas, the Reformation has split families apart, made former friends into enemies, and threatened the very stability of many nations. However, our realm knows better than to fall victim to this theological quarreling. We are a people and a realm of many religions, after all.

hun_revolutionized_military_tactics.d: As military technology advances, so do battlefield tactics. It is imperative to the survival of our state that we keep pace with the ever-evolving nature of land warfare.

b: Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities: +0.5
hun_strengthened_towns.d: Towns are key factors in producing the wealth Hungary needs to grow and prosper. If we ensure the operations of our townships are protected from the power-hungry machinations of the nobility, they will continue to bring in trade, which we can tax.

tambo_advance.d: The Tambo is a supply depot of the Incas. The purpose of the Tambo varies significantly depending on the size of the structure. Smaller tambos serve as road stops for passing travelers while larger ones can even serve as an office for the province's administration.

ira_sasanian_heritage.d: Before the Islamic Conquest of Persia, the region was home to the Sasanian Empire, which once ruled from Caucasia in the West to the Kirthar Range in the East. Many of its great cultural accomplishments have shaped our cultural and artistic identity.

ira_islamized_persia.d: The Islamization of Persia has been a lengthy process. It is not yet completely finished, but our religion has still become one of the major pillars of our national identity. Many of our ancient traditions have been combined with the teachings of Islam, and now make up our current core culture.

ira_shahnameh.d: The Šāhnāme - the Book of Kings - is an epic poem, and a national treasure of the Farsi people. Describing the historical and mythical past of the empires which once occupied Greater Persia, its stories contribute to the Farsi culture in uncountable dimensions.

ira_persian_plateau.d: The great plateau at the heart of our realm does not result in a weakness for us but instead turns into our strength. As the origin of great empires, our people have for countless generations crossed its great plains and the rugged mountain ranges surrounding it, like the Zagros or the Alborz. The same terrain that exhausts foreign armies is where our soldiers, our merchants, and our administrators thrive. We will use this familiarity to move across our lands and govern them with an ease that no outsider can match.

ira_restoration_of_cities.d: The Mongol invasion of Persia was catastrophic for the entire region. Population centers of magnificent size were reduced to mere rubble. But it is finally time to rebuild what was once destroyed, and restore the awe-inspiring empire of Persia.

ira_improved_silk_road.d: A system of upgrades to roads and bridges, a system of guards to protect the roads — for a small fee — and a chain of Caravanserai for rest and refreshment. All these improvements will help the merchants as they traverse the Silk Road, and also provide revenue for the state.

ira_promotion_of_irrigation.d: As a consequence of the Mongol invasion of the past, Persia is somewhat depopulated compared to the earlier empires which claimed these lands as their own. Promoting the practice of irrigation should help our people develop the agriculture needed to boost the local population and help us recover from the death toll of past conflicts.

ira_persian_horses.d: Horses play a fundamental role in our society. Many of our people are raised alongside their steeds, which is reflected in both the care our horse breeders take and the durability of our cavalry.

ira_spread_of_persian_influence.d: Persian is an ancient language with a history longer than the lifespan of many empires. Even the Muslim conquest could not diminish the core of the Persian identity, and many other states try to imitate our culture.

ira_persian_rug_production.d: Persia has long been famous for its beautiful carpets and rugs. However, when the Mongols devastated the empire, much of this cultural heritage was lost. For Persia to fully recover its tumbled glory, we must regain our economic strength, and restoring this legendary ancient industry is the first step in that direction.

lor_mining_tradition.d: Our lands are rich in ore and coal. Extracting these resources could make us a rich country and lay the groundwork for our grand ambitions.

lor_cultural_diversity.d: Our territory is home to many different peoples and cultures. Establishing a single state to govern this diverse population will not be easy, but we must. Only then will we be worthy successors to the Lorrainian state from which we descend.

lor_three_bishoprics.d: Lorraine is home to many bishops with powerful supporters abroad and within the Church itself. Cooperating with them will be useful when making our voice heard within the broader Church. Having the support of the bishops will also help us to pacify the population more easily.

lor_between_great_powers.d: Our lands were once an important part of Lotharingia, one of the Frankish kingdoms. If we do not want to fall into irrelevance, we will need to secure our diplomatic position and establish lasting alliances.

lor_fortified_cities.d: We occupy vital crossing points on several rivers, which we must defend at all costs if we want to secure our independence. To this effect, we must modernize the large bridge castles of our cities, and construct large citadels at strategic points.

moroccan_sharifian_descent.d: Our dynasty claims direct descent from the Prophet Muḥammad through Ḥasan ibn 'Alī, a sharīfī lineage that the Idrīsid founders carried west of Egypt in the eighth century and that we now invoke as the sacral foundation of our throne. No Berber dynasty (Almoravid, Almohad, Marinid, or Waṭṭāsid) could match the prophetic genealogy that our court genealogists publish, certify, and recite at every bay'a ceremony. This sharifian descent secures the loyalty of the ulema and lifts the standing of our court before every Muslim peer.

moroccan_bay_a.d: The bay'a is the formal oath by which the ulema of Fez, the urban notables, and the tribal qā'ids pledge allegiance to a newly-acclaimed sultan, a covenant renewed at each succession and at every great political crisis. The act binds rulers and subjects in mutual obligation: the sultan undertakes to defend the faith and the customary law, while the assembled representatives undertake to support the state with their levies and their tax compliance. This consent-based legitimacy stabilizes our succession and dampens the centrifugal pressures that the absence of consultation would otherwise unleash.

moroccan_andalusi_refuge.d: Successive waves of Andalusi exiles settle in the cities of our coast: Tetouan rebuilt by the Manẓarī family, the Andalusi quarter of Fez, the Hornachero corsair colony at Salé, and the silk-weavers of Chefchaouen. They bring with them the gunpowder craftsmanship, banking expertise, urban architecture, and Andalusi-style cuisine of their lost peninsula, knowledge our older merchant houses immediately absorb. This refugee influx revitalizes our cities and gives our crown a class of skilled burghers whose loyalty is bound to the realm that gave them sanctuary.

atlantic_trade_routes.d: The Portuguese and Castilian rounding of Cape Bojador has opened a new Atlantic shipping system that runs along our entire coastline, from Tangier through Salé and Larache down to Mogador and Agadir. We host European factors at the funduq an-Naṣārā in our Atlantic ports, take customs duties on every vessel that calls for water or repair, and re-export goods inland to the Saharan caravan markets. This Atlantic-facing economy gives our state a permanent commercial advantage over the wholly-Mediterranean Maghrebi states to our east.

moroccan_malhun_poetry.d: Our urban poets, the shuyūkh al-malḥūn of Fez, Meknes, Marrakesh, and Salé, compose and perform the sung-poetry tradition that distinguishes Moroccan-Arabic culture from every other Arab poetic school. The qṣīda and grīḥa forms set vernacular Darija verse to the rhythmic patterns of Andalusi-Maghrebi music, treating themes of love, satire, mysticism, and dynastic politics in a register accessible to every urban household. This popular literary tradition spreads across our cities and oasis caravans alike, giving our peasants and burghers a cultural medium that sustains the prestige of Moroccan-Arabic identity long after individual rulers fade from memory.

moroccan_nahda_maghribiyya.d: Our Moroccan branch of the Nahḍa gathers in the Salafiyya circles of Fez around 'Allāl al-Fāsī and Abū Shu'ayb al-Dukkālī, in the Tangier-based Arabic press of Lisān al-Maghrib, and in the Tetouan–Fez bilingual periodicals that bring European thought into the western-Maghrebi conversation. We recover the medieval manuscripts of Ibn Khaldūn, al-Maqqarī, and the Marinid chroniclers from foreign libraries, reissue them in critical editions, and standardize Moroccan classical Arabic against the centralizing pressures of foreign administrative languages in our schools and registries. This intellectual renewal binds the scattered Moroccan elite into a shared modern identity that no centralizing foreign administration can easily fragment.

nav_transatlantic_whaling.d: For four centuries the fishermen of San Sebastián, Bermeo, and Lekeitio have hunted the Biscay right whale in the Cantabrian Sea, perfecting the harpoon, the try-pot, and the open-boat pursuit. Pressed by overhunting close to home, our crews now sail to Newfoundland and the Strait of Belle Isle, building seasonal txalupa try-works at Red Bay and trading whale oil to England and the Hanseatic League. This long-range whaling industry gives the Basque coast a permanent Atlantic presence decades before any other European fleet ventures regularly into North American waters.

nav_fearless_seamen.d: The Basque coast offers little arable land between the Pyrenees and the sea, and our coastal communities have long looked to the Bay of Biscay for their livelihood through fishing, trade, and piloting. Sailors from Bilbao, Pasaia, and Bayonne crew the merchant fleets of half of Europe — Juan de la Cosa pilots Columbus's Santa María, Juan Sebastián Elcano completes the first global circumnavigation, and Andrés de Urdaneta charts the Pacific return route from Manila to Acapulco. This concentration of navigational talent makes the Basque-speaking ports the indispensable training grounds of Iberian seamanship.

nav_people_of_the_sea.d: From the ports of Bilbao, Pasaia, and San Sebastián, Basque-speaking crews fill the lower decks of every great Iberian voyage of discovery in proportions far beyond what our small population would suggest. Our pilots draft the first charts of the Newfoundland banks, our boatswains rig the Manila galleons, and our gunners man the heavy ships of the Spanish armadas in disproportionate numbers. This unmatched maritime expertise gives any state that holds the Basque ports a recruiting pool for blue-water navies that landlocked monarchies cannot replicate.

nav_an_industrious_folk.d: The mountain valleys of Bizkaia and Gipuzkoa hold the richest iron deposits in western Europe, worked since Roman times in small water-powered forges called ferrerías. Our smiths produce a Biscayan steel of such hardness that the swords of Toledo, the harquebuses of the Tercios, and the anchors of every Spanish galleon depend on Basque ironmasters. This vertically integrated mining, smelting, and forging economy gives the Basque country an industrial weight out of all proportion to its population.

nav_shipyards_ironworks.d: The shipyards of Pasaia, Orio, and Mutriku and the ironworks of the Deba and Cadagua river valleys form a single integrated industrial belt sustained for centuries by Pyrenean charcoal and Vizcayan iron ore. We modernize the forges with Walloon and Swedish hammer techniques, lay down keels on Dutch designs at the Real Astillero of Pasaia, and contract Manuel de Cosío to design the new fleets of three-deckers for the Crown. This industrial complex remains the only place in Iberia capable of producing first-rate ships of the line from raw ore to launch within its own region.

nav_royal_basque_society.d: The Real Sociedad Bascongada de los Amigos del País, founded at Bergara by the Count of Peñaflorida and a circle of Basque nobles, is the first modern learned society on the Iberian Peninsula. Its Seminario Patriótico at Bergara teaches modern chemistry, mathematics, and economics to the sons of the regional gentry, and it produces Fausto and Juan José Elhuyar who isolate tungsten for the first time in history. This learned institution gives the Basque provinces a scientific and economic vanguard role in the wider Enlightenment of the Spanish monarchy.

netherlandish_protoindustry.d: For a long time, our land has been home to bustling towns and cities with a higher concentration of craftsmen than our neighbors. This focus has made us a highly productive nation.

frisian_trading_traditions.d: Long before the counties south of us developed their own routes, our ancestors dominated coastal trade in Europe, from the Baltic to Biscay. We must revive this ancient maritime expertise to reclaim our rightful position.

a_dynamic_society.d: Our lands are a haven for the bold. Those looking to better their lives will find opportunity here, and we will in turn capitalize on the talents of these ambitious individuals to strengthen our nation.

frisian_resisting_invader.d: Surrounded as we are by enemies, our people are accustomed to aggressively defending their lands, fighting so fiercely that many would-be invaders turn tail and never return. Those who cannot escape us can take comfort in the thought that their blood shall nurture the Frisia soil.

an_early_urbanization.d: The Low Countries have traditionally had a high rate of urbanization, which has allowed us to achieve power beyond what most might expect. We should accelerate this trend by creating a robust network of prosperous settlements that can help us create a wealthier future.

frisian_legend_grutte_pier.d: There are stories in our lands about a pirate who was seven feet tall and strong as an ox. These tales inspire many to take to the seas and do what our ancestors did best: loot unguarded coasts.

por_establishment_portuguese_navy.d: In 1317 King Dinis appointed the Genoese merchant Manuel Pessanha as Almirante-Mor of Portugal, charging him to defend the coast against North African corsairs and to build a national fleet from imported expertise. Pessanha brought Genoese pilots, naval architects, and accountancy methods with him, founding the institutional base from which the Portuguese voyages of the next century launched. This royal naval foundation gives Portugal a Mediterranean-grade maritime administration almost two centuries before any Atlantic neighbor builds an equivalent institution.

por_estimulate_rural_areas.d: The plagues and emigration of the fourteenth century have left the Alentejo and Trás-os-Montes underpopulated, with abandoned villages and uncultivated fields draining the kingdom's tax base. We will reissue royal forais to repopulate hamlets, exempt new settlers from manorial dues for a generation, and import Galician and Castilian laborers willing to clear scrubland for sharecrop tenancies. This rural recovery will restore the food-producing heartland to productivity just as Portugal's overseas ventures begin to demand reliable inland provisioning.

por_bombardeiros.d: The Portuguese caravels and naus that round the Cape of Good Hope face Indian Ocean fleets composed of larger but lightly armed vessels. To turn this disparity into a decisive advantage, our shipwrights shall reinforce the upper decks and gun ports of the new naus to mount heavy bronze cannon cast at the Lisbon arsenal under the direction of Bombardeiro-Mor João Anes. This reinforced gun-platform doctrine will give Portuguese fleets the standoff firepower to destroy the Mamlūk navy at Diu and secure the spice route for a century.

por_the_bandeirantes.d: The Bandeirantes — armed expeditionary bands ranging out of São Paulo and São Vicente starting in the late sixteenth century — penetrate the unmapped Brazilian interior in search of indigenous captives, escaped slaves, and rumored mines. Domingos Jorge Velho, Antônio Raposo Tavares, and Fernão Dias Pais Leme all push the Tordesillas line steadily westward through campaigns lasting years, mapping the Mato Grosso and Goiás highlands as they go. This continental-scale colonization extends Portuguese sovereignty far beyond the original treaty line and establishes Brazil's modern continental footprint.

por_colonial_governors.d: The seventeenth-century reform of the colonial administration replaces the patchwork of feudal donatário captaincies with appointed royal governors and viceroys answerable directly to the Conselho Ultramarino in Lisbon. The Viceroy of the Estado da Índia at Goa, the Captain-General of Angola, and the Governor of Brazil at Salvador each command a salaried bureaucracy of Crown officials, magistrates, and treasury inspectors. This unified colonial administration tightens royal control over distant possessions and dramatically increases the proportion of colonial revenue reaching the metropolitan treasury.

por_vinho_porto.d: On the steep terraced slopes of the Douro Valley, the grapes that produce a fortified red wine of unusual longevity have been cultivated since the seventeenth century. Following the Methuen Treaty, English merchants house themselves in Porto, the Real Companhia das Vinhas do Alto Douro is chartered by the Marquis of Pombal, and Vinho do Porto becomes a protected denomination governed by the first formal demarcation of a wine region in history. This regulated luxury export generates a continuous stream of British silver in exchange for Portuguese wine, sustaining the kingdom's positive trade balance through the entire eighteenth century.

sav_savoyard_flexibility.d: Due to our precarious location between greater powers, we must rely on our diplomatic skills for survival. By maintaining diplomatic relations even with our most dangerous foes, we will be able to shift our alliances to ensure the endurance of our country.

scottish_salmon.d: Our rivers and coastlines are rich in salmon. With careful attention and strict legislation, we will be able to harness this resource and shape our local economy towards export of this highly sought-after fish.

scottish_morale.d: Since the start of our war against English tyranny, we have preserved our independence through the valiant efforts of the courageous Scottish people. The memory of brave men like William Wallace will motivate our armies to defend and protect Scottish independence for all time!

scottish_longbowmen.d: Now that our ties to England have been strengthened, we shall incorporate some of their military tactics, refining our units into fearsome forces.

peel_towers_advance.d: Peel Towers were developed to mitigate the dangers of life in our borderlands. They serve as protection against incursions of hostile raiding parties, sheltering both people and valuable livestock, and are a fast way to alert neighboring towns of approaching hostile armies by being a high place to light signal fires.

scottish_highland_tradition.d: The clans of the Highlands have always moved and fought differently from lowland armies. Raised among the glens, lochs, and steep braes of the north, our clansmen are naturally comfortable engaging in terrain that would exhaust and disorient outsiders. This intimate knowledge of the local landscape is passed down from father to son, and no foreign conqueror has ever truly mastered it.

scottish_tenacity.d: War can be a long and tiring affair. If we are to defend our independence, we need to be prepared to endure hard times. Luckily, our people are as tenacious as the land they call their home, and resist foreign invaders to their last breaths.

influx_of_english_nobles.d: Securing peace with our southern neighbor has led to a steady influx of English aristocrats entering our administration. This makes it possible to exert our control over our country more effectively.

scottish_trade_connections.d: Our country is situated at the far edge of Western Europe and is sparse in resources. If we are to thrive economically, we need to invest and expand our trade connections to further regions. The North Sea can connect us to rich markets and business opportunities, provided we learn to harness its potential.

comets.d: We have recently received a rather curious new tome. It is called On the True Significance of Comets against the Vanity of Astrologers, and it is positively filled with vital information on these highly suspicious entities. We have decreed that all in the realm should be aware of its contents.

c.t: Is or was the country Isles (LOI)

modernized_royal_scots_navy.d: Since the Wars of Independence, we have been looking at reinforcing and updating our navy. Previously, we had used feudal obligations to bulk out our fleets with crew and ships, but we will now create a modern fleet, owned by the King and based in our port of Newhaven.

royal_revenue.d: If Scotland is to continue its independent existence, we must secure stable sources of income. By tightening our control over the obligations owed to us by royal estates and feudal properties, we can increase our rightfully received taxes. Through these methods, we can ensure the Crown has sufficient funds to enact their will without relying on other sources of money.

scottish_education.d: Having sent our brightest scholars to be educated in foreign universities for many years, it is time to improve our domestic education, and provide a place here in Scotland where the greatest minds of our nation can learn and grow. Our people should strive to acquire valuable knowledge and skills in their home country rather than wasting their money on expensive travel and their time on foreign institutions.

act_of_revocation.d: It has long been the custom to gift parts of the Royal Domain to our nobility as a reward for their services, but this system cannot be sustained if we want to ensure the integrity of our domain. From now on, we will insist on renting these lands instead of outright giving them away.

scottish_diplomacy.d: For centuries, we relied on diplomacy and contact with foreign powers on the continent to ensure our independence. It is time to formalize this practice, and secure the endurance of our bonds for centuries to come.

scottish_highlander_advance.d: Recruiting regiments from the people who live in the Scottish Highlands can be a crucial measure for our military efforts.

u.t: Production method: Scottish Whisky Distillery Mills

scottish_whisky.d: While distilleries have existed in Scotland for a long time, we should ensure these industries are finally put under the purview of the state. This supervision will allow us to establish ourselves at the forefront of liquor production, and expand our exports industry.

scottish_enlightenment.d: Rapid advancements in philosophy, political economy, and medicine have led to a plethora of accomplishments by our fellow countrymen that will propel Scotland to the forefront of global innovation. This period of Scottish Enlightenment can be a very powerful tool for us on the world stage.

serbian_zaduzbina.d: The Serbian elite and commoners alike are bound by the tradition of the Zadužbina — the 'endowment for the soul'. This cultural drive to build stone churches and monasteries creates a permanent, physical landscape of Serbian presence across the Balkans. These buildings serve as more than religious centers; they are repositories of history, art, and literacy that define the Serbian 'living space'. This architectural obsession ensures that the Serbian culture is physically anchored to the land, providing a sense of permanence and historical continuity that inspires the people to defend their 'holy ground' at any cost.

home_of_hussars.d: Although light cavalry formations are an old concept, the first Balkan hussars — or gusars — appeared as auxiliary units of Byzantium, recruited mainly from Byzantine-held Serbia in the 10th and 11th centuries. Even after Byzantine power dwindled, this tradition remained, and was further refined over the following centuries.

serbian_serbian_epic_poetry.d: Serbian people have developed a 'living history' through epic poetry. The Guslar — a wandering bard — is the primary guardian of the national soul. The Guslar recites thousands of verses accompanied by the gusle. These songs preserve genealogies, legal precedents, and moral imperatives. Serbian culture ensures that even the most illiterate shepherd has an understanding of ancestral rights and a shared identity. Every village gathering becomes a session of historical indoctrination.

serbian_the_icon_of_saint_sava.d: The cultural foundation of the Serbian people is defined by Saint Sava. By blending Byzantine spirituality with local Slavic customs and a fierce commitment to the Serbian language in liturgy, Sava created a national church that is inseparable from the people's identity. This cultural anchor resurfaces again among our people and ensures that all Serbians, whether nobles or peasants, view themselves as part of a distinct, sacred community that remains unified even when political borders shift or collapse, providing an internal stability that resists foreign cultural assimilation.

serbian_seobe.d: The Serbian people have mastered the art of 'mobile identity'. This is characterized by the ability to move entire communities to new lands without losing cultural cohesion. This cultural mobility ensures that the 'Serbian Hearth' is not a fixed geographic point, but a portable and indestructible social contract; wherever the Serbian community strikes its staff, the old laws and the traditions of the Slava are immediately re-established. This resilience makes the Serbian culture functionally impossible to decapitate, as the nation can abandon scorched valleys only to reappear as a fully formed, military society on a new frontier, waiting for the opportune moment to strike back at the heart of their ancestral lands.

serbian_enlightenment.d: Inspired by other nations of the Enlightenment, our national heroes, such as Dositej Obradović, have sought to elevate our vernacular language and literature. Touched by the dearth of secular works accessible to the common folk, Dositej Obradović has taken the lead in bridging the gap between written and spoken Shtokavian. By diligently crafting grammar books and dictionaries, authoring new tomes, and translating foreign works, our nation is fostering a literary revival thanks to the work of these visionaries.

tamazight.d: The Amazigh-speaking communities, from Jerba and the Matmata highlands in the east, through the Zenata confederations of the high plateaus, to the menceyatos of the Canary archipelago in the Atlantic, preserve the Tamazight language family, customary law, and pastoral wool economy that long predate the Arab and Castilian conquests of the wider region. Our weavers turn the long staples of mainland and island flocks into the rugged textiles, tent panels, and burnouses that no urban industry can match, while our tribal councils and menceys maintain a parallel system of customary justice independent of any external jurisprudence. This dual cultural-economic inheritance gives the Berber-rooted communities, from the Saharan oases to the Atlantic islands, a language, livestock, and textile base running parallel to and independent of the urban Maghrebi and Iberian mainstreams.

amazigh_group_agraw_council.d: Our village assemblies (the agraw in the Kabyle highlands, the jma'a across the Maghreb, the tagrart among the Saharan confederations, and the tagoror of the Canary menceyatos) convene the household heads to deliberate water rights, herd movements, blood-money settlements, and the response to any external authority that presents itself at our gates. Decisions taken in council bind every clan that participated and are recorded in the oral memory of the assembled imghassen elders rather than in any written register vulnerable to royal seizure. This deliberative practice spares our crown the costs of suppressing every petty dispute and binds the rural majority of our population to decisions they helped reach.

amazigh_group_igherman.d: Our settlements take the form of the igherman, the fortified stone villages adapted to each landscape we inhabit: the rammed-earth qasbah of the High Atlas, the layered ksar of the southern oases, the tower-house taddart of the Kabyle peaks, and the walled tagoror of the Canary uplands. Each settlement is built communally by the families who will occupy it, with shared granaries, watch-towers, and refuge cisterns concentrated within walls that an attacker cannot afford to siege one by one across our entire territory. This dispersed defensive architecture makes our heartlands disproportionately expensive to invade and bleeds any imperial campaign long before its main force has accomplished anything.

amazigh_group_taqbilt_solidarity.d: The taqbilt, our network of patrilineal clans bound by descent from a shared apical ancestor, is the elementary unit of political life across every Amazigh confederation. A clan that has migrated abroad keeps its place in the home federation and reciprocates with envoys, intelligence, and the hospitality networks that knit our kin from Senegambia to Anatolia together. This kinship infrastructure gives our crown a diplomatic capacity and an envoy reach across the Maghreb, the Sahel, and the Mediterranean that transcends any individual ruler's authority and persists through every dynastic crisis.

amazigh_group_levy_traditions.d: Each Amazigh household stands liable to provide one armed warrior to the village muster when the assembly declares mobilization, with the village blacksmiths furnishing weapons, the women preparing provisions of dried meat and parched grain, and the elders selecting the order of march. The levy reports within days rather than the weeks required by salaried armies, accepts only its own clansmen as captains, and disperses just as quickly when the campaign closes, never developing the permanent costs of a standing force. This customary mobilization gives our crown rapid response and lower military overhead than the regulated regiments of our centralizing neighbors.

amazigh_group_tifinagh_revival.d: Our nineteenth-century intellectuals, the Kabyle scholars led by Si Amar Boulifa, the Tuareg copyists of the Hoggar, and the Mzab schoolmasters, recover the ancestral Tifinagh script from Saharan rock inscriptions, Tuareg veil amulets, and pottery marks, standardizing the geometric letterforms for modern printing presses. We open schools of writing where children of every Amazigh confederation learn to render their Tamazight dialect in a script no Arabic or Latin alphabet can claim. This linguistic-cultural recovery binds the scattered Berber world from the Canaries to the central Sahara into a shared modern identity that the centralizing European empires cannot easily fragment.

tunisian_maliki_heartland.d: Kairouan, the oldest mosque-city west of Cairo, founded by 'Uqba ibn Nāfi' in the seventh century, and the Zaytuna mosque-university of Tunis together anchor the Mālikī school's western capital, training the qadis and muftis of every Maghrebi polity for seven hundred years. Our scholars copy and transmit the foundational Mudawwana of Saḥnūn, our Quranic schools teach the same chain of authority that the Andalusi and Saharan ulama trace their training to, and our judicial opinions bind clients from the Atlantic to the Niger bend. This twin religious-academic axis gives our culture a juridical-scholarly infrastructure that no other Maghrebi heartland (neither Fez nor Tlemcen nor Marrakesh) can match for antiquity and continuity.

tunisian_sahel_ribats.d: The fortified ribāṭ complexes of Sousse, Monastir, and Mahdia, built in the early centuries of Aghlabid and Fatimid rule as combined coastal-monastery garrisons, train the resident religious-warrior caste that defends the Sahel against Christian raiding and inland Berber pressures. Each ribat houses both a permanent garrison and a community of pious volunteers, the murābiṭūn, who alternate watch duty with Quranic study and inter-tribal mediation. This combination of coastal defense and religious training gives the Tunisian Sahel a militarized-monastic frontier infrastructure that no other Maghrebi coast can replicate at our scale.

tunisian_andalusi_refuge.d: The fall of Granada draws successive waves of Andalusi refugees to our Sahel ports of Sfax, Sousse, and Bizerte, and to the inland centers of Testour and Soliman, where they bring with them the Andalusi crafts, dialects, agricultural techniques, and architectural memories of al-'Andalus. Our merchant guilds absorb their craft workshops, our orchards adopt their irrigation techniques, and our scholars copy the manuscripts they salvaged from the Iberian libraries. This Andalusi-Ifrīqiyan synthesis gives our urban culture a fusion that the more inland Maghrebi heartlands lack.

tunisian_shadhili_tariqa.d: The Shādhiliyya, founded by Abū al-Ḥasan ash-Shādhilī (whose formative spiritual years were spent in Tunisia before he settled in Egypt), spreads through the Maghreb under our zawiyas in successive waves, anchoring a Sufi-orthodox synthesis that our ulama uniquely endorse. Our scholarly caste straddles Mālikī jurisprudence and Shādhilī mystical practice without contradiction, our shayḵs are simultaneously qadis and silsila-holders, and our religious peripheries (Berber tribes of the south, Hilali Bedouins of the steppes) are drawn into the tariqa's network of lodges and loyalty oaths. This Sufi-juridical synthesis gives our religious culture a doctrinal flexibility that no purely-juridical Maghrebi rival can match.

tunisian_maliki_hanafi_synthesis.d: Our beylical courts maintain parallel benches of Mālikī and Ḥanafī judges: the older Maghrebi madhhab serving the indigenous population and the newer Ḥanafī school serving the Ottoman-incoming garrisons and their families, with both accorded equal procedural weight in matters of civil law. Our muftis cross-reference each other's opinions, our caravan merchants choose the bench that best suits each contract, and our shari'a archives preserve the precedents of both schools side by side. This plural-jurisdiction settlement gives our urban culture a juridical flexibility that the strictly-Mālikī Maghrebi west and the strictly-Ḥanafī Ottoman east both lack.

tunisian_nahda_circle.d: Our reformist circle, gathered around Khayr ad-Dīn Pasha, Ibn Abī aḍ-Ḍiyāf, and the Zaytuna modernists, drives the Nahḍa that transforms Tunisian administration, education, and law a generation before equivalent movements take root in the Egyptian and Levantine Arab heartlands. We translate European political treatises into Arabic, found the Sadiki College with its bilingual curriculum, and draft the regulations that the 'Ahd al-Amān fundamental pact will enshrine into beylical practice. This early-and-internal Arab reform movement gives our culture a modernist intellectual infrastructure that the later Egyptian and Levantine Nahḍas come to acknowledge as foundational.

zmw_experienced_cattle_herder.d: Herding animals requires some skill, and is crucial for our survival. If we want to stabilize and expand our rule, we should expand our herding and grazing grounds as well.

zmw_stone_builders.d: The astonishing stone buildings of Zimbabwe impress many visitors to our great country. Continuing our architectural traditions will allow us to expand our great cities of stone, which shall stand tall for centuries.

zmw_encourage_new_settlements.d: Beyond our borders lie vast expanses of land, studded with resources and herding grounds waiting eagerly to be claimed by our people. We must encourage settlement in these territories, and establish new towns.

zmw_rekindling_the_royal_fires.d: Our subordinate chiefs must prove their loyalty to us and the gods by traveling to the capital once a year, and using our flames to rekindle their own local fire. Once a year has passed, our army will extinguish their fire, and they will have to make a new journey.

zmw_strict_gold_regulations.d: The land provides us with plenty of goods that foreign merchants have a keen interest in, but our abundant reserves of Gold shine brighter than any other. While such riches are a blessing, the state must tightly regulate all trade and ownership of Gold in order to help prevent the destructive effects of human greed and skullduggery from affecting our bottom line.

zmw_spokesman_before_the_dead.d: Our ruler is not only our leader in the temporal sense, but is also expected to speak on our behalf before the spirits of the dead. Prior to any campaign or harvest, he will communicate our respect and needs to the spirits of our ancestors through ceremonies or dances. Without a diligent ruler to maintain the royal graves and keep in close contact with our dead, things might go awry very quickly.

zmw_elected_administrators.d: Traditionally, all of our administrators, even on the local level, have been direct relatives of our ruler. As our empire has grown and matured, however, it is time we show deference to the local knowledge of our subjects, and allow them to select their own administrators.

zmw_discipline_and_traning.d: Discipline, preparation, and training are the factors that win battles. With this in mind, our commanders have successfully pioneered elaborate new tactics and organizational improvements. Let us make good use of these innovations by dividing our warriors into regiments and having them train regularly with their bows, assegais, daggers, and axes. Practice will also allow them to fight in formation without fear, defeating many more numerous enemies.

zmw_merchant_taxes.d: With the arrival of new traders in the Zambezi area, the need has arisen to assert our authority. Anyone who wishes to trade here, and carry our precious Gold and Ivory to other shores, must first be approved by our ruler and pay a tax in order to be granted access. Should payments lapse, all foreign merchandise will be confiscated by our state.

zmw_controlling_the_mutapan_riches.d: Western travelers have named our land 'Ophir', and the riches of our gold mines and the Zambezi trade have made many visitors envious of us over the centuries. Let us leverage our control over these riches, and build permanent trade posts which can grow into sprawling cities.

albanian_the_kanun.d: In the absence of a central crown, our social order is maintained by the Kanun, a sophisticated code of customary law. This legal framework governs everything from property rights to the sacred duty of Besa (the sworn oath). The Kanun provides a bedrock of stability and honor that foreign administrators can never fully dismantle.

albanian_prokletije.d: The Accursed Mountains that rise in the heart of our lands are as much a part of our people as the Kanun itself. Even the humblest villager knows which passes are passable in winter, which ridges offer shelter from ambush, and which valleys lead nowhere. Invaders who march into these mountains find themselves trapped in a maze by the terrain long before they meet our warriors.

albanian_the_stradioti_tradition.d: The poverty of our mountains has turned our men into the finest light cavalry in Christendom. These Stratioti are sought after by every major power from Venice to France for their unparalleled skills in skirmishing and reconnaissance. By exporting our martial prowess, we bring wealth back to our hills and ensure our soldiers are the most experienced in Europe.

albanian_the_sacred_oath.d: The concept of Besa has evolved into a national institution of trust and hospitality. An Albanian's word is his bond, and this reputation for unwavering loyalty makes us the most trusted guards and mercenaries in the Mediterranean. In a world of shifting alliances, our word is our most valuable currency.

albanian_the_transhumance_networks.d: The seasonal movement of livestock — Transhumance — allows our people to utilize the high summer pastures and the warm winter plains of the coast. This mobile lifestyle makes our population difficult to pin down and provides a resilient food supply that cannot be easily burned by a scorched-earth campaign. Our wealth walks on four legs, always ready to move to safer ground.

albanian_the_fortified_kulla_houses.d: Throughout the countryside, the nobility and wealthy farmers have constructed Kulla — fortified stone tower houses. These structures serve as miniature citadels, protecting families from both blood feuds and enemy raids. They represent a society that is permanently mobilized for defense.

albanian_the_albanian_alphabet_commissio.d: Scholars and patriots are working tirelessly to standardize the Albanian language using a unified Latin alphabet. By establishing national schools and printing newspapers in the vernacular, we are breaking the cultural hegemony of foreign tongues. Literacy in Albanian is the first step toward true independence.

pukara_advance.d: The Pukara is a building placed in hill or mountainous terrain, and serves both as weapon storage and as a defensive fortification. They incorporate the difficulty of the terrain into their design, making them comparatively cheaper and easier to construct and maintain than regular forts.

terraces_advance.d: The Terraces are sloped areas for the purpose of effective farming in the complex terrain of the Andes. Constructed on different height levels, the terraces can provide prime soil for many different crops in a close area.

incamisana_advance.d: The Incamisana is a temple in honor and worship of water and the divine patrons of it. As a combination of architectural beauty and technical ingenuity, the Incamisana has a dual purpose of being a religious building and an irrigation system.

a_bedouin_cavalry_advance.d: The Bedouin are a wandering people who travel through the desert regions of the Arabian Peninsula, North Africa, the Levant and Mesopotamia. Through their nomadic lifestyle, they have mastered their riding skills, and the usage of the Arabian horses makes them a formidable cavalry force.

arm_legacy_of_hayk.d: Hayk, descendant of Noah, founded our kingdom at the base of Mount Ararat after defeating the Babylonians, and thus became the patriarch of our nation. All our people know this story, and all are proud to belong to such an ancient lineage.

arm_mount_ararat.d: Mount Ararat, where Noah's Ark came to rest after the Great Flood, is where our nation first formed. As a result, our people resist with a particularly holy fervor when the sanctity of our territory is threatened.

arm_apostolic_church.d: Armenia was the first nation to declare Christianity as its state religion. As such, our religious traditions, especially those of our clergy, are a major component of our identity.

arm_land_reclamation.d: Armenia has been ravaged by war for centuries. By reclaiming the lands lost in these struggles, making them suitable for inhabitation, and restoring ruined churches and fortresses, we can improve the lives of our people and take firmer control over our territory.

arm_border_nation.d: Since ancient times, Armenia has been the reluctant battleground between larger nations. Even after regaining our sovereignty, remaining neutral is extremely difficult — it is not impossible to appease everyone, but it is not easy, either.

arm_melikdom_organization.d: As one of the few bastions of an independent Armenian state, Armenia is governed by feudal suzerains called meliks, as the old system of Nakharar Titles collapsed after the Mongol invasions. The relationship between meliks and their subordinates is that of a military commanding officer and junior officer, and not of feudal lord and a serf.

arm_mountain_armies.d: Armenia is a mountainous land. Our people have adapted to this terrain over the centuries, and we have developed many ways to use those mountains to our advantage. Our armies will gather readily when called, confident in the additional protection our unique environment provides.

arm_nakharar_titles.d: The Nakharar system of titles was in continuous use in Armenia from its inception until the times of the Mongol invasions, when it collapsed. Although the titles themselves are no longer in use, certain characteristics of that system persist, enhancing the abilities of both our nobles and armies.

arm_greater_armenia.d: In our long and illustrious history, Armenian kingdoms spread over a large territory, and so did our Armenian people. By emulating these bygone realms, we become a beacon of all Armenian people, who will happily unite under our leadership.

bng_bengali_vassal_system.d: During the reign of Delhi, the Bengali people served their overlord as productive vassals. The Dehlavi system shall serve as the foundation for our own vassal systems for the years of Bengali sovereignty to come.

bng_bengali_paik.d: The paiks are the backbone of our military. While other states have the Paik System active and use paiks as their general levies, our state maintains smaller, but very well-organized paiks, and provides them with sufficient military support.

bng_bengali_architecture.d: A mixture of ancient urban architecture, Muslim engineering influences, and traditional Bengali roof-building techniques, the unique Bengali architectural style is used for religious and cultural buildings of all kinds. Due to our expertise in this style, constructing such buildings is significantly easier and more affordable for us than other nations.

bng_habshi_generals.d: Abyssinian slave-soldiers play a significant role in our military as elite infantry. Those who excel as leaders shall be given greater levels of command, while those who demonstrate exceptional loyalty shall make up the palace guard.

bng_war_elephants.d: Although slow, the maneuverability of elephants in the riverine terrain of our country is crucial to quickly resupplying our military. Additionally, war elephants will aid our troops on the battlefield with their imposing stature and terrifying strength.

bng_rupees.d: The lack of a widely adopted standardized currency is stunting our commercial development. As one of the foremost economic powers on the subcontinent, we are in a good position to begin minting a new silver coinage with standard weights, which we shall call the rupee.

bng_bengali_traders.d: The Indian Ocean connects our local markets with those of South East Asia and China. We shall therefore greatly emphasize maximizing our presence in these markets via sea routes, and through this increase our trade profits.

bng_bengali_poetry.d: The written word is one of the most influential and enduring forms of art. Bengali poetry shall tell the tales of epic conquerors, relatable dramas, and engaging philosophical questions, all of which shall further the spread and reputation of Bengali culture.

bng_religious_pluralism.d: India is home to many religions: Hinduism for the majority, Islam as the preferred faith of the ruling classes, and a few remarkable minor religions such as Buddhism and Jainism amongst the working minorities. Promoting one religion over another will cause inevitable chaos and unrest. Thus, we should aim for religious pluralism, and neither favor nor discriminate against any religion in our state.

bng_artillery_corps.d: Cannons are an impactful asset to military campaigns. We must ensure an efficient artillery corps that specializes in dealing damage to the enemy's rows before they even start to clash with our soldiers on the field.

bng_bengali_trade_fleet.d: The Bengali trade fleet brings exotic goods from foreign lands, as well as precious Gold and Silver, to the markets of the Ganges Delta. Our merchants are well renowned in far-flung parts of the world, thanks to our impressive trade fleet.

bng_shipbuilding_industry.d: Maritime trade is vital to our state. Our trade and our warships are some of the most important aspects of our economy, and therefore we focus heavily on supporting the shipbuilding industry.

bng_bengali_industrialization.d: Bengal is uniquely situated in India to start a revolution unlike any seen before. Muslin — the special cotton fabric Bengali spinners are famous for — is a prime trade good for industrialization. We stand poised to exploit new developments in our already world-class textile industry. Let us begin an industrial revolution!

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

ara_a_maritime_realm.d: The Counts of Barcelona have inherited a Mediterranean-facing realm shaped by the trade traditions of Roman Tarraco and the Carolingian Marca Hispanica. Our merchants on the long Catalan coast, from Tarragona and Barcelona to Sant Feliu and the ports of the Empordà, drive the maritime economy of the early Crown, financing royal campaigns in exchange for privilegis of trade. This commercial-naval orientation makes Catalonia the engine of every Aragonese eastward expansion from Mallorca to Sicily.

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

ara_fleet_ordinances.d: The Crown of Aragon's diverse galley fleets draw crews from Marseille to Sicily, and no single port-city statute can govern conduct on multinational vessels in foreign waters. Bernat de Cabrera, under Peter the Ceremonious, has therefore codified the Ordinacions sobre lo Fet de la Mar — Ordinances on What Happens at Sea — one of the earliest naval military codes in Europe. This code consistently regulates the duties of admirals, captains, and crews drawn from every Aragonese realm, turning the Catalan-Aragonese fleet into a coherent fighting institution at a time when other powers still rely on city-state contingents that fight only when paid.

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

ara_valencian_golden_age.d: From the conquest of Valencia by James I in 1238 through the fifteenth-century mercantile boom, the city has become the cultural capital of the eastern Crown of Aragon. Joanot Martorell's chivalric novel Tirant lo Blanch, the love poetry of Ausiàs March, and Isabel de Villena's Vita Christi have established Valencian as a literary language equal to Castilian or Tuscan. This cultural standing gives our realm prestige in courts as far as Naples and Cyprus, marking the Crown of Aragon as a producer of European culture rather than a mere consumer.

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

ara_chartered_merchant_companies.d: Free-for-all competition among Catalan merchant houses dilutes profits and weakens our negotiating position with foreign powers. The Crown therefore charters consortia such as the Compañía de Navegación de Levante and the Compañía de Filipinas, granting them temporary trade monopolies on specific routes in exchange for renewable royal levies and an obligation to defend our convoys with armed vessels. This regulated mercantile system channels Catalan capital into ventures that can compete with the Genoese, Dutch, and English chartered companies operating from the same basins.

b: Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities: +0.5

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

ara_constellation_cities.d: The Crown of Aragon has always been less a kingdom than a federation of capitals — Zaragoza for the Aragonese, Barcelona for the Catalans, Valencia for the Valencians, Palma for the Mallorcans, and Cagliari for the Sardinians. Each metropolis preserves its own Generalitat or Diputación del Reino, its own currency, and its own commercial bourse, exchanging consular agents and ambassadors among themselves under the king's nominal authority. This polycentric urban network gives the Crown an extraordinary administrative resilience — losing any one source of capital never paralyzes the realm, and the rivalries among them sustain a permanent commercial dynamism.

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

ara_mossos_esquadra.d: The Mossos d'Esquadra — the squads of countrymen organized by Pere Anton Veciana — are a permanent rural police force recruited from the local communities they protect. Operating outside the regular military chain and reporting directly to the captain general of Catalonia, they pursue bandits and smugglers through terrain that royal troops cannot effectively patrol. This local policing arm secures the trade routes of the Principality without alienating the population, providing a template that other Iberian realms will eventually imitate.

cha_matrilineal_heritage.d: Women in our society are given more reverence and appreciation than in many of our neighboring countries. The birthright of any child comes from their mother's side, and women have a wide array of liberties and social responsibilities.

cha_religious_tolerance.d: Our society is a melting pot of different religious influences. The Buddhist ideas from China, the Hindu practices from India, and the spread of Islam in South East Asia create a unique environment where religious tolerance is paramount to keeping our society together.

cha_dharmic_presence.d: The Dharmic gods bless us with their presence. May their strength guide us through the most difficult of times.

cha_kshatriya.d: The Kṣatriya is a term adopted from Hindu societies, and describes the elite nobles of our state. Given the origin of this term, it follows that our nobility take similar roles in military and court affairs as their counterparts in India.

cha_veteran_shipbuilders.d: Our state relies on maritime dominance to secure its political, military, and economical presence in Indochina. As such, being able to build ships swiftly is of great importance to our survival.

cha_haluwbilau.d: The Haluwbilau are elite warriors who occupy key positions in both our land and naval forces. Selected for their talents and bravery, these men lead armies and ships into battle against external threats, and also mediate disputes in local communities.

cha_commercial_state.d: Much of our wealth comes from trade. We should concentrate on expanding and refining our exchange practices, with the ultimate goal of creating a commercial state in the process.

cha_boarding_tactics.d: Due to our challenging native terrain, would-be conquerors must rely on their naval capabilities when attempting to invade us. Decades of piracy in the surrounding seas have taught us valuable boarding tactics, which allow us to use an opponent's own ships against them.

cha_towers_on_water.d: As a maritime power, much of our wealth and power comes from the sea and our dominance over it. In order to secure this supremacy, our shipwrights have designed special large warships which are known as Towers on the Water, hybrid creations between a heavy ship and a galley.

cha_cham_cultural_influence.d: Although some of our neighbors see our culture as inferior, they are just in denial, as many of our cultural aspects make their way into their self-proclaimed 'civilized' courts. Cham drumming, songs, dances, poetry... all of these art forms have left a clear and lasting mark on what other nations consider artistic achievement!

corsican_the_machja.d: The Corsican interior, dominated by the dense, aromatic evergreen shrubland known as the Machja (Macchia in standard Italian: the Scrubland), has become the central pillar of the people's survival strategy. Rather than fighting superior maritime invaders on the vulnerable coasts, the population has developed a culture of 'Strategic Retreat' into the impenetrable granite mountains. This has created a society of highlanders who are masters of concealment and rapid movement through vertical terrain. This cultural adaptation has turned the island's geography into a living fortress for our culture, where the people can preserve their laws and customs indefinitely, safe from the naval reach of any invader.

corsican_the_vindetta.d: As past occupiers of our island attempted to impose a rigid legal framework, the Corsican people responded by strengthening their own traditional justice system based on the Vendetta. While viewed as lawlessness by outsiders, this is a sophisticated social mechanism of honor and self-regulation. It creates a culture where the individual is responsible for his own protection and that of his kin, leading to a populace that is universally armed and tactically proficient. This 'Culture of the Long Memory' means that any offense is met with a generational blood-feud. In a national context, this means making the cost of occupation by foreign troops prohibitively expensive in both coin and lives.

corsican_the_castagniccia.d: Past Genoese occupation heavily promoted the cultivation of the chestnut tree, particularly in the central highlands. This has created a unique culture around the chestnut that provides the population with a reliable, low-labor food source that is immune to the grain-price fluctuations of the Mediterranean market. This gives the Corsicans incredible strategic autonomy; they can retreat into the mountains and subsist indefinitely on chestnut flour, making them immune to the standard naval blockades and 'siege by starvation' tactics employed in the past by the Genoese maritime fleets.

corsican_the_corsican_baroque.d: A wave of Baroque church construction has hit the island, funded by the wealth of returning mercenaries and merchants. These churches are characterized by an 'Austere Grandeur', reflecting the rugged and pious nature of the people. Culturally, this is a display of civilizational defiance — a statement to our neighbors that Corsica is a wealthy, cultured society capable of producing grand monuments. These churches will serve as the primary nodes of social cohesion, where the community gathers to celebrate their distinct identity through choral polyphony and theatrical religious ritual.

corsican_lamentu_and_voceru.d: The Corsican culture of oral poetry, specifically the Lamentu (Lamento in standard Italian: mourning songs) and Voceru (Vocero in standard Italian: songs of vengeance), has become the primary vehicle for preserving national memory. These songs act as a living archive of the people's struggles and the names of their martyrs. Culturally, this ensures that the spirit of resistance is ingrained in every child from birth, making it impossible for an occupier to 're-educate' or assimilate the population. This oral tradition functions as a powerful psychological weapon, maintaining a state of perpetual high morale and cultural defiance even during the darkest periods of foreign military occupation.

corsican_chjame_rispondi.d: During the long years of foreign military pressure, the Corsican oral tradition of Chjam'è Rispondi (Call and Response) evolved into a sophisticated tool of social cohesion. This improvised poetic competition allowed the people to debate politics, honor their fallen heroes, and mock their occupiers through coded metaphors in the town squares. This all has ensured that the principles of the Enlightenment and the memories of the Revolution remain accessible to even the illiterate segments of society. By encouraging this we will create a unified cultural narrative that is immune to censorship, ensuring that the flame of Corsican identity remains burning bright through every situation.

dalmatian_the_maritime_commune_spirit.d: Our culture is defined by the Commune, where every citizen's honor is tied to the prestige of their city. This spirit of urban competition drives our people to build more beautiful cathedrals and faster ships than their neighbors, creating a culture of extreme local pride and innovation. This 'City-State' mentality ensures that our people are highly invested in their local governance and defense, fostering a population that is exceptionally resilient and self-reliant, capable of managing its own affairs even when the central crown is distant or weak.

dalmatian_the_cult_of_the_local_patron_s.n: The Cult of the Local Patron Saint
dalmatian_the_cult_of_the_local_patron_s.d: Every Dalmatian city is anchored by the intense veneration of its own unique patron — Saint Chrysogonus in Zadar, Saint Domnius in Split, Saint Tryphon in Kotor. These saints are not just religious figures; they are the 'Foundational Sovereigns' of the city. Their feast days are the primary social and political events of the year, uniting all classes in a shared ritual that reinforces the city's independent identity. This intense localism ensures that Dalmatian culture is a mosaic of fiercely independent urban identities, making it impossible for any foreign power to culturally dominate the entire coast at once.

dalmatian_the_guild_of_the_stone_master.d: The abundant, bone-white limestone of the coast has birthed a culture of master stone-cutters who view the karst as a canvas. Our craftsmen have developed a 'Gothic-Renaissance' style that is world-renowned for its structural innovation and delicate carving. This is not merely art; it is a physical statement of our permanence. By building every church, palace, and city wall from local stone, our people create a landscape that is both beautiful and indestructible, fostering a national pride that views the Dalmatian town as a sacred, eternal monument to our skill that no sea-borne empire can truly erase.

dalmatian_the_high_chancery_style.d: The Dalmatian patriciate has adopted the 'High Dalmatian' literary standard for their private correspondence and diplomatic registries, emulating their Italian Peninsula counterparts. This cultural pivot away from the medieval Latin towards the refined vernacular aligns the coastal cities with the heart of the Italian Renaissance. This shared linguistic aesthetic creates a seamless intellectual bridge with the Venetian Studio, allowing Dalmatian poets and lawyers to participate in the most exclusive humanist circles of Italy. This 'Linguistic Refinement' ensures that our diplomats are regarded as cultural peers in any Western court, providing a diplomatic shield based on shared civilization rather than raw military force.

dalmatian_the_accademia_degli_oziosi.d: Modeled after the Italian literary academies, the intellectuals of our cities have founded societies like the Accademia degli Oziosi to discuss physics, astronomy, and classical poetry. These 'Idle' scholars are anything but — they serve as the scientific advisors to the naval admiralties, applying the new Baroque rationalism to cartography and ballistics. This cultural institutionalization of curiosity ensures that the Dalmatian urban centers remain the 'Scientific Watchtowers' of the Adriatic, preserving the coast as a hub of European Enlightenment even as the interior of the Balkans remains locked in traditionalist cycles.

dalmatian_mediterranean_cosmopolitanism.d: Centuries of maritime trade and bilingualism have produced a culture of Cosmopolitanism, where our people are at home in any port from Venice to the Levant. This cultural openness allows us to absorb and adapt the best ideas from across the globe, creating a society that is uniquely flexible and resilient. Our people are the 'citizens of the sea', possessing a world-view that is far broader than that of the landlocked interior. This cosmopolitan spirit ensures that the Dalmatian culture remains vibrant and commercially successful, serving as the 'window to the world' for the entire Balkan Peninsula.

emilian_al_po_doma.d: Living in a flood-prone plain, the Emilian people have mastered the art of river canalization. These are not just for drainage but serve as a renewable energy source for silk mills and grain grinders. This has not only allowed our landlocked cities like Modena and Bologna to function as industrial hubs, transporting goods via artificial waterways to the Po River and the Adriatic Sea, but also tamed the Po river and its destructive floods.

emilian_the_via_emilia.d: Emilian cities shall leverage their position on the Via Emilia (the ancient Roman artery) to establish international trade fairs. We will provide the means for these activities to develop with total security and will standardize weights and measures. This will help us gain the trust of international traders, so that traders from the Alps and the Mediterranean can meet. This trade-centric mindset will allow Emilian states to thrive as essential middlemen in the luxury silk and spice trades.

emilian_dispenza_emigliana.d: The Emilian courts have developed a culture where each chef acts as an ambassador of the region. Our region's unique products (balsamic vinegars, cured hams, and aged cheeses) are used to woo foreign monarchs. This strategy of conquering through the palate will ensure that we are always influential in the courts of Europe, securing alliances through the sheer exclusivity and quality of our premium foods.

emilian_the_tera_cruda.d: Facing our enemy's modern cannons, we have realized brick is too brittle. We will pioneer the use of rammed-earth and brick-faced ramparts. This adaptation to the lack of stone - that will be known by many as the Trace Italienne - will make our engineers become the world's most sought-after military consultants, exporting our 'Silt-and-Brick' defensive science to the rest of the world.

emilian_la_mzura_dal_sol.d: To maximize the efficiency of the Po Valley, the state will implement a scientific mapping of every drainage ditch and field. This measuring will turn the landscape into a giant spreadsheet. It will allow for the most precise tax collection in Europe, ensuring that every acre of the fertile silt is paying its fair share to our treasury to fund the modernization of the nation.

emilian_al_melodram.d: The construction of massive public opera houses will become a state priority. These theaters will be the 'Parliaments of the People', where the rising bourgeoisie meet to share common national myths through music. This culture will ensure that the Emilian population is the most politically mobilized in Italy, steeling the population to face every challenge.

galician_rias_atlanticas.d: The deep estuaries of our Atlantic coast — the Rías Baixas of Vigo, Pontevedra, Arousa, and Muros, and the Rías Altas of A Coruña, Betanzos, and Ferrol — penetrate inland for dozens of kilometers and produce some of the richest fishing grounds in Europe. Every village along these inlets sends men to sea from boyhood, harvesting sardines, hake, and shellfish that supply our markets and the inland Spanish economy beyond. This natural harbor geography gives our fleets shelter from Atlantic storms and our population a permanent core of skilled sailors that no inland realm can match.

galician_camino_pilgrimages.d: The pilgrim's road to Santiago de Compostela draws tens of thousands of devout travelers from across Christendom each year, from Picardy and Cologne, from Bologna and Vienna, and even from the British Isles and Scandinavia. Every albergue, parish, and roadside shrine along the way collects money from these visitors, and our inland towns prosper directly from their passage. This pilgrim economy turns spiritual duty into a steady inflow of foreign coin that no other Iberian realm receives at our scale.

galician_foros.d: Our long-term tenancy contracts — the Foros — give peasant families heritable rights to their plots for three generations or more in exchange for fixed rents owed to the lord, monastery, or city that holds the underlying title. This security of tenure encourages our smallholders to invest in clearing, draining, terracing, and planting orchards that a short-term tenant would never undertake. This stable tenure system raises agricultural productivity across our patchwork of small plots and protects rural population growth from the worst feudal predation.

galician_irmandinos_legacy.d: The Irmandiños — the great peasant brotherhoods that rose against the abuses of the Galician nobility — left a permanent legacy of communal organization in our villages and parishes. Though the rebellion was eventually suppressed, its negotiated aftermath produced the foro reforms that protect peasant tenure and the irmandade tradition that still binds neighbors into mutual-aid associations against any future tyranny. This communal organizational capacity gives our state ready-made militia, labor, and credit networks the moment the Crown calls for them.

galician_mountain_minerals.d: The interior mountains of Lugo, Ourense, and the Bierzo conceal substantial deposits of tin, wolfram, slate, and silver that we now exploit through systematic mining concessions. The Minas de Galicia produce ore that feeds the iron forges of Asturias and silver that supplements the Crown's coinage at Ferrol. This mineral wealth diversifies our regional economy beyond fishing and dairy and gives our towns a manufacturing base that less geologically fortunate realms cannot easily replicate.

galician_rexurdimento.d: Our cultural renaissance — the Rexurdimento — bursts into the nineteenth century with lyrical poetry, epic histories, bardic verse, and radical satires. After centuries of decline as a written tongue, Galician returns to print as a vehicle for literary expression respected far beyond our borders. This linguistic revival raises literacy across our region and gives every Galician a sense of pride in a regional identity that the centralizing nation-state cannot easily erase.

geo_georgian_highlands.d: The lands of Georgia are nestled among the Caucasus Mountains, and no foreign power has ever found it easy to penetrate our territory. Our tenacity and resilience are legendary.

geo_georgian_script.d: The 'Georgian alphabet', created centuries ago, is not just one alphabet, but in fact three. Mkhedruli is the script used by the civil administration, while Asomtavruli and Nuskhuri is used by our church. As such, our Holy Scriptures can remain uninfluenced by the lay language, while our people can still feel connected to them.

geo_georgian_isolation.d: Surrounded by powerful countries with vastly different religions and cultures from ours, we are forced to use opportunistic diplomacy, and often change allegiances in order to appease everyone and preserve peace for as long as possible.

geo_legacy_of_saint_nino.d: Georgia has one of the oldest Christian churches in the world, tracing its roots back to the conversion of the region by Saint Nino over a millennium ago. Through the centuries, the Georgian Church has served as an increasingly unifying force in all Georgian states, and has served as a central element in Georgian culture in the face of Byzantine, Mongol, and Muslim influence. With few other Christian kingdoms left in this region, and given the splintered loyalties within Georgia, the Church still plays an important role as a unifying force against outsiders.

geo_restoration_of_fortresses_and_church.d: Our many fortresses and churches have helped our country to resist and continue to survive among encroaching foreign influences. Our fortresses protect the land while our churches protect our spirit, and we must keep both in prime condition if we are to thrive.

geo_sadrosho_districts.d: Sadrosho, banners, are special military districts used for mobilization purposes. By dividing our territory into several sadrosho, each under the command of their own dedicated military official, we can better organize the recruitment and distribution of all our troops.

geo_dasturlamali.d: Georgia has experienced tumultuous centuries since the Mongol invasion, marked by periodic division, shifting external pressures, and the rising influence of the local nobility. The old Georgian feudal system has been made obsolete, or at least partially discarded. The Dasturlamali, a comprehensive set of rules and guidelines detailing the obligations of subjects and nobles toward king and state, strengthens internal order and serves as the foundation for our kingdom's legal framework.

geo_georgian_embassies.d: We have a tradition of establishing strong diplomatic ties with all nations around us, regardless of our possible differences. As a result, our diplomats are always well received and respected.

geo_georgian_unification.d: Georgia has been divided in the past, both by foreign influences and internal causes. But the patriotic Georgian people are more than willing to fight to ensure that Georgia is never divided again.

arabian_horsemanship.d: The Horses we raise are desired in many foreign lands for their beauty and strength. With our focus set on raising and exporting them, we will benefit greatly from their renown.

arabian_desert_warfare.d: The inhospitable deserts of Arabia have made our warriors stronger, able to wear down the enemy before moving in for the killing blow.

chinese_siege_engineers.d: Our thick, sturdy fortifications represent generations of defensive engineering expertise. Conversely, our thorough understanding of fortification weaknesses, learned from building impregnable walls, helps us to develop particularly effective siege tactics and strategies.

chi_legitimate_claimant.d: Our origins may be humble, but we have proven our ability to lead, and have inspired and won the loyalty of many faithful subjects. We are now seen as worthy claimants to the Mandate of Heaven and the Middle Kingdom.

chi_great_rivers_of_china.d: While the great rivers flowing through our lands do have some associated risks for nearby settlements, they are also an invaluable tool for crop production.

b: Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities: +0.25
swabian_league_of_cities.d: Swabia is home to many wealthy cities, which are desirable targets for foreign ambition. To better protect our nation, we should come together in times of war and fight united against foreign incursions.

westphalian_monastic_traditions.d: Northern Germany is home to many Catholic strongholds, such as the Bishoprics in Münster and Paderborn. Monastic life and associated regional religious traditions have a generally positive effect on the literacy and education of our clergy, as there are plenty of opportunities for them to further educate themselves. This access to learning also helps the Holy Mother Church by creating an intellectual flock well-suited to priestly duties.

north_german_hanseatic_traditions.d: The people of Northern Germany have for a long time reaped the benefits of access to the Baltic Sea. While many of our southern neighbors must make do using rivers to transport goods, our traders have a long tradition of sailing the Baltic to make their fortunes, bringing enviable wealth back to our shores.

custom_union_of_the_rhine.d: In the sprawling patchwork of our great empire, cooperation and collaboration between neighboring groups is vital to the health of our economy. We shall join the customs union of the Rhine and adopt their gulden coins to make business transactions less complicated for our merchants, and streamline our international diplomacy.

german_baltic_sailors.d: Harsh climates breed hardy people. Traversing the cold Baltic Sea has certainly left its mark on our sailors, making them mentally resilient and particularly skilled at their profession. This is for their ultimate benefit, as the sea can be a merciless mistress.

franconian_proud_knights.d: Our people have committed a long line of proud knights to Imperial service. They embody knightly ideals that have become less common over time, but remain an essential part of our identity. We have a long history to look at for proper education in both chivalric conduct and military matters. This tradition of Imperial knights naturally increases the willingness of our noble class to contribute levies in hopes of winning glory in honorable combat.

saiger_process.d: A new and revolutionary smelting process, enriching silver-containing copper with lead, will allow us to increase the productivity of our mining operations.

german_river_toll_castle_advance.d: A small castle placed along the river facilitates control over passing traders, granting our state a vital share of the local trade income.

german_mountain_toll_castle_advance.d: A small castle placed on a crucial mountain pass facilitates control over passing traders, granting our state a vital share of the local trade income.

german_populating_the_countryside.d: By encouraging settlement in rural areas and giving the people land to work there will be a great foundation to slowly but surely increase the wealth and productivity of our more sparsely populated territories.

landsknechte.d: A new type of unit organization has been born out of Germany's constant wars: The Landsknechte, which takes the form of mixed troops formed by innovative pikemen squares, with arquebusiers supporting from their flanks, and a front line composed of the infamous Doppelsöldner, 'double-pay men', carrying two-handed swords. This allows for tactics that combine close-quarters and medium-range combat.

swabian_frugal_people.d: Many have accused our people of stinginess, and laughed at our good sense of economic caution. Fortunately, we cannot hear their mockery over the sound of all these ducats jingling in our purse.
