pun_punjabi_textile_industry.d: The Punjab is a major center for textile production. Cloth from our weavers is specially made for markets all over Asia and Europe, and our weavers are among the most productive in India.

pun_strength_of_the_misls.d: The administrative system of the Misl states of Punjab allows them to field impressive cavalry forces. In times of need, we may call upon these forces to fight a common enemy.

pun_reforming_the_punjabi_army.d: The ways of our forefathers were sound, and have served us well over the years. But in order for our armies to continue to triumph on the battlefields, we must create a more professional military. By studying the way other countries organize their armies and adapting their methods when prudent, we may create a more efficient Punjabi army while still retaining the unique qualities of our current military system.

raj_militaristic_society.d: There is almost no division between civil and military society among the Rajputs. Our nation is a host, defined by its people rather than by the land we control, and its people are warriors. We must ensure that military divisions properly meet our administrative needs as the host expands.

raj_combat_training.d: Every soldier is trained for battle, but our people start combat training at a much younger age, granting them skills surpassing those of other green soldiers.

raj_clan_loyalties.d: The influence of our clan extends far beyond our own borders. We are able to draw from other Rajput groups from all over northern India when filling the ranks of our armies.

raj_monumental_architecture.d: What purpose does victory serve if there is nothing to immortalize our achievements? Monuments, such as an awe-inspiring Tower of Victory, shall be erected, so future generations will know of our greatest battles and be appropriately inspired.

raj_marwari_horses.d: Like their masters, Rajput cavalry horses are meticulously trained to perform on the field of battle. It is said that a Marwari horse will only leave the battlefield under one of three conditions - victory, death, or when carrying a wounded master to safety. By taking good care of these divine beings, we will ensure the everlasting dominance of our horsemen on the battlefields of India.

raj_reorganized_rajput_regiments.d: Traditional clan structures are an excellent foundation for a modernized regimental system. Existing hierarchies based on kinship and unconditional loyalty can be easily translated into an organized and formal chain of command.

raj_martial_smiths.d: Wars are not only won through tactics and bravery, but also through weaponry. Our blacksmiths shall forge the finest martial weapons for our warriors to wield in defense of the Rajput people.

raj_fortress_architecture.d: The rise of Delhi, and the invading Muslim warriors of the past, were wake-up calls. We must always be prepared for foreign invaders, and thus, we must hire the most skilled architects to design impregnable forts throughout our realm. The immensely long walls that will be needed to protect our land make this an ambitious project, but our determination to defend our people shall ensure that it is done.

raj_expanded_artillery_arm.d: Sieges are what win wars. We must experiment with ways of creating bigger and better cannons to bring down the many forts of our enemies, both within India and outside it.

raj_the_purbias.d: The Rajputs have spread themselves throughout northern India in their pursuit of glory. The Purbias, elite Rajput soldiers who venture as mercenaries, are renowned for their combat ability, and as such spread our fearsome reputation.

raj_mandatory_firearm_drilling.d: Many Rajput soldiers are experts in the use of personal firearms. We should put these hardened veterans to work training the next generation of soldiers, rather than risking the loss of their expertise in battle. All of our soldiers must be drilled in firearms tactics before they are expected to meet our enemies on the front line.

raj_painting_school.d: Rajput painters already have an excellent reputation, but it could be even better. We must encourage our artists to develop their skills and add to the glory of our dynasty by creating a school of painting particular to our state.

raj_rajput_resistance.d: Rajput poet-musicians tell stories of our people's many battles against foreign invaders, and how our ancestors would rather die than admit themselves defeated. We must encourage this spirit of unity, and give our musicians reason to write new ballads of bravery in the face of death.

raj_martial_ethos.d: The upbringing and traditions of Rajput warriors ensure a wide base for recruiting officers to lead our armies. In order to capitalize on this, we should formalize career opportunities and advancement paths to encourage these promising young fighters to serve as officers in our forces.

romagnol_al_teri_dlesarchet.d: Romagna has preserved a unique legal artifact of the Byzantine Exarchate of Ravenna. Unlike the Lombard-influenced north, Romagnol culture has retained a deeper layer of Roman-Byzantine administrative law. This has fostered a differentiated culture, where even the smallest towns claim ancient imperial privileges. This administrative complexity makes the region a nightmare for large empires to centralize efficiently, as every valley is protected by its own Roman web of exemptions and local statutes.

romagnol_mura_malatestiani.d: Romagnol towns, caught between the Papal States and Venice, have become laboratories for defensive architecture. The region has pioneered the use of the Roca (Rocca in standard Italian: the Fortress), a fortress with rounded towers that deflect fire from primitive cannons. These fortifications mean that every village is a tactical strongpoint. They will force invaders into a slow, attritional style of warfare, allowing the small Romagnol states to punch far above their weight in Mediterranean power politics.

romagnol_the_sangiovese_viticulture.d: The Romagnol hills are dedicated to the cultivation of the Sangiovese grape. This is not just agriculture; it is a 'Warrior's Wine', robust and hearty. The state will formalize wine-making protocols to ensure a high-calorie, durable product for the infantry. This will also provide a reliable high-value trade good that integrates the rugged Apennine peasants into the urban market, ensuring rural loyalty through economic prosperity.

romagnol_the_stampa_dpopul.d: Romagna will become a center for broadside printing — cheap, popular pamphlets in the local dialect. This will create a public narrative, where news, prophecies, and folk songs are disseminated to even the rural population. This literacy-based mobilization will ensure that the state can communicate its decrees rapidly and effectively, fostering a highly informed and politically active populace.

romagnol_the_agricultural_academies.d: Following the trends of the late Baroque, every major Romagnol town will establish an Académia focused on improving agricultural yields. These local scientific societies will study the drainage of the Vâli (marshes) and the selection of disease-resistant vines. These agronomy projects will turn the region into an experimental farm, leading to a surplus of crops that will fuel the regional manufactories and provide the state with high-value trade goods for the Adriatic markets.

romagnol_la_streda_rumegna.d: The state and local communes will unite to undertake the radical modernization of the ancient Via Romea coastal road. By building new stone bridges and drainage systems, we will reconnect the Romagnol coast to the Venetian and Papal markets. This plan will turn the coastal towns from isolated fishing villages into significant trade hubs, facilitating the movement of Romagnol agricultural products and providing the strategic mobility necessary for any future war that threatens our soil.

veche_advance.d: The Veche is a popular assembly with its origins in ancient tribal councils, which themselves existed long before the time of the Rus'. It is the highest judicial and legislative authority of the state.

russian_integration.d: The East Slavic are vast and diverse in their culture. To unify them like the rulers of old once did, we should promote our shared history and forge an unbreakable cultural bond between the different groups.

russian_resiliance.d: The Mongol invasions of the past left a strong determination within the East Slavic to resist foreign rule. We can utilize their zeal to reinforce our troops.

land_of_the_rus.d: Reunification of the Rus' is a common goal among the East Slavic rulers, and aspiring conquerors can use this as a justification of conquest.

the_mestnichestvo_advance.d: The Mestnichestvo is an ancient system that assigns positions of state to people based on the antiquity of their lineage and the seniority they hold within their families. The most tangible demonstration of this system involved the seating order of Boyars at the Tsar's table, which reflects their individual rank and precedence.

voivode_advance.d: The Voivode is a military leader with regional administrative authority, defending territory and maintaining order. A voivode can be useful in overcoming the challenges posed by the limited means of communication available, as they have the authority to make crucial decisions without waiting for approval.

siberian_frontier.d: The distant wastes of Siberia call to us. We must clear a path to its frozen heart, and let our Cossacks go forth and claim land for the Russian people.

ostrog_advance.d: The Ostrog is a small, wooden fortification which is constructed in remote territories of Russia. Due to their reliance on lumber, Ostrogs are relatively inexpensive and swift to construct.

russian_artillery_yard.d: Superior firepower is what determines who wins the sieges of today as well as the pitched battles of tomorrow. We must build a state-of-the-art artillery yard in the heart of our country, to ensure our armies are never without cannons nor ammunition.

table_of_ranks.d: The abolishment of the Mestnichestvo was the first step toward creating a more meritocratic state bureaucracy. The Table of Ranks further codified this principle, making military advancement conditional on performance rather than noble birth.

russian_legitimization.d: The East Slavic people have occupied and ruled these lands for centuries. It is only natural that a East Slavic ruler should govern their own people. The more East Slavic we present ourselves to be, the easier the people will accept our leadership.

flexible_loyalty.d: Our nation is caught in a conflux between the warring religions of Europe and a variety of foreign threats. The only way we can ensure our survival in this storm is to take a flexible stance towards cooperating with local mercenary bands.

heritage_of_the_rus.d: The lands of the Rus' shattered into fragmented states long ago, but the memory of our once-great empire, ruled from Kyiv, burns brightly in us all. If we style ourselves in the old fashion, and highlight our connection to our ancestors, we will be able to carve out a distinctive set of traditions for our people.

mother_of_russian_cities.d: Kyiv was once the shining capital of a great empire spanning from the northern forests of Novgorod to the southern shores of the Black Sea. After suffering the dissolution of the Rus' and the invasions of the Mongols, little remained of it. But the time has come for our revival, and no matter what our cities have endured, we vow that they will recover and prosper for centuries to come!

international_influences.d: Many foreign merchants and travelers frequent our roads, bringing vast wealth to our land. We could convince some of these avid traders to permanently settle in our towns and cities, if we assure them they will not face persecution for their beliefs.

reuniting_rus.d: We are the true heir of the Kievan Rus', and those lands must be reunited under our banner!

united_faith.d: No matter our situation, we must ensure the unity of our faith. Only if our clergy is aligned, and no discord exists between factions of the faithful, will they be able to focus on their primary function of guiding and aiding our population.

east_and_west.d: Our strategic position between eastern and western empires has given our merchants the opportunity to act as essential middlemen for lucrative regional trade routes.

ruthenian_state_advance.d: In the past, we bowed to foreign influences, and were obliged to adapt to their customs to ensure friendly relations. But times have changed, and now we must affirm our own customs, or risk falling into the sphere of foreign influences again.

ruthenian_rural_buildings.d: Much of Ruthenia is rural, empty land. While our great cities like Kyiv serve many important purposes, we cannot neglect the remote lands or small villages that provide us with crucial supplies of food and raw materials.

ruthenia_commoner_education.d: By establishing local schools, we will ensure that our population is well-educated at all levels of society.

sardinian_the_barbagia.d: The central mountains (the Barbagia) have remained a 'Land of Barbarians' to every Mediterranean invader for centuries. The culture here is defined by the S'Ard (Sardinian) identity — a fierce, isolated pastoralism that rejects any form of external taxation or conscription. This has created a cultural redoubt where the ancient Nuragic spirit of independence is preserved. An invading state can master the coastal cities, but the heart of the island will remain a forbidden zone, ensuring the survival of our customs through pure geographical and social defiance.

sardinian_the_artizanu.d: In the cities and towns, a distinct class of Sardinian artisans and silver-smiths is emerging, blending foreign aesthetics with indigenous motifs. These guilds are fiercely protective of their liberties, often coming into conflict with foreign merchant monopolies. This creates a vibrant urban culture that is both Mediterranean in outlook and Sardinian in soul, providing the state with a literate and skilled middle class that can manage the complexities of maritime trade.

sardinian_the_ademprivio.d: Sardinian culture remains anchored in the Ademprivio — the right of the people to use feudal lands for grazing, wood-cutting, and water. Despite attempts to privatize land, the Sardinian peasants have maintained their culture of 'Sacred Commons'. This prevents the total impoverishment of the rural classes, and ensures a high level of internal stability, as we recognize that the stability of our lands rests on the shared prosperity of these pastoral communities.

sardinian_the_turres_costeras.d: To combat the pirate threat, our people will construct a chain of coastal towers. This will give rise to the 'Coastal Vigil', where entire families will move from the shore to the hills while maintaining a permanent rotation of watchers. This culture of 'Horizon Scanning' will turn the entire island population into a strategic state asset, ensuring that the Mediterranean's most vital sea-lanes are constantly monitored by a populace that views defense as a daily ritual.

sardinian_the_hymnu_sardu.d: As a modern national consciousness begins to emerge, our culture is shifting from feudal loyalty to a new 'Patriotism of the Kingdom'. This is expressed through a boom in Sardinian literature and political pamphlets that demand a 'Sardinia for the Sardinians'. This cultural movement provides the state with a new, modernized administrative class that seeks to reform our ancient feudal laws into a modern sovereign constitution.

sardinian_the_industrial_transition.d: With the discovery of new lead and zinc veins, our traditional pastoral culture is beginning to merge with the industrial era. We will establish the first modern mines and foundries, staffed by Sardinian workers who bring their traditional 'Guild Discipline' to the contemporary age. This mining culture will provide us with the raw materials needed for modern warfare and infrastructure, turning the island into the industrial battery of our rising state.

scandinavian_fishing_privileges_advance.d: This Location has been granted exclusive rights over nearby fishing grounds and the trade in dried and salted fish. Norwegian coastal towns organized around these privileges supplied Fish across Northern Europe.

scandinavian_bergslag_privileges_advance.d: The Crown has recognized this Location as a mining community (bergslag), granting it collective rights over local ore extraction, its own court, and freedom from military conscription. The Commoners of the mines hold a stronger legal standing than in ordinary towns.

scandinavian_thing_rights_advance.d: This Location has been granted formal assembly rights (tingsrätt), giving its inhabitants a recognized legal forum for governance and justice. Royal authority is curtailed in exchange for a more orderly and loyal population.

scandinavian_tar_privileges_advance.d: This Location has been granted rights to harvest and export Tar and Naval Supplies from Crown forests. These forest industries are the backbone of Baltic shipbuilding supply chains.

legacy_of_the_normans.d: Forged in the crucible of conquest, the Sicilian Norman army blended the unstoppable charge of Norman knights with the strategic sophistication of Byzantine, Arab, and Lombard warfare. Masters of both battlefield ferocity and tactical flexibility, they carved a kingdom at the crossroads of civilizations.

sic_naval_vigilance.d: Constant raids from Barbary pirates and Ottoman ships have forced Sicily to maintain a vigilant coastal defense. Its galleys and forts became critical for protecting southern Europe.

sic_sicilian_silk.d: In the time of Frederick II, Silk was Sicily's major export. Although our Silk industry has declined in the intervening centuries, Sicily's productions having been outstripped by that of the northern Italian states, there is no reason why it should not rise again. By investing in our Silk production, we can see our weavers and craftsmen flourish anew.

sicilian_the_cult_of_the_santuzze.d: The religious identity of Sicily has for a long time been tied to powerful female patron saints, who are believed to protect cities from plague and lava. The massive, theatrical processions (like the Festino of Palermo) associated with their worship serve as a release valve for social tension, and as a display of communal unity. These rituals are the heartbeat of Sicilian public life, reinforcing social cohesion.

sic_sicilian_enlightenment.d: Though distant from the great salons of Paris or Wien, Sicily has fostered its own Enlightenment. Intellectuals challenged feudal privileges, promoted science, and advocated legal reforms, building a tradition of critical inquiry that navigated the tensions between faith and reason. These ideas laid the groundwork for modernity in the shadow of monarchy and tradition.

sic_sicilian_reforms.d: As time passes, our institutions become obsolete or just inefficient. Reforms are necessary if we want our nation to prosper and thrive. Our best minds will work hard to ensure that no waste happens, and that our processes are as efficient as possible.

slovak_the_urban_syncretism.d: Following the devastation of the Mongol invasions, the state encouraged the arrival of Zipser German settlers to rebuild the shattered economy. Unlike many other colonial movements, these settlers integrated deeply with the local Slavic population, resulting in a unique cultural and legal syncretism known as the 'Saxon Law'. This blending of traditions created a multilingual and highly skilled urban middle class that combined Slavic agricultural resilience with German technical expertise in mining and metallurgy. This atmosphere of shared knowledge fostered a culture of innovation, where the exchange of ideas between different linguistic groups accelerated the spread of new technologies and administrative practices, making the Slovak towns some of the most progressive in the region.

slovak_the_slovensky_vernacular.d: The local Slavic vernacular — distinct from Czech or Polish — has begun to appear with increasing frequency in official town records and legal documents, most notably in the Žilina Book. This development may signal the birth of a formal Slovak administrative language if we support it, allowing the local government to communicate more effectively with the peasantry and the lower nobility without relying solely on Latin or German. By codifying local speech into a written administrative format, the state will improve the efficiency of its judicial system and strengthen the bond between the common people and the government. This early linguistic standardization will provide a sense of 'National Agency', making the state more resilient to foreign administrative overhauls.

slovak_the_slovak_rome.d: The city of Trnava has become the intellectual and spiritual sanctuary of Slovakia. This has led to a dramatic boom in High Baroque architecture, with the city's skyline filled with grand churches and academic halls. The printing of Slavic-language books is flourishing here, making Trnava the primary engine of intellectual resistance against heretics and heathens. By strengthening this cultural concentration, we will ensure that the Slavic population remains deeply anchored in a sophisticated, literate, and religiously unified identity during a period of extreme existential threat.

slovak_the_slovak_sappers.d: The deep-mining culture of the Slovak Ore Mountains has produced the most skilled subterranean engineers in Europe. The state has begun drafting these Slovak Miners (Banskí Chlapi) into specialized 'Sapper and Miner' regiments. Their cultural familiarity with black powder, tunneling, and structural bracing in the dark will make them terrifyingly effective in siege warfare. They can collapse enemy bastions from below or build fortified trenches in half the time of standard laborers. This 'Miner-Soldier' identity will turn the Slovak workforce into a strategic military asset, making the capture of Slovak mining towns a high priority for any empire seeking to master the art of 17th-century siegecraft.

slovak_the_highland_architecture.d: A unique architectural culture is emerging, wherein the sophisticated stone-working of the Germans meets the ancient Slavic tradition of heavy timber construction. This results in 'Articular Wooden Churches'. Culturally, this represents an 'Architecture of Resistance' — buildings that can be constructed rapidly in the mountains, but are designed with hidden defensive features, like reinforced oak shutters and elevated entrances. This cultural aesthetic is born from a need for beauty in a state of permanent distrust, creating a landscape of cultural supremacy. By learning from this lesson, we can capitalize on these techniques for the glory of our nation.

slovak_the_slovak_romanticism.d: A new generation of Romantic intellectuals is shifting the linguistic base to the Central Slovak dialects, creating a version of the language that is becoming the standard. This is not merely a literary shift but a radical political movement, as they are using poetry, folk songs, and journalism to elevate our identity. This Romantic fervor will turn every cultural production into a call for national greatness, unifying the peasantry and the burgeoning middle class in a shared vision of national pride.

slovene_the_freising_fragments.d: Drawing upon the ancient traditions of the Freising Fragments, the Slovenian peasantry and local clergy have maintained a distinct linguistic identity, which has survived within the ecclesiastical structures of the Holy Roman Empire. This early vernacular tradition serves as a silent but resilient cultural anchor that distinguishes the Windisch speakers from their Germanic and Italian neighbors.

slovene_the_dukes_chair_tradition.d: The ancient ritual of installing the Dukes of Carinthia in the Slovenian language symbolizes a unique contractual relationship between the ruler and the ruled. This custom reinforces the idea of a free peasantry with specific legal rights, preventing the total disenfranchisement of the rural population. This social contract fosters a stable and productive agricultural base across our domains.

slovene_the_tabor_defense_system.d: As a border nation, we have always been in a dangerous position against our enemies, so our people have developed the Tabor — fortified church enclosures where villagers can retreat with their livestock and valuables. This decentralized defense system turns every village into a minor fortress, forcing any invader into a grueling war of attrition they cannot win.

slovene_the_catechismus_and_abecedarium.d: The soul of our people has found its voice through the printing presses. Primož Trubar has published the Catechismus and Abecedarium, the first books ever printed in the Slovenian language. This is far more than a religious act; it is a political earthquake that standardizes our various dialects into a single literary tongue. By giving the common folk the tools of literacy in their own language, we have forged a unified national consciousness that transcends the borders of old feudal duchies. This intellectual awakening accelerates the adoption of modern administrative institutions and allows the light of new ideas to spread rapidly from the pulpit to the plow.

slovene_the_glory_of_carniola.d: Following the lead of Janez Vajkard Valvasor, we have undertaken a monumental effort to map the geography, history, and customs of our lands. This scientific survey provides the state with an unparalleled understanding of its resources and people, allowing for more efficient taxation and the rapid application of technological innovations.

slovene_the_zois_circle.d: Baron Sigmund Zois, a wealthy mineralogist and patron of the arts, has started organizing a circle of intellectuals who spearheaded the Slovenian National Awakening (Preporod). This group promotes the use of Slovenian in high culture, science, and politics, effectively transforming a 'peasant tongue' into a language of modern statehood.

religious_melting_pot.d: Many different religions have influenced our people, from their traditional folk beliefs to Hinduism and Buddhism, both from India and China. Over time, our people have developed some degree of religious syncretism, mixing some beliefs with others and not fully disregarding any.

akson_thai.d: Originally based on ancient Khmer script, Thai writing has evolved to be quite distinct from its original form to accommodate the complex phonology of our language. Having a unique written language has certainly contributed to the development of our unique culture.

father_governs_children.d: Our rulers are famed for their close connection to the common man. May our people always live free and happily under the guiding light of their majestic, heavenly rulers!

thai_war_elephants.d: War elephants have been used in Indochina for generations, both for cavalry and as personal mounts for the kings, who would then engage in elephant duels with the opposing side's leader.

thai_royal_poets.d: What is the point of winning wars if no songs are sung about our victories? Our court shall be a haven for poets, and our history shall be their source of inspiration.

trading_links.d: Our country has been a crossroads of trade since ancient times. Our proximity to India and China has allowed trade to flow through our lands, and with it relationships and interactions with the many different countries around us.

foreign_mercenaries.d: We have recently received an influx of barbarians from foreign lands. Some are merchants but some are fighting men. Let us make use of them in our armies.

toi_muay.d: Taught to our soldiers for use in combat, it is an unarmed martial art featuring punches, grappling, and ground-fighting techniques. Proficiency in this art allows our troops to remain deadly in battle even if they lose their weapons.

trading_embassies.d: The numerous trade ships coming in and out of our waters have familiarized us with many distant realms. By establishing permanent trading embassies with these far-off places, we can transform casual commerce into formal relationships.

photduang.d: Our currency may feel strange to outsiders, but Photduang have served us well for centuries. Roundish balls of silver and stamped with official marks, they serve as the basis of our economy.

personal_executions.d: From now on, the most heinous criminals will be executed personally by the ruler. With this, people will know that we are an orderly nation committed to justice, and they will show the appropriate obedience to the law.

close_subjects.d: For us, our subjects are not something separate from the nation, but rather an integral part of it. We keep close ties with them, and they are fully integrated into our bureaucracy and administration.

birthplace_of_renaissance.d: Our dedication to fine arts, cultivating artistic talent, and innovative thought have led us to be regarded as one of the foremost leaders of cultural, philosophical, and scientific advancements around the world.

a_land_of_banks.d: Tuscany is the center of banking in Europe, with many powerful financial institutions headquartered in its major cities. From these bases, their influence extends across Italy and into northern Europe through extensive trade networks and lucrative partnerships.

tuscan_merchant_houses.d: Across the great trading cities of the continent, the name of our merchants is known wherever bills of exchange are signed and goods are weighed. From the wool markets of England to the spice routes of the Levant, our trading houses extend our reach far beyond our borders, wielding an influence that no army could match. This web of commerce and credit ensures our voice is heard in the courts of distant kings.

tuscan_the_mezzadria.d: Across the fertile hills and valleys of our lands, the ancient partnership between landowner and sharecropper ensures that fields are worked with care and harvests shared in good faith. The Mezzadria is more than an agricultural arrangement — it is a social covenant that sustains both the peasantry and the merchant class who depend on the contado's output. This bond between city and countryside is the foundation upon which our prosperity rests.

tuscan_literary_academies.d: Our cities have given rise to learned societies dedicated to the purification of language, the pursuit of knowledge, and the cultivation of civic virtue. From the philological investigations of our literary scholars to the natural philosophy of our scientists, these academies gather the finest minds of the age and sharpen the wit of our administrators. This tradition of organized inquiry is already raising the quality of our governance and the ambition of our institutions.

tuscan_enlightenment.d: The rational spirit of the Enlightenment has taken deep root in our cities, where thinkers and reformers challenge superstition, codify the law, and redesign our institutions from the ground up. Our rulers, schooled in the new philosophy, regard the welfare of their subjects as both a moral duty and a measure of good government. This commitment to reason and reform is transforming our streets, our courts, and our academies into models for the modern world.

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

ven_venetian_palaces.d: The cities of the Veneto built their wealth and order on the Comùn (Comune in standard Italian: the Commune) — a covenant between burghers and nobility to share the obligations of governance rather than leave them to a single lord. From Padua to Verona and the mountain towns beyond, this tradition of elected councils, written statutes, and civic courts gave our urban life a stability and confidence that purely feudal regions could not match. This communal heritage makes our institutions resilient and our burghers invested in the success of the city they help govern.

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

ven_state_inquisition.d: Before Florence claimed the Renaissance as its own, the scholars of the Veneto were already recovering the texts of antiquity and asking what it means to live as a citizen rather than a subject. Francesco Petrarca spent his final years among us, and the libraries and courts of the region drew men of letters who saw no contradiction between classical learning and Christian faith. This tradition of Umanesimo shapes how our governors think — not only as administrators but as men formed by history and argument, elevating the quality of every negotiation we conduct.

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

ven_venetian_painting.d: The painters of our cities have developed a style unlike any other in Italy — abandoning the hard outlines of the Florentine tradition for the warm luminosity of color and the soft blending of light that only the Pittura Veneziana commands. Giovanni Bellini, Giorgione, and Tiziano Vecelli have made our workshops the envy of every patron in Christendom, and foreign lords send commissions across the Alps because no other school can match the richness of our pigments or the confidence of our compositions. This tradition of painting gives our culture a reputation for sensory refinement that travels further than our armies, drawing patrons, wealth, and admiration from courts that we could never reach by force.

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

ven_mixed_naval_tactics.d: Andrea Palladio drew on the proportions of ancient Rome and the building materials of the Veneto to create a style that is simultaneously learned and practical, at home in a villa on the Brenta as in a civic loggia on a market square. His principles spread from Vicenza across every Terraferma city, giving our public buildings a dignity grounded in mathematics rather than fashion. This Oordine Palladiano not only beautifies our cities but makes them legible — a visitor entering our towns reads confidence, prosperity, and permanence in every facade.

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

ven_ship_mounted_gunpowder_weapons.d: The aristocracy of the Veneto has made the Terraferma its summer country, building villas that are at once working farms, places of retreat, and stages for the cultural life that cannot be conducted on a canal. Along the Brenta and through the hills of Vicenza and Treviso, these estates host salons, concerts, and philosophical conversations that rival anything the academies of the cities can offer. This culture of the Vìla (Villa in standard Italian: country estate) draws talent from across the region and keeps our governing class connected to the land they administer, giving them a practical knowledge that purely urban oligarchies tend to lose.

c.t: Has government reform: Partitio Terrarum Imperii Romaniae

ven_venetian_thalassocracy.d: In the weeks before Lent, the cities of our culture put on the Bauta and briefly become equals — a merchant in a mask walks beside a senator and cannot be distinguished, and the rules that govern dress, movement, and address are suspended by universal consent. This tradition of supervised disorder has served us for centuries as a pressure valve, and it has drawn visitors from across Europe who spend freely while marveling at the spectacle. This annual carnival sustains our reputation for a kind of governed liberty that no other culture in Europe can quite replicate.

dai_vietnamese_architecture.d: Though influenced by the Chinese, our architecture remains distinct and unique to our state. While still following the concepts of Fēng Shuǐ, many typical Chinese elements have been left out or adapted to our unique environment.

dai_hung_dao_trans_military_feats.d: Trần Hưng Đạo was an Imperial Prince of Đại Việt long ago. He served as officer during the first Mongol invasion of Đại Việt in 1258, and as leading commander during the second war against the Mongols in 1285 and their third attempt in 1287. During these bloody conflicts, Trần Hưng Đạo managed to develop tactics which reliably repelled the oncoming onslaught of cavalry.

dai_nha_nhac.d: The Nhã Nhạc is the traditional music played at our courts and performed at annual ceremonies. It is a prominent aspect of our culture, and a pillar of our traditions.

dai_confucian_administration.d: Our state bureaucracy is obviously of the utmost importance, and as such, we select only the most capable administrators to hold government office. Learned in the Confucian texts of China, these bureaucrats ensure smooth and stable bureaucratic operations.

dai_giao_chi_arquebus.d: The Giao Chỉ Arquebus is a staple of our military. Self-produced and adapted to the specific needs of our troops, this type of arquebus gains praise from not only Chinese people, but also Western observers.

dai_ca_tru.d: The Ca Trù is a Vietnamese genre of musical storytelling which serves both entertainment and religious purposes.

dai_trade_advance.d: Our existence has been shaped by China for too long. To leave our own mark on the world, we must expand our reach beyond the Chinese sphere of influence.

dai_literary_reform.d: For centuries, we used Classical Chinese to write our documents. However, the script used to write our language is Chữ Nôm, a native script based on Chữ Hán, the script of Classical Chinese. Chữ Nôm was non-standardized and not used often enough compared to Classical Chinese, so there has been some pressure to reform the script and make it more suitable for our administrative purposes.

dai_don_dien.d: The Đôn Điên is a system which utilizes military colonies, in which soldiers and landless peasants clear the area for the establishment of new villages. These villages are then incorporated into our administrative system after three years, and the people who cleared the land may then claim and work it.

dai_thuan_thien.d: Thuận Thiên, or Heaven's Will, is the name of the legendary sword wielded by our liberator, Lê Lợi. According to the tales, the sword gave him the strength of a thousand men, enough to finally throw off the yoke of Chinese rule. Many in our country look upon Lê Lợi as the perfect embodiment of the ideal leader.

vivaro_alpine_drailles.d: The ancient seasonal routes that shepherds use to move their flocks between highland summer pastures and lowland winter grazing — the drailles — are among the most carefully maintained paths in the region, crossing passes and valleys in patterns refined over centuries. The communities along them have developed systems of collective grazing rights, waypoint shelters, and dispute arbitration that turn transhumance from a seasonal risk into a reliable cycle of production. This managed seasonality of the pastoral economy gives our highlands a food-producing capacity that purely sedentary agriculture cannot match.

vivaro_alpine_infantry.d: The mountain terrain has bred a tradition of light, mobile foot soldiers who could fight in conditions that make cavalry and heavy armor useless — men who need no road, no level ground, and no supply line longer than their own backs can carry. The valleys of our culture produce soldiers accustomed to cold, altitude, and sudden ambush, capable of holding narrow passes against forces many times their number. This tradition of alpine warfare gives our armies a quality in difficult terrain that opponents trained on the open lowland battlefield are consistently unprepared for.

vivaro_alpine_passes.d: Mont Cenis, the Col de Montgenèvre, the Col de Larche — the great transalpine routes connecting the Mediterranean world to northern Europe all pass through our territory, making even modest lords the indispensable gatekeepers of international movement. Merchants, armies, papal legates, and pilgrims all pay to cross our ground, and the traffic that passes through our hands gives us information, contacts, and leverage that purely inland powers could never accumulate. This position as the crossroads of transalpine exchange makes our diplomacy unusually well-informed and our merchants unusually well-connected.

vivaro_alpine_herbes_des_alpes.d: The alpine flora of our region provides us with an extraordinary pharmacopoeia — gentian, arnica, valerian, and dozens of others — and the communities here have developed traditions of herbal preparation and botanical knowledge that keep these isolated valley populations healthier than their lowland counterparts. This is the result not of folk magic but systematic observation, transmitted from generation to generation in the form of practical recipes and the accumulated memory of what had worked and what had not. These Herbes des Alpes give our healers tools that the physicians of great cities, dependent on imported remedies, cannot easily replicate.

vivaro_alpine_valley_councils.d: The isolation of our mountain communities has forced them to develop functional self-governance long before larger states thought to organize them — village councils managing collective pastures, local courts arbitrating disputes, and elected officers coordinating the resources that kept valley communities alive through the winter. These institutions run on knowledge of local conditions that no governor sent from outside could replicate, and they have accumulated over generations a tradition of deliberation and record-keeping that gives our communities an administrative depth disproportionate to their size. This Conseilh de Valat tradition makes our governance unusually competent and our subjects unusually engaged in the management of their own affairs.

vivaro_alpine_nature.d: Rousseau's idealization of mountain simplicity, followed by the poets and painters of the Romantic movement, transformed the Alps from a barrier to be crossed into a destination to be sought. Our valleys, peaks, and ancient communities became mirrors for everything that educated Europe felt it had lost, drawing visitors, naturalists, and artists in numbers that the passes had never seen for any other reason. This reputation for embodying a kind of unspoiled authenticity gives our culture an influence far beyond what our political weight could command — people come to us to understand themselves, and they carry home memories that outlast any treaty.

griot_advance.d: The griots are storytellers, historians, counselors, musicians, and poets all at once. They safeguard the stories and legends of past generations, mediate between warring parties, and serve both their rulers and local people as advisors.

west_african_caravan_stop_advance.d: The great deserts of our world are no barrier to determined merchants. For centuries, caravans have crossed the burning sands carrying Gold, Salt, and the most precious goods between distant lands. The Caravan Stop, a place of rest, water and shelter, is the cornerstone of this commerce, ensuring that the hardships of the desert do not extinguish the fires of trade.

sudano_sahelian_architecture_advance.d: The grasslands, savannas, and deserts of Western Africa provide few resources suitable for construction projects, so we have made the best of what we can get. The usage of mudbricks and adobe plaster reduces the cost of buildings significantly while also giving them a distinct style that is pleasing to the eye.

unlock_byzantine_cataphracts_2_advance.d: The Late Medieval Cataphracts are mail-clad riders and horses alike, thundering into battle behind long lances and dense shields. Their shock charges and iron discipline are a frightening sight for our foes.

unlock_byzantine_cataphracts_3_advance.d: These Reformed Cataphracts blend old Imperial drills with newer tactics, combining lances with bows and sidearms. They fight as a flexible heavy cavalry corps, able to harass at range and then finish off their foes in close combat.

unlock_byzantine_cataphracts_4_advance.d: The Heavy Cataphracts ride in layered armor that deflects most missiles and blades. Organized into wedges of elite fighters, they break enemy lines with repeated charges that few formations can withstand.

unlock_byzantine_cataphracts_5_advance.d: Chosen from the finest lancers, the Guard Cataphracts serve as the mounted guard of the throne and our capital. Their presence in every battle is both a weapon and a symbol, rallying our troops and terrifying our foes.

unlock_byzantine_cataphracts_6_advance.d: The Imperial Cataphracts are the culmination of centuries of cavalry tradition: armored veterans, superbly mounted and drilled to perfection. They serve as the Emperor's personal guard, able to decide campaigns with a single, well-timed charge.

expansionist_ambitions.d: As the Balkans fractured, many rising powers looked outward. Ambitious rulers pursued integration of diverse lands under a single, stronger crown, taking advantage of Byzantine weakness.

poklisars.d: Since the earliest days of our nation, we have often cast our gaze beyond our borders, be it to establish profitable trade routes, placate formidable neighbors and build alliances, or even to forge robust partnerships against common adversaries. Poklisars are the ambassadors who carry out these missions in our name.

vojvodstvo_advance.d: Among the South Slavs, the Vojvoda serves as a high military commander, leading the nobles into battle and administering frontier lands. The title is preserved through generations of war, carried by princely warlords and resistance leaders alike.

balkan_hajduks.d: As the central authority of medieval kingdoms fractures under the weight of imperial expansion, the social vacuum is filled by the Hajduks. Originally simple cattle drovers (hajtó) and seasonal laborers, these men have transitioned into a semi-mythical class of guerrilla fighters and highwaymen. They operate in small, disciplined bands (cheta) led by a Harambaša, governed by strict internal codes of conduct that emphasize loyalty and the protection of the local peasantry (the raja). In our eyes, they are nothing more than brigands; to the commoners, they are the only shield against the depredations of foreign tax collectors and unruly invaders. By codifying their presence within our military structure, we empower a force that thrives on the very lawlessness of the frontier.

cro_pandurs_recruitment.d: The state must harness the ferocity of the frontier without succumbing to its chaos. The Pandurs — once mere night watchmen and local security — are reorganized by charismatic leaders into a professionalized light infantry. These soldiers are a terrifying sight on the European battlefield, accompanied by their own bands of martial music. They are the masters of skirmishes, specializing in raiding supply lines, screening the main army, and psychological warfare. While their discipline remains erratic and their propensity for plunder high, they provide a ruler with a flexible tool of intimidation that conventional line infantry cannot match.

voievodate_advance.d: Across the Carpathian basin, the Voievod stands as both sovereign ruler in Wallachia and Moldavia and as a high crown office in Transylvania and the Hungarian kingdom. The office binds the ruler to a powerful nobility through ancient custom and elective right.

b: Damage Done versus Heathens in Battle: +10%
cas_the_reconquista.d: The Reconquista is the campaign by which the Christian kingdoms of Hispania shall reclaim Iberia from the successor states of al-'Andalus. Iberian arms carry the heaviest share of this effort, from the joint victory at Las Navas de Tolosa in 1212, to the taking of Córdoba in 1236, Valencia in 1238, and Seville in 1248. This permanent state of holy war has produced a military culture, a chivalric ethos, and a frontier social order that no other European kingdom can match.

tercio.d: Tercio infantry were developed principally by the brilliant general Gonzalo Fernández de Córdoba, called El Gran Capitán, during the Italian Wars. It is a mixed infantry formation of pikemen and musketeers. Because of this combined-arms approach, the formation simultaneously utilizes both the rigidity of its heavy infantry and the long-range firepower of its musketeers, making it an ideal defensive and offensive formation.

catalan_galley.d: The Catalan Galley is a larger version of the ancient Greek galleys that once dominated the Mediterranean Sea.

early_iberian_caravel.d: Originally of Iberian origin, the first caravels were small but very fast ships that were used for offshore fishing and coastal trade. Their use in Iberia is so widespread that the region can easily boast of possessing the most advanced caravels.

iberian_caravel.d: The need for faster and more reliable caravels has driven our shipbuilding experts to make improvements to their design. While caravels have become common across Europe, the Iberian models remain superior in both innovation and speed.

early_iberian_galleon.d: An early, but powerful ocean-going vessel, the Early Iberian Galleon is an original invention from Iberia that has a lower forecastle and a long hull, making them especially stable and resistant to headwinds.

square_rigged_caravel.d: By combining the Iberian Caravel and the Carrack, a new ship has been born: fast, strong, and exactly what we need help us dominate the seas.

iberian_galleon.d: The Iberian Galleon is a more stylized version of the Early Iberian Galleon. They are tremendously powerful vessels that absolutely crush any opposition on the high seas.

spa_naval_reforms.d: The Iberian peninsula's coastline spans three different seas — the Bay of Biscay, the Atlantic approaches, and the western Mediterranean — each with its own maritime tradition built up over centuries by the different Iberian cultures' fleets. We will consolidate the historical patchwork of peninsular naval commands into a unified professional Armada under centralized captain-general authority, standardizing recruitment, signal codes, and provisioning across every shipyard from coast to coast. This regional consolidation gives our Crown the capacity to crew, maintain, and deploy the dual-ocean fleets that the coming centuries of global empire will demand.

lieutenancy_advance.d: As the Crown of Aragon's possessions grow to encompass realms scattered from the Pyrenees to Sicily, the king's physical absence from any one territory becomes a permanent feature of governance. The office of Lloctinent is institutionalized in the fourteenth century, with a senior noble or royal relative deputized to hold court, dispense justice, and command troops in the king's name during his absence. This institution allows a composite monarchy to function as a single political unit across distances that would otherwise fragment it into warring viceroyalties.

spa_viceroyalties.d: The vast Castilian and Portuguese territories conquered after Hernán Cortés took Tenochtitlan and Francisco Pizarro took Cajamarca require a level of royal supervision that no medieval feudal arrangement can supply. We will establish the Virreinatos — first the Viceroyalty of New Spain at Mexico City under Antonio de Mendoza, then the Viceroyalty of Peru at Lima under Blasco Núñez Vela — each headed by a viceroy holding the king's full personal authority over governance, justice, finance, and defense. This viceregal system gives the Iberian crowns a model of distant administration that successfully holds together the largest contiguous empires in human history.

ara_almogavars.d: Almogavars are a class of light infantry soldiers originating from the Crown of Aragon. These quick-moving warriors serve as frontier defenders and foot soldiers. In addition to their role in the Reconquista, they have also found employment as mercenaries in Italy, the Frankokratia, and the Levant.

ara_catalan_crossbowmen.d: Some of the fiercest and deadliest crossbowmen in the Western Mediterranean, the Catalan Crossbowmen compete against the Genoese Crossbowmen for supremacy in this field.

ara_late_almogavars.d: The Almogavars, embracing new innovations, have undergone remarkable adaptations to enhance their efficiency on the battlefield. Integrating cutting-edge weaponry and strategic advancements into their traditional tactics, these formidable warriors have become even more formidable. With a blend of ancient expertise and modern tools, they stand as a prime example of the seamless fusion between tradition and innovation in warfare.

cas_lanzas_de_castilla.d: Inspired by the Moorish jinete, the Lanzas de Castilla ride lighter than a knightly lance but fight heavier than a skirmisher, closing to break a formation where a true light horseman would only harass and withdraw.

por_cacadores.d: Nicknamed the Fighting Cocks, the Caçadores are an elite light infantry unit in the Portuguese Army who wear brown uniforms to distinguish them from regular soldiers.

italy_great_families.d: After the foundation of our unified Italian state, we have absorbed many great noble families into our country. We should utilize their prestige and reputation to improve our own, while keeping those capable people busy.

italian_condottieri.d: Our nation is renowned for producing great military minds, whether they serve their own interests or are sworn in loyalty to the state. We should ensure that these adept intellects are willing to serve us first and foremost.

city_of_scholars.d: Our Maghrebi madrasas (the Qarawiyyīn of Fez, the Zaytūna of Tunis, the Tashfīniyya of Tlemcen) have drawn students and teachers from every quarter of the Maghreb since the thirteenth century. Our jurists train in the Mālikī fiqh under masters whose chains of transmission run to Córdoba, and our astronomers, physicians, and grammarians correspond with peers from Cairo to Fez. This sustained intellectual infrastructure gives our courts the standing as intellectual capitals of the central and western Maghreb.

slave_raid_advance.d: Our Maghrebi ports license the ra'īs, corsair captains who sail under our flag to cruise the western Mediterranean and the Atlantic approaches, taking Christian shipping for prize-money and Christian crews for our slave markets. We will arm light xebec and galley squadrons in our harbours, channel a share of every haul into the Crown's treasury, and let the Trinitarian and Mercedarian friars ransom back the captives our captains hold. This corsair economy funds our state through prize and ransom revenues on a scale that no regular taxation of our coastal provinces could ever match.

mor_marabouts.d: The marabouts, Sufi shayḵs of the Qādiriyya, Shādhiliyya, and Tijāniyya ṭarīqas, have planted zāwiya lodges across the rural Maghreb, where they teach, arbitrate disputes, and channel popular religious feeling. Their tombs become pilgrimage sites, their living successors hold moral authority that rivals the jurists of the cities, and their endorsement of a ruler legitimizes that ruler with the tribal countryside. This rural network of Sufi authority gives every maghreb_region_ADJ state a religious infrastructure that reaches into every village without requiring direct administrative penetration.

trans_saharan_trade.d: The northern termini of the trans-Saharan caravan routes (Sijilmasa, Ouargla, Tlemcen, Ghadāmis, and Tripoli) sit on our soil, gathering the Bambuk and Buré gold dust, Slaves, and ivory of the Sudan into our markets. Our jallāba merchants finance the desert crossing, our mints strike golden dinārs from the inbound gold under royal monopoly, and our re-export trade redistributes Sudanese goods to Mediterranean and Atlantic buyers. This commanding position over the northern half of the Saharan economy gives every Maghrebi state both a trade-route revenue and a minting prestige that no purely Mediterranean kingdom can match.

slave_soldiers.d: The Hafsid sultans of Tunis or the Zayyanid emirs of Tlemcen have built up corps of ghulām and mamlūk-style retainers since the fourteenth century, purchased from Black African markets, taken in raids on Christian Iberia, or born into the institution as the children of earlier slave-soldiers. These troops swear personal loyalty to the ruler rather than to tribe or region, making them the reliable counterweight to the unstable Banū Hilāl levies that no Maghrebi sultan can fully trust in succession disputes. This institutionalized military slavery gives our state a politically reliable infantry and cavalry that no purely tribal army can match.

hispano_moresque_style.d: Andalusian craftsmen fleeing the Christian frontier have settled in our Maghrebi cities for two centuries, bringing their tilework, woodcarving, and stuccowork into our mosques, madrasas, and palaces. The Almoravid pulpits of our great mosques, the lacework arches of our royal courts, and the funerary cupolas of our shrines all bear the unmistakable Hispano-Moresque signature. This influx of Andalusian artistry gives the Maghrebi courts an aesthetic that rivals Granada itself and sets the standard for the Maghreb's high culture.

tuareg_veiled_cavalry.d: The Tuareg Veiled Cavalry are the indigo-veiled camel-and-horse riders of the deep Sahara, grown out of the a_tuareg_camelry into a heavier arm that can hold ground as well as raid. They carry the straight takouba broadsword and the long allagh lance, taking payment from the caravans they escort and plunder from those they do not.

rais_of_the_navy.d: Our corsair captains, the Ra'īs, are more than just pirates: they are seasoned naval commanders, and their experience at sea feeds a deep well of maritime tradition that strengthens our navy's proud heritage. Our admiralties train every promising young captain under a veteran Ra'īs's command, perpetuating a body of practical seamanship that no formal naval academy could replicate. This concentration of professional captaincy gives the Maghrebi states a naval officer corps that no inland treasury could finance through formal training alone.

andalusi_arquebusiers.d: The Andalusi Arquebusiers are firearm infantry trained by the Andalusi exiles who filled the Maghrebi cities after the fall of Granada, keeping the gunpowder craft of the Nasrid emirate's last decades. They fought as shock troops at the Battle of the Three Kings.

maghrebi_galiots.d: The Maghrebi Galiot is the swift small-galley of the Maghrebi corsair shipyards. Built on Mediterranean galiot lines but shallower and lighter-gunned, it trades firepower for speed and oar-power, slipping into coves that heavier Christian war-galleys cannot reach. Our captains raid Christian merchant shipping and screen our own traders.

maghrebi_xebec.d: The Maghrebi Xebec is the fast lateen-rigged warship of the Barbary corsair states, blending a galley's maneuverability with the windward sailing of the lateen rig, gunned enough to threaten a convoy yet shallow enough to slip into coves no war-galleon can follow. Our shipyards at Algiers, Tunis, Salé, and Tripoli build them by the fleet.

subsaharan_musketeer_corps.d: The Sub-Saharan Musketeers are the black musketeers of the Saadian armies, men brought north across the desert as captives and put to the matchlock in the garrison towns of Merrakš and Fas. The sultans prize a musket line with no clan behind it and no stake in a succession quarrel.

conquistador_advance.d: The discovery of the New World attracts adventurers of all stripes to risk their fortunes and lives on uncertain expeditions, with the promise of unparalleled wealth, fame, and power. These expeditions are formalized through agreements between expedition leaders and the government, legally manifested as 'capitulations of conquest'.
